2. Aluminum Melting and Separation Physics

2.1 The Aluminum Window — Thermodynamic Basis

The "Aluminum Window" is the 60°C interval between 660°C and 720°C where:

  • Aluminum is liquid (MP 660.3°C for pure Al; alloys liquidus 577-652°C)
  • Magnesium is liquid but not vaporizing (MP 650°C, BP 1091°C, significant vapor >720°C)
  • Copper is solid (MP 1084.6°C) — 365°C margin
  • Iron is solid (MP 1538°C) — 878°C margin
  • All Stage 4 metals (Pb, Sn, Zn, In, Bi) REMOVED — drum cleared below 450°C

This window exists because of the unique melting point hierarchy of common metals in electronics scrap. No engineering adjustment can widen it — it is a thermodynamic constant.

MetalMelting Point (°C)Boiling Point (°C)State in Window ------------ Mg6501091Liquid (co-melts with Al) Al (pure)660.32470LIQUID Al alloys (A380)566-577577-590Liquid (eutectic) Al alloys (6061)582652Liquid Al alloys (7075)477635Liquid Cu1084.62562Solid Fe15382861Solid Ni14552913Solid Cr19072671Solid Ti16683287Solid

2.2 Aluminum Melt Properties at 680°C

PropertyValueSignificance --------- Density (liquid)2.38 g/cm³Lightest structural metal — inner annulus Viscosity1.3 mPa·sExtremely fluid — flows like water Surface Tension0.86 N/mHigh — resists droplet formation, forms film Thermal Conductivity90 W/m·KRapid heat distribution in melt pool Electrical Resistivity4.5×10⁻⁸ Ω·mGood induction coupling at 10 kHz Skin Depth (10 kHz)δ ≈ 0.9 mmExcellent for 1-5 mm Al particles Latent Heat of Fusion397 kJ/kgSignificant energy at phase change Specific Heat (liquid)1.18 kJ/kg·KSensible heat in 60°C window: 71 kJ/kg Thermal Expansion (liquid)1.3×10⁻⁴ /KVolume change affects film thickness Vapor Pressure (720°C)<10⁻⁶ PaNegligible Al loss — unlike Mg Oxidation Rate (680°C, 1 ppm O₂)0.1 µm/minForms protective Al₂O₃ skin

2.3 Centrifugal Film Formation and Drainage

At 300 RPM (ω = 31.4 rad/s, r = 0.3 m), the molten aluminum forms a continuous annular film at the drum wall:

Film Thickness (Nusselt falling film analogy, centrifugal): $$\delta = \left( \frac{3 \mu Q}{2\pi \rho \omega^2 r} \right)^{1/3}$$

For Q = 5 kg/min Al flow, μ = 1.3 mPa·s, ρ = 2380 kg/m³: δ ≈ 0.8 mm — thin, stable film

Drainage Velocity: $$v = \frac{\rho \omega^2 r \delta^2}{3\mu} \approx 0.15 \text{ m/s}$$

Time to traverse 800 mm drum length: ~5 seconds — drainage is rapid

Centrifugal Pressure at Port 5: $$\Delta P = \frac{1}{2} \rho \omega^2 (r_{wall}^2 - r_{port}^2) = \frac{1}{2} \times 2380 \times 31.4^2 \times (0.3^2 - 0.05^2) = 33 \text{ kPa}$$ Sufficient to overcome 1.5 bar N₂ backpressure (150 kPa) with 5× margin when combined with static head.

2.4 Melt Pool Dynamics and Wave Stability

The rotating molten aluminum film is subject to hydrodynamic instabilities:

Kelvin-Helmholtz Instability (gas-liquid interface): $$\omega_{KH}^2 = \frac{(\rho_g U_g - \rho_l U_l)^2 k^2}{(\rho_g + \rho_l)^2} - \frac{(\rho_l - \rho_g)gk + \sigma k^3}{\rho_g + \rho_l}$$ At 680°C, ρ_l = 2380 kg/m³, ρ_g = 1.2 kg/m³ (N₂ at 1.5 bar), U_g ≈ 0, U_l = v = 0.15 m/s, σ = 0.86 N/m. For film thickness δ = 0.8 mm, dominant wavelength λ ≈ 2πδ = 5 mm. Growth rate: ω_KH ≈ 50 s⁻¹ — waves form but are stabilized by rotation

Rayleigh-Taylor Instability (centrifugal acceleration): $$\omega_{RT}^2 = \frac{(\rho_l - \rho_g) \omega^2 r k - \sigma k^3}{\rho_l + \rho_g}$$ Centrifugal acceleration stabilizes the interface (heavy liquid outward). The 25 G field suppresses RT instability completely.

Result: Stable, uniform annular film with small-amplitude ripple waves (1-2 mm) that enhance heat transfer without causing droplet entrainment.

2.5 Heat Transfer in the Melt Pool

Induction Heating Power Density: $$P_v = \frac{\pi^2 B_{peak}^2 d^2 f^2}{6 \rho_{Al} D}$$ At 10 kHz, B_peak = 0.3 T, d = 3 mm (particle size), ρ_Al = 4.5×10⁻⁸ Ω·m, D = 0.3 m (drum): P_v ≈ 1.2 MW/m³ — volumetric heating within Al particles

Thermal Diffusion Time (Al particle, 3 mm): $$\tau_{th} = \frac{d^2}{4\alpha} = \frac{(0.003)^2}{4 \times 7.6 \times 10^{-5}} \approx 0.03 \text{ s}$$ Al particles heat uniformly — no thermal gradients.

Melt Pool Temperature Uniformity: With 384 FBG sensors (48 per zone × 8 zones), axial temperature variation <±2°C achieved through:

  • Induction zone power modulation (Zones 4-5 independently controlled)
  • Drum rotation distributing heat circumferentially
  • High Al thermal conductivity (90 W/m·K) spreading heat axially

3. Magnesium Removal Strategy

3.1 The Mg Challenge

Magnesium is the primary impurity in aluminum scrap that degrades castability and mechanical properties. In Stage 5 feedstock:

  • 6061/6063 extrusions: 0.8-1.2% Mg
  • 7075 aerospace: 2.1-2.9% Mg
  • A356 cast: 0.3-0.45% Mg
  • 5xxx sheet: 2.5-5.5% Mg
  • Overall feedstock Mg: 0.3-1.5%

Problem: Mg co-melts with Al (MP 650°C). At 680°C, Mg is fully dissolved in Al melt. Standard Al refining removes Mg by: 1. Chlorine flux sparging — forms MgCl₂ gas (toxic, environmental hazard) 2. Vacuum distillation — energy intensive, slow 3. Solid flux reaction — NaCl/KCl + cryolite forms MgO/Al₂O₃ dross

Aegis-Forge Solution: In-drum NaCl/KCl/cryolite flux with selective Mg oxidation — no chlorine, no vacuum, continuous with centrifugal separation.

3.2 Flux Chemistry — NaCl/KCl/Cryolite System

Flux Composition:

  • NaCl: 47.5 wt% (melting point 801°C, eutectic with KCl at 657°C)
  • KCl: 47.5 wt% (lowers melting point, improves fluidity)
  • Na₃AlF₆ (Cryolite): 5 wt% (dissolves Al₂O₃, adjusts flux basicity)
  • Eutectic melting point: 657°C — fully liquid at Stage 5 temperatures

Mg Removal Reactions: 

Primary:  2Mg (in Al) + CO₂ (from flux decomposition) → 2MgO (dross) + C
Alternative: 3Mg + Al₂O₃ (drum liner wear) → 3MgO + 2Al
With cryolite: Mg + Na₃AlF₆ → MgF₂ (in flux) + 3NaF + Al

Flux Basicity Control:

  • NaCl/KCl is neutral (basicity = 1.0)
  • Cryolite adds AlF₃ which reacts with MgO: MgO + AlF₃ → MgF₂ + Al₂O₃
  • Target flux basicity: 0.8-1.0 (slightly acidic) — maximizes MgO solubility in flux, minimizes Al loss

Flux Injection Protocol: TimingFlux RateTotal per BatchNotes ------------ Ramp 660→680°C0.5 kg/min5 kgInitial flux blanket Dwell 680°C (25 min)0.2 kg/min5 kgContinuous Mg scavenging Ramp 720°C0.3 kg/min2 kgFinal dross conditioning TOTAL—12 kg~10% of Al mass

3.3 Mg Removal Kinetics

The Mg removal rate is controlled by mass transfer from bulk Al melt to flux interface:

Mass Transfer Coefficient (k_m): $$k_m = \frac{D_{Mg}}{\delta_{BL}} \approx \frac{5 \times 10^{-9} \text{ m}^2/\text{s}}{0.5 \text{ mm}} = 1 \times 10^{-5} \text{ m/s}$$ Where D_Mg = Mg diffusivity in liquid Al at 680°C, δ_BL = boundary layer thickness.

Removal Rate: $$\frac{d[Mg]}{dt} = -k_m \cdot A \cdot \frac{[Mg]_{bulk} - [Mg]_{eq}}{V}$$ With A/V = 3/δ (film geometry) = 3750 m⁻¹, [Mg]_eq ≈ 0 (MgO precipitation): At [Mg]_0 = 1.0 wt% = 41 mol/m³: d[Mg]/dt = -0.015 wt%/min Time to reach 0.1 wt%: ~60 minutes — but centrifugal renewal of surface reduces this to 25 min dwell.

Centrifugal Surface Renewal: Film drainage exposes fresh metal to flux interface continuously. Surface renewal frequency: f = v/δ = 0.15/0.0008 = 187 Hz Effective removal rate enhanced 100× vs static melt — 25 min dwell sufficient.

3.4 Cryolite Role and Fluoride Chemistry

Cryolite (Na₃AlF₆) serves three critical functions:

1. Al₂O₃ Solubility: Dissolves protective Al₂O₃ skin on melt surface (solubility ~3 wt% at 680°C), exposing fresh Al to flux 2. Mg Fluoride Formation: Mg + Na₃AlF₆ → MgF₂ + 3NaF + Al (ΔG = -45 kJ/mol at 680°C) — irreversible Mg capture 3. Flux Fluidity: Lowers viscosity from 2.5 mPa·s (NaCl/KCl) to 1.8 mPa·s — improves mixing

Fluoride Balance:

  • Cryolite input: 0.6 kg/batch (5% of 12 kg)
  • MgF₂ formed: 0.4 kg/batch (from 0.15 kg Mg removed)
  • NaF generated: 0.3 kg/batch — remains in flux, recycled
  • Net fluoride consumption: negligible — closed loop in flux recycle

3.5 Mg Removal Efficiency

ParameterTargetMeasurement --------- Mg in feed Al0.3-1.5%ICP-OES on feed sample Mg in Al product<0.1% (1000 ppm)ICP-OES on slug sample Mg removal efficiency>93%Mass balance: Mg in dross / Mg in feed Al loss to dross<5% of feed AlAl in dross / Al in feed Dross generation rate8-12% of Al massWeighed dross / Al produced

Mg Partitioning:

  • 85-90% of Mg → MgO in dross (flux reaction)
  • 5-10% of Mg → MgF₂ in flux (cryolite reaction)
  • <1% of Mg → remains in Al product
  • Al loss mechanism: Mechanical entrapment in dross (not chemical)

3.6 Alternative Mg Removal Methods (Evaluated and Rejected)

MethodPrincipleRejection Reason --------- Cl₂/Ar spargingMg + Cl₂ → MgCl₂(g)Toxic gas, environmental permit, corrosion SF₆ cover gasMg + SF₆ → MgF₂ + SO₂Potent GHG (GWP 23,500), banned in EU Vacuum distillationMg vaporization at 720°C, 10⁻³ mbarEnergy intensive, slow, separate equipment Electrolytic (3-layer)Mg²⁺ migration to cathodeCapital cost, not compatible with batch process NaCl/KCl/Cryolite (SELECTED)Mg oxidation + fluoride captureNo toxic gas, in-drum, continuous, proven

4. Aluminum Alloy Fractionation

4.1 Fractionation Strategy

The Stage 5 output is a mixed aluminum alloy slug (85-97% Al, 1-8% Si, 0.5-3% Cu, 0.3-1.5% Mg). Downstream refining (PROD-112, FOLLOW-20) separates this into two primary product streams:

Product StreamTarget CompositionSource AlloysApplication ------------ Wrought Al (Remelt)Al >99.7%, Si <0.15%, Fe <0.2%, Mg <0.1%, Cu <0.05%1xxx, 3xxx, 5xxx, 6061 (low Cu), clean 6063Extrusion billet, rolling slab, wire rod Cast Al (Secondary)Al 88-92%, Si 5-12%, Cu 1-3%, Mg 0.3-0.5%A380, A356, 319, 7075 (high Si/Cu)Die-casting, sand casting, tooling

Fractionation Method: Sequential Port 5 Collection by Temperature Ramp

  • 660-680°C: Early melt = lowest liquidus alloys (A380, A356, 5xxx) — higher Si/Mg
  • 680-700°C: Mid-range = 6061, 6063, 3xxx — moderate Mg/Si
  • 700-720°C: Late melt = pure Al, 1xxx, clean 6063 — highest purity
  • Each 5-minute temperature band collected to separate ZrO₂ mold position

4.2 Wrought vs Cast Separation Logic

CriterionWrought StreamCast Stream --------- Si content<0.15%5-12% Fe content<0.20%0.2-0.8% Cu content<0.05%0.5-3% Mg content<0.10%0.3-0.5% Primary sourceExtrusions, wire, foil, sheetDie-cast, engine parts, housings DownstreamHomogenize → DC cast → extrudeDirect remelt → die-cast/sand cast Value$2.50-3.00/kg$1.80-2.20/kg

Separation Control:

  • Inline XRF at Port 5 exit — real-time Si, Fe, Cu, Mg
  • Temperature band assignment logged per mold position
  • Post-batch assay of each slug confirms fractionation

4.3 Thermodynamic Basis for Fractionation

The sequential melting of Al alloys follows their liquidus temperatures:

AlloyLiquidus (°C)Collection WindowMold Position ------------ A380 (Si 8.5%, Cu 3.5%)577660-670°C (early)1-2 A356 (Si 7%, Mg 0.35%)613665-675°C2 5xxx (Mg 3-5%)630-650670-680°C2-3 6061 (Mg 1%, Si 0.6%)652675-685°C3 6063 (Mg 0.7%, Si 0.4%)655680-690°C3-4 1xxx (pure Al)660685-700°C4 3xxx (Mn 1%)655-660690-705°C4-5 7075 (Zn 5.6%, Mg 2.5%, Cu 1.6%)635670-680°C (but Zn removed)—

Note: 7075 and other Zn-containing alloys have Zn removed in Stage 4, so their liquidus shifts. The remaining Al-Cu-Mg system melts in the 670-690°C range.

4.4 Fractionation by Impurity Segregation

During solidification in ZrO₂ molds, impurity segregation further purifies the wrought stream:

Scheil Equation (non-equilibrium solidification): $$C_s = k C_0 (1 - f_s)^{k-1}$$ Where C_s = solid composition, C_0 = initial composition, f_s = fraction solidified, k = partition coefficient.

ImpurityPartition Coefficient (k)Segregation Behavior --------- Si0.12Strongly rejected to liquid — last 10% of solid has 8× bulk Si Fe0.03Extremely rejected — forms FeAl₃ in interdendritic regions Cu0.17Rejected — enriches in last-to-freeze zones Mg0.35Moderately rejected Mn0.45Mildly rejected

Practical Application: Wrought slugs (Positions 4-5) are cast with directional solidification (bottom chill plate at -150°C N₂ quench). The first 80% of solidification produces Al with <0.05% Si, <0.1% Fe, <0.02% Cu. The last 20% (high-impurity zone) is cropped and recycled to cast stream.

4.5 Real-Time Fractionation Control Algorithm

FOR each 5-min temperature band in [660-665, 665-670, 670-675, 675-680, 
                                     680-685, 685-690, 690-695, 695-700, 
                                     700-705, 705-710, 710-715, 715-720]:
    1. READ XRF (Si, Fe, Cu, Mg, Mn)
    2. CALCULATE predicted final composition after solidification
       (using Scheil model with measured cooling rate)
    3. ASSIGN mold position:

           Position = NEXT_WROUGHT_POSITION
       ELSE:
           Position = NEXT_CAST_POSITION
    4. LOG assignment (timestamp, temperature, XRF, prediction)
    5. DIVERT Port 5 flow to assigned ZrO₂ mold (rotary carousel)
ENDFOR


WROUGHT_POSITIONS = [1, 2, 3, 4]   # 4 molds for wrought
CAST_POSITIONS = [5, 6, 7, 8]      # 4 molds for cast

5. Dross Management

5.1 Dross Formation Mechanism

Dross forms at the melt surface by: 1. Al oxidation: 4Al + 3O₂ → 2Al₂O₃ (even in N₂, trace O₂ exists) 2. Mg oxidation: 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO (primary dross component with flux) 3. Nitride formation: 2Al + N₂ → 2AlN (at 680°C in N₂ atmosphere) 4. Flux entrapment: NaCl/KCl/cryolite mechanically trapped in oxide layer

Dross Composition (Typical):

  • Al₂O₃: 40-50%
  • MgO: 20-30% (from Mg removal)
  • NaCl/KCl: 15-20% (entrapped flux)
  • AlN: 5-10%
  • Metallic Al (entrapped): 10-20% of dross mass

Dross Formation Rate Model: $$\frac{dm_{dross}}{dt} = k_{ox} A_{surface} p_{O_2}^{1/2} + k_{nit} A_{surface} p_{N_2} + \dot{m}_{flux\_entrain}$$ Where:

  • k_ox = 2.5×10⁻⁶ kg/m²·s·Pa^0.5 (Al oxidation rate constant at 680°C)
  • k_nit = 1.2×10⁻⁷ kg/m²·s·Pa (AlN formation rate at 680°C)
  • A_surface = 2πrL = 1.5 m² (drum inner surface area)
  • p_O₂ = 1 Pa (1 ppm in 1.5 bar N₂)
  • p_N₂ = 1.5×10⁵ Pa
  • m_flux_entrain = 0.1 kg/min (empirical)

Calculated: dm_dross/dt ≈ 0.4 kg/min → 12 kg over 30 min — matches observed 8-15 kg/batch.

5.2 Salt Flux Dross Recovery

Recovery Process (Downstream of Stage 5): 1. Hot dross (680°C) discharged with Al stream — skimmed at Port 5 2. Rotary furnace re-melt: Dross + 5% NaCl/KCl flux, 750°C, 30 min 3. Stirring: Recovers entrapped Al (90% recovery of metallic Al in dross) 4. Skim: Clean Al returned to cast stream; salt slag to Stage 7

Recovery Metrics: MetricTarget ------ Al recovery from dross>90% Salt flux recycle rate>80% (recovered flux reused) Final salt slag to Stage 7<2% of Al feed mass Energy for dross re-melt15 kWh/ton dross

Rotary Furnace Design (FOLLOW-20 Detail):

  • Capacity: 500 kg dross/batch
  • Rotation: 15 RPM (gentle — prevents Al oxidation)
  • Atmosphere: N₂ + 5% H₂ (reducing — prevents further oxidation)
  • Flux: NaCl/KCl (same as Stage 5 — recycle loop)
  • Tilt: 5° for slag discharge
  • Al recovery: 92% typical (1.8 kg recovered from 2 kg entrapped)

5.3 Dross to Stage 7

The salt slag (NaCl/KCl/MgO/Al₂O₃/AlN) exits the Aegis-Forge I with the Stage 7 ferrous stream. It is processed in the Phoenix Protocol hydrometallurgical refinery:

  • Water leach: NaCl/KCl dissolved, recovered by evaporation
  • MgO/Al₂O₃/AlN residue: Acid leach for REE recovery (Stage 8 minerals)
  • Zero waste — all flux components recycled or valorized

5.4 Dross Thermodynamics and Phase Diagram

The NaCl-KCl-MgO-Al₂O₃ system at 680°C:

Phase Relations:

  • NaCl-KCl: Complete liquid miscibility (eutectic 657°C)
  • MgO: Solubility in NaCl/KCl = 0.5 wt% at 680°C
  • Al₂O₃: Solubility in NaCl/KCl = 0.1 wt%; in cryolite = 10 wt%
  • MgO-Al₂O₃: Forms spinel MgAl₂O₄ (melting point 2135°C) — stable solid

Dross Cooling Path: 1. 680°C: Liquid flux + suspended MgO/Al₂O₃/AlN + entrapped Al 2. 657°C: NaCl/KCl eutectic solidification begins 3. 600°C: Flux fully solid — MgO/Al₂O₃/AlN trapped in salt matrix 4. 25°C: Final dross — crystalline NaCl, KCl, MgAl₂O₄, AlN, metallic Al

This solidification behavior enables mechanical separation of salt from oxides in the rotary furnace (salt melts at 657°C, oxides remain solid).

Resonance Tracking (Induction):

  • Frequency sweep ±3% around 10 kHz every 15 sec
  • Phase-locked loop maintains ZVS
  • Load change detection: Al melt increases coupling → frequency shift tracked

11.3 Metal Level Sensors (POF)

Plastic Optical Fiber (POF) Level Detection at Port 5:

  • PMMA fiber (1 mm core) at r = 280 mm, 3 axial positions (200, 400, 600 mm)
  • Light transmission attenuated by molten Al film (n_Al ≈ 1.2 vs n_air = 1.0)
  • Resolution: 0.3 mm film thickness
  • Response time: <50 ms
  • Used for: Continuous flow verification, mold fill level, overfill protection

11.4 Composition Feedback Control (XRF)

Inline XRF at Port 5 Exit:

  • Si-PIN detector, 50 kV Rh anode, 10 sec acquisition
  • Measures: Si, Fe, Cu, Mg, Mn, Zn, Ti, Pb, Sn
  • Real-time fractionation decision: XRF Si content → mold position assignment
  • Si < 0.5% → Position 1 (Wrought)
  • Si 0.5-3% → Position 2 (Mixed wrought/cast)
  • Si 3-8% → Position 3 (Cast A356)
  • Si > 8% → Position 4-5 (Cast A380/high-Si)

11.5 Flux Injection Control

  • Pneumatic powder injection (N₂ carrier) at drum top flux port
  • Mass flow controller per component (NaCl/KCl blend, cryolite separate)
  • Injection synchronized with temperature profile
  • Feedback:
  • XRF Mg in Al stream → adjust cryolite rate (Mg removal efficiency)
  • Dross alkalinity (pH of quench water) → adjust NaCl/KCl ratio
  • Flux consumption rate → inventory management

11.6 Mold Carousel Control

8-Position ZrO₂ Mold Carousel (PROD-08 Integration):

  • Rotation: Indexed by Port 5 discharge events (XRF trigger)
  • Position 1-4: Wrought molds (water-cooled Cu chill plates)
  • Position 5-8: Cast molds (insulated for slower cooling)
  • Cooling: N₂ quench at -150°C for wrought; ambient air for cast
  • Cycle time: 5 min per position (matches temperature band dwell)
  • Synchronization: Carousel index triggered by XRF band decision + Port 5 flow confirmation

11.7 Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA)

HMI Screens: 1. Thermal Overview: Real-time FBG map (8 zones × 48 sensors), temperature profile tracking 2. Composition Monitor: XRF trends (Si, Fe, Cu, Mg), fractionation assignment log 3. Flux Management: Hopper levels, injection rates, recycle loop status 4. Dross/Skim: Skim frequency, dross mass, Al recovery rate 5. Energy Dashboard: Induction power, heat recovery, exergy efficiency 6. Safety Status: Interlock states, emission monitors, vibration spectra

Alarm Hierarchy:

  • Level 1 (Critical): Temp >725°C, O₂ >2%, Port 5 fail, Vibration >5 mm/s — Auto shutdown
  • Level 2 (Major): Temp ramp >10°C/min, RPM ±10%, Pressure >1.8 bar — Auto hold + alarm
  • Level 3 (Minor): XRF drift, Flux level low, Emission >50% limit — Alarm only
  • Level 4 (Info): Band transition, Mold index, Batch complete — Log only

Data Historian:

  • 1 Hz logging for all FBG, XRF, POF, induction, rotation, pressure
  • 10-year retention (compressed)
  • OPC-UA interface for enterprise integration

A.3 Emergency Shutdown Sequence

A.4 Key Equations

  • Centrifugal G: G = ω²r/g = (2π·RPM/60)²·0.3/9.81
  • Skin depth: δ = √(2ρ/ωμ) (ρ=resistivity, μ=permeability)
  • Film thickness: δ = (3μQ/2πρω²r)^(1/3)
  • Drainage velocity: v = ρω²rδ²/3μ
  • Mg oxidation: 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO (ΔG < 0 at 680°C)
  • Exergy efficiency: η_ex = Ex_products / Ex_inputs

B.2 Thermal Cycling Performance

Wrought Mold (3Y-TZP + Cu chill):

  • Thermal shock ΔT: 680°C → -150°C = 830°C in <10 s
  • 3Y-TZP thermal shock resistance: ΔT_critical = 650°C (conservative)
  • Design margin: Cu chill absorbs 80% of heat flux, ZrO₂ sees ΔT ≈ 160°C — safe
  • Mold life: 500 cycles (inspected per PROD-08 schedule)

Cast Mold (3Y-TZP insulated):

  • Thermal shock ΔT: 680°C → 25°C = 655°C in 60 s
  • Well within 3Y-TZP capability
  • Mold life: 2000 cycles

B.3 Solidification Control

Wrought (Directional Solidification):

  • Bottom chill: Copper plate at -150°C (liquid N₂ circulated)
  • Heat extraction: 500 kW/m² → solidification front velocity 2 mm/s
  • Columnar grain zone: 80% of height
  • Equiaxed zone: 20% (top) — cropped

Cast (Equiaxed Solidification):

  • Insulated walls: 5 mm ceramic fiber blanket
  • Heat extraction: 50 kW/m² → solidification time 15 min
  • Uniform equiaxed grains: 200-500 µm (target for cast alloys)
  • No cropping needed — entire slug usable

B.4 Mold Change Procedure

1. Carousel rotates to unload position (outside drum envelope) 2. Robotic arm extracts solidified slug (cooled to 200°C) 3. Mold cleaned by N₂ blast (removes oxide skin) 4. Mold pre-heated to 200/300°C (induction heater on carousel) 5. Carousel indexes to Port 5 position 6. Cycle time: 3 minutes — fits within 5-min temperature band

PHYSICAL SEPARATION PRINCIPLE:
• The "Copper Window": 1085°C (pure Cu MP) to 1200°C (Fe remains solid, Ni MP 1455°C)
• At 1085°C: Cu melts, Fe (1538°C), Ni (1455°C), Co (1495°C), Cr (1907°C) remain solid
• Centrifugal force (250 RPM, G=17.4) drives molten Cu film to drum wall
• Port 6 (1180°C setpoint) drains continuous Cu stream to anode molds
• Precious metals (Au, Ag, Pd, Pt) DISSOLVE in Cu melt — partition to anode slime
• H₂/N₂ reducing atmosphere prevents Cu₂O; controls As/Sb/Bi volatilization
• Anode casting: 4× ZrO₂ molds (50 kg each) on carousel — continuous cast/cool cycle
• NO flux added — Cu self-fluxing; CaO only if needed for slag basicity control

2.2 Induction Heating Physics — Zone 6 (5 kHz)

Skin Depth Calculation: 

δ = √(2ρₑ / ωμ) = √(2 × 1.15×10⁻⁷ / (2π × 5000 × 4π×10⁻⁷)) = 4.2 mm
  • At 1150°C, Cu resistivity increases ~3× → skin depth ~7.3 mm
  • Drum wall thickness (ZrB₂-SiC): 25 mm → adequate penetration to center
  • 5 kHz selected for balance: deep enough for bulk heating, high enough for power density

Power Coupling Efficiency: 

P = (π² B² f² d² σ) / (8 ρₑ) × V_eff
Where B = magnetic flux density, f = frequency, d = characteristic dimension, σ = conductivity
  • Target: 250 kW into ~80 kg Cu charge
  • Heating rate: 250,000 W / (80,000 g × 0.42 J/g·K) = 7.4 K/s theoretical
  • Practical: 2-3 K/s with losses → 6-10 min to 1150°C from 720°C

Resonant Tank Design (from PROD-10):

  • GS66516T GaN HEMT half-bridge Class E
  • Switched capacitor bank + varactor for 4.5-5.5 kHz tuning
  • ZVS maintained across full power range
  • Efficiency: 98.7% at 200 kW (PROD-10 Table 2.4)

2.3 Centrifugal Separation — Copper Film Dynamics

Film Thickness and Drainage Velocity: 

h_film = (3μQ / ρg_eff)^(1/3)  [Nusselt film condensation model adapted]
g_eff = ω²r = (250 × 2π/60)² × 0.3 = 206 m/s² = 21.0 G
  • At 250 RPM, r=300mm: g_eff = 206 m/s²
  • Cu film thickness on drum wall: ~1.2 mm
  • Drainage velocity: v = (ρg_eff h²) / (3μ) = 0.28 m/s
  • Transit time to Port 6 (280 mm radius): t = 0.28/0.28 = 1 second
  • Rapid drainage prevents PM segregation during transit

Centrifugal Density Stratification Operator: 

C[ρ, ω, r, t] = r_eq = √(r₀² + (2μ/ρω²) ln(ρ_liquid/ρ_particle))
For solid particles in molten Cu:
  • Fe particles (ρ=7.87): r_eq = 285 mm (slightly inward of Cu film)
  • Ni particles (ρ=8.90): r_eq = 298 mm (near Cu film)
  • Mineral particles (ρ=3-4): r_eq < 200 mm (well inward, remain in drum)
  • PM atoms in Cu melt: no separation (dissolved); PM oxides/particles: r_eq = 290-300 mm

3. Precious Metal Partitioning to Anode Slime

3.1 Partitioning Thermodynamics

Precious Metal Behavior in Molten Copper: ElementMelting PointBoiling PointSolubility in Cu (1150°C)Partition Coefficient K = C_slime/C_Cu --------------- Gold (Au)1064°C2856°CComplete (fcc, same structure)>10⁴ (strong slime affinity) Silver (Ag)962°C2162°CComplete (fcc, same structure)>10³ Palladium (Pd)1555°C2963°C8.5 wt% at 1150°C10²-10³ Platinum (Pt)1768°C3825°C0.5 wt% at 1150°C10² Rhodium (Rh)1964°C3695°C0.1 wt% at 1150°C10-50 Iridium (Ir)2410°C4428°C<0.01 wt%10-50 Ruthenium (Ru)2334°C4150°C<0.01 wt%10-50 Osmium (Os)3033°C5012°C<0.001 wt%10-50

Partition Mechanism: 1. Dissolution: PMs dissolve in molten Cu during 30 min dwell (diffusion time τ = L²/D; D_Au_in_Cu ≈ 10⁻⁸ cm²/s at 1150°C → τ ≈ 10 s for 100 μm particle) 2. Solidification Segregation: During anode casting, Cu solidifies dendritically; PMs partition to interdendritic liquid (K < 1) 3. Slime Formation: Final interdendritic liquid enriched in PMs, O, S, Se, Te → forms anode slime at mold interface 4. Collection: Slime mechanically separated during anode demold/handling

3.3 Anode Slime Collection System

Slime Formation Location:

  • Forms at Cu/ZrO₂ mold interface during solidification
  • Interdendritic liquid (final 5-10% of solidification) enriched in PMs
  • Collected by:
1. Mechanical skimming during anode demold (slime layer on top) 2. Mold wash with N₂ jet after demold (recovers residual slime) 3. Anode surface brushing before electrolytic cell loading

Slime Handling Protocol: 1. Each anode mold has dedicated slime catch tray (ZrO₂, 500 cm²) 2. Slime falls into tray during demold → conveyed to sealed container 3. Container purged with N₂, weighed, sampled (LIBS), sealed 4. Transferred to FOLLOW-19 electrorefining queue 5. Chain of custody: Slime container UUID linked to anode UUIDs

4.1 Zone Architecture — 4-Zone Design for Stage 6

4.2 Zone 6-1: Charge and Preheat

Feed Introduction:

  • Feed from Stage 5 enters via Port 5→6 transfer chute (ZrO₂ lined, 5° decline)
  • Feed rate controlled by vibratory feeder (KNbO₃-BaTiO₃ ultrasonic, 10 kg/min)
  • Real-time mass flow: FBG force sensors on feed chute
  • Feed composition verification: Inline LIBS at feed entry (PROD-08 LIBS head)

Preheat Profile: 

T(t) = 720 + (1085-720) × (1 - exp(-t/τ)), τ = 300 s
  • Target: 1085°C at t=15 min
  • Power: 100 kW ramp to 150 kW
  • Atmosphere: 5% H₂/95% N₂ established before feed entry

4.3 Zone 6-2: Melt and Dwell — The PM Dissolution Reactor

Process Parameters:

  • Temperature: 1150°C ±5°C (superheat 65°C above MP)
  • Duration: 30 minutes
  • RPM: 250 (G=17.4)
  • Atmosphere: 5% H₂/95% N₂ at 1.2 bar

PM Dissolution Kinetics: 

dm_PM/dt = k_diss × A_PM × (C_sat - C_bulk)
k_diss = 2D/δ_diff  (mass transfer coefficient)
D_Au_in_Cu = 1.2×10⁻⁸ m²/s at 1150°C
δ_diff = √(D×t) = 0.0015 m at t=1800 s
  • 100 μm PM particle dissolves in ~30 seconds
  • All PMs fully dissolved within first 5 minutes of dwell
  • Remaining 25 minutes: homogenization, gas equilibration, anode prep

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Anode Specifications (per PROD-08):

  • Mold cavity: 100 × 50 × 40 mm = 200 cm³ × 4 inserts = 200 cm³ effective
  • Anode mass: 50 kg (Cu ρ=8.96 g/cm³ → 5,580 cm³ total)
  • Anode dimensions: 100 × 500 × 112 mm (fits standard electrolytic cell)
  • Surface: Cast finish (no machining required for electrorefining)
  • Stamp format: BATCH-YYYYMMDD-NNN-6-1150-SSSS (PROD-08 Section 4.1)

Solidification Control (Chvorinov): 

t_solid = B × (V/A)²
B (ZrO₂ mold, Cu) = 1.8 min/cm²
V = 5,580 cm³, A = 2×(100×500 + 100×112 + 500×112) = 1,544 cm²
V/A = 3.6 cm
t_solid = 1.8 × 3.6² = 23 min theoretical
  • Practical: 6 min with N₂ quench (PROD-08 Table 3.3)
  • Microstructure: Columnar-to-equiaxed transition (CET) at center
  • CET position controlled by N₂ flow rate — target 60% columnar for anode strength

4.5 Zone 6-4: Transition to Stage 7

Residual Clearance:

  • After anode casting complete (4 anodes = ~200 kg Cu), residual Cu < 2 kg
  • Power taper: 250 → 100 → 50 → 0 kW over 5 min
  • Temperature: 1150 → 1200°C (Stage 7 entry)
  • Atmosphere: 5% H₂/95% N₂ maintained (Stage 7 uses same)

Slag Conditioning:

  • Mineral residue (Fe, Ni, Co, CaO, SiO₂, REE oxides) heated to 1200°C
  • CaO addition (if needed) for basicity: B = CaO/SiO₂ = 1.2 target
  • NO flux added for Cu — Cu self-fluxing; CaO only for slag

Stage 7 Handoff:

  • Drum contains: Fe 80 kg, Ni/Co 10 kg, Minerals 60 kg, Cu residue <2 kg
  • Stage 7 induction (Zone 7, 2 kHz) takes over heating
  • Port 6/6A sealed at 1200°C (Ti₃AlC₂/ZrO₂ valves)

5. Oxidation Control and Atmosphere Management

5.1 Reducing Atmosphere Chemistry

Target Atmosphere: 5% H₂ / 95% N₂ at 1.2 bar, dew point <-40°C

Equilibrium Reactions: 

2Cu + ½O₂ ⇌ Cu₂O          ΔG° = -146 kJ/mol at 1150°C
H₂ + ½O₂ ⇌ H₂O            ΔG° = -198 kJ/mol at 1150°C
Cu₂O + H₂ ⇌ 2Cu + H₂O     K = p_H₂O/p_H₂ = 10⁻⁹ at 1150°C

Required H₂ Partial Pressure for Cu₂O Prevention: 

p_H₂ / p_H₂O > 10⁹
With p_H₂O < 10⁻⁴ bar (dew point <-40°C): p_H₂ > 10⁻⁵ bar (trivially met at 5%)

Atmosphere Control System:

  • N₂ supply: GFGS Train A (PROD-07), 99.999% purity
  • H₂ supply: On-site electrolyzer (CsMFAB000000000105) or bottled
  • Mixing: PEEK CF40 mass flow controllers (±1% accuracy)
  • Dew point: Molecular sieve dryer (3Å) on N₂ line, continuous monitor
  • Pressure: 1.2 bar maintained by back-pressure regulator (ZrO₂ diaphragm)
  • H₂ monitor: Catalytic bead sensor (SIL-2) + IR backup — trip at 4% LEL

5.2 Impurity Volatilization Control

Volatile Impurities in Cu Feed (from PCBs, solders):

ImpuritySourceVolatility at 1150°CReactionCapture --------------- Arsenic (As)PCB solder, leadframeHIGHAs + 3H → AsH₃ (g)Train B chemisorbent (Cu-impregnated carbon) Antimony (Sb)Flame retardants, solderHIGHSb + 3H → SbH₃ (g)Train B chemisorbent Bismuth (Bi)Lead-free solderMODERATEBi + 3H → BiH₃ (g)Train B chemisorbent Lead (Pb)Solder residueLOWPb + H₂ → PbH₂ (unstable)Condenses in off-gas cooler Sulfur (S)PCB laminateHIGHS + 2H → H₂S (g)Train A lime scrubber Chlorine (Cl)PVC residueHIGHCl + H → HCl (g)Train A lime scrubber

Off-Gas Management (to PROD-07):

  • Off-gas flow: ~50 SLPM (N₂ sweep + H₂ + volatiles)
  • Temperature: 1150°C → cooled to 200°C in ZrO₂ heat exchanger
  • Train A: Lime (Ca(OH)₂) scrubber — HCl, H₂S, SO₂ capture → CaCl₂, CaSO₄
  • Train B: Cu-impregnated activated carbon — AsH₃, SbH₃, BiH₃ chemisorption
  • Train C: Plasma torch (PROD-07) — residual organics, CO destruction
  • Train D: HEPA + carbon — particulate, Hg, residual volatiles
  • Train E: PSA CO₂ capture — CO₂ recycle to drum purge

Emission Limits (per PROD-07):

  • As: <0.1 mg/Nm³
  • Sb: <0.5 mg/Nm³
  • Bi: <1 mg/Nm³
  • Pb: <1 mg/Nm³
  • SO₂: <50 mg/Nm³
  • HCl: <10 mg/Nm³
  • Dioxins/furans: <0.1 ng TEQ/Nm³

12. Control System

12.1 Control Architecture — Stage 6 Specific

Cascade PID Structure (from PROD-10, extended for Stage 6): 

STAGE 6 CONTROL HIERARCHY
══════════════════════════



SUPERVISORY (1 Hz)
├── Batch State Machine: CHARGE → PREHEAT → MELT → DWELL → ANODE_CAST → TRANSITION
├── Recipe Management: Temp profile, RPM, gas, power per stage
├── Quality Gate: LIBS/XRF pass/fail before next state
└── Phoenix Registry: Slug UUID, grade, downstream route



ZONE 6 PID (1 kHz) — PROD-10 Zone 6
├── Master: Drum wall temp (FBG median, 48 sensors) → Power setpoint
├── Slave 1: Resonance tracking (GaN inverter) → Frequency/phase
├── Slave 2: POF level (melt height) → Feed rate / drain rate
├── Slave 3: Gas analyzer (H₂, dew point) → MFC setpoints
├── Slave 4: XRF composition (Cu, Ag, Au) → Dwell time adjust
└── Slave 5: Anode mold FBG (6 per mold) → N₂ quench flow



ANODE CAROUSEL CONTROL (10 Hz)
├── Position: Ultrasonic motor encoder ±0.05°
├── Fill: Mold FBG temp → Port 6A valve (open at 1180°C ±2°C)
├── Cool: N₂ flow → mold FBG cooling rate → 50°C/min target
├── Demold: Ejector sequence (extend 2s, dwell 0.5s, retract 2s)
├── Stamp: Piezo actuation, vision verify, Data Matrix etch
├── LIBS: Trigger at demold, grade assign, registry write
└── Transfer: Conveyor advance, handoff packet to Machine 113



SAFETY INTERLOCKS (Hardwired, <10 ms)
├── H₂ >4% LEL → Emergency N₂ purge, power cut
├── Temp >1210°C → Power cut, N₂ flood
├── Pressure >1.5 bar → Vent, power cut
├── Vibration >5 G → Power cut (drum bearing failure)
├── FBG comm loss >100 ms → Power cut
└── Carousel position error >1° → E-stop

12.2 Key Control Algorithms

Anode Casting Fill Control: 

IF mold_FBG_temp > 1178°C AND mold_FBG_temp < 1182°C:
    OPEN Port_6A_valve
    SET fill_rate = 50 kg / (mold_FBG_thermal_mass × target_cooling_rate)
    MONITOR mold_FBG[1..6] for uniform fill
    WHEN mold_FBG[4] (top sensor) > 1150°C:  # Cu solidus at top
        CLOSE Port_6A_valve
        START N₂_quench_profile

PM Dissolution Verification: 

PM_dissolved = XRF_Ag + XRF_Au + XRF_Pd
IF PM_dissolved < 0.95 × feed_PM_estimate AT t=5 min:
    EXTEND dwell by 5 min
    INCREASE RPM to 280 (temporary, for mixing)
    ALERT operator

Slime Yield Prediction: 

slime_kg = 0.25 × anode_kg × (1 + 0.5 × (O_ppm/1000) + 0.3 × (S_ppm/100))
PREDICT slime mass per anode → compare to actual at demold
IF deviation > 20%: FLAG for investigation

PHYSICAL SEPARATION PRINCIPLE:
• The "Ferrous Window": 1200°C (cast iron MP) to 1600°C (Cr MP, minerals solid)
• At 1200°C: Cast iron melts, carbon steel (1370-1400°C), stainless (1400-1430°C) solid
• At 1538°C: Pure Fe melts, Ni (1455°C), Co (1495°C) already liquid
• At 1600°C: Cr (1907°C) remains solid → Stage 8; minerals (ZrO₂, REE oxides, Al₂O₃) solid
• Ferromagnetic coupling (2 kHz, below Curie 770°C) → 2-10× power density vs non-ferrous
• Centrifugal force (200 RPM, G=13.9) drives molten Fe film to drum wall
• Port 7 (1550°C setpoint) drains continuous Fe stream
• REE magnets (NdFeB, SmCo) melt and partition: REEs to slag, Fe to bullion
• Slag engineering: CaO addition for basicity B=1.2; MgO/Al₂O₃ from upstream dross
• Carbon control: CO/CO₂ gas injection maintains C=2-4% in Fe bullion

2.2 Induction Heating Physics — Zone 7 (2 kHz)

Ferromagnetic Coupling Advantage: Below Curie temperature (770°C for Fe), ferromagnetic materials concentrate magnetic flux, increasing effective permeability μᵣ from 1 to 100-1000. This gives 2-10× power density vs non-ferrous metals at same frequency.

Skin Depth Calculation: 

δ = √(2ρₑ / ωμ) = √(2 × 1.2×10⁻⁷ / (2π × 2000 × 4π×10⁻⁷)) = 8.5 mm
  • At 1580°C, Fe resistivity increases ~3× → skin depth ~14.7 mm
  • Drum wall thickness (ZrB₂-SiC): 25 mm → adequate penetration
  • 2 kHz selected for: deep penetration, ferromagnetic coupling below 770°C, eddy current above

Power Coupling Efficiency (Ferromagnetic Phase): 

P = (π² B² f² d² σ μᵣ) / (8 ρₑ) × V_eff
  • Below 770°C: μᵣ ≈ 200 → 5× power density boost
  • Above 770°C: μᵣ = 1 → eddy current only
  • Target: 400 kW into ~120 kg Fe charge
  • Heating rate (ferromagnetic): 400,000 × 5 / (120,000 g × 0.82 J/g·K) = 20 K/s theoretical
  • Heating rate (non-magnetic): 4 K/s theoretical
  • Practical: 5-8 K/s average → 8-12 min to 1580°C from 1200°C

Resonant Tank Design (from PROD-10):

  • GS66516T GaN HEMT half-bridge Class E
  • Switched capacitor bank + varactor for 1.8-2.2 kHz tuning
  • ZVS maintained across full power range
  • Efficiency: 98.8% at 350 kW (PROD-10 Table 2.4)

2.3 Carbon, Silicon, Manganese Control

Target Fe Bullion Composition: ElementTarget RangeControl Method --------- Carbon (C)2.0-4.0%CO/CO₂ gas injection ratio; decarburization by FeO in slag Silicon (Si)1.0-2.0%SiO₂ reduction by C in melt; slag basicity control Manganese (Mn)0.5-1.0%MnO reduction by C; partitions to slag at high basicity Phosphorus (P)<0.05%Oxidizes to P₂O₅ → slag at high basicity Sulfur (S)<0.03%Forms FeS → slag at high basicity; CaO addition

Carbon Control via Gas Injection: 

C (in Fe) + CO₂ (gas) ⇌ 2CO (gas)        ΔG° = +172 kJ/mol at 1580°C
C (in Fe) + FeO (slag) ⇌ CO (gas) + Fe   ΔG° = -15 kJ/mol at 1580°C
  • CO/CO₂ ratio controls carbon activity: a_C = K × p_CO²/p_CO₂
  • Target p_CO/p_CO₂ ≈ 10 for C=3% at 1580°C
  • Gas injection system: PEEK CF40 lance through Port 7 vicinity
  • CO supply: From pyrolysis gas (PROD-07 Train A) + supplemental
  • CO₂ supply: From PROD-07 PSA capture

Silicon Control via Slag Basicity: 

2FeO (slag) + Si (in Fe) ⇌ 2Fe + SiO₂ (slag)   Distribution ratio L_Si = (%SiO₂)/[%Si]²
  • L_Si increases with basicity B = CaO/SiO₂
  • Target B = 1.2 → L_Si ≈ 50 → [%Si] = √(%SiO₂/50)
  • With %SiO₂ = 35% in slag → [%Si] ≈ 0.8% (within 1-2% target with adjustment)

Manganese Control: 

MnO (slag) + C (in Fe) ⇌ Mn (in Fe) + CO (gas)
  • Mn partitions to slag at high oxygen potential
  • FeO reduction by C lowers oxygen potential → Mn stays in metal
  • Target: 0.5-1.0% Mn (beneficial for cast iron strength)

2.4 Centrifugal Separation — Iron Film Dynamics

Film Thickness and Drainage Velocity: 

g_eff = ω²r = (200 × 2π/60)² × 0.3 = 132 m/s² = 13.5 G
h_film = (3μQ / ρg_eff)^(1/3)
  • At 200 RPM, r=300mm: g_eff = 132 m/s²
  • Fe film thickness on drum wall: ~1.5 mm
  • Drainage velocity: v = (ρg_eff h²) / (3μ) = 0.18 m/s
  • Transit time to Port 7 (280 mm radius): t = 0.28/0.18 = 1.6 seconds

Centrifugal Density Stratification — REE Partitioning: 

C[ρ, ω, r, t] = r_eq = √(r₀² + (2μ/ρω²) ln(ρ_liquid/ρ_particle))
For particles in molten Fe:
  • Fe₃C particles (ρ=7.66): r_eq = 282 mm (near Fe film)
  • REE oxide particles (ρ=7.5): r_eq = 280 mm (co-mingle with Fe)
  • Slag liquid (ρ=2.8): r_eq = 195 mm (well inward)
  • NdFeB/SmCo droplets (ρ=7.5-8.0): r_eq = 275-285 mm → report with Fe stream

3. Rare Earth Magnet Recovery (NdFeB, SmCo)

3.1 Magnet Melting and REE Partitioning

NdFeB (Neodymium-Iron-Boron) Behavior:

  • Composition: Nd₂Fe₁₄B (~26% Nd, 72% Fe, 1% B, ~1% Dy)
  • Melting Point: 1177°C (eutectic) — fully liquid at Stage 7 entry (1200°C)
  • In molten Fe: Nd dissolves in Fe matrix (solubility ~5% at 1580°C)
  • Boron: Forms Fe₂B, partitions to slag as B₂O₃
  • Dy (heavy REE): Substitutes for Nd, follows Nd behavior

SmCo (Samarium-Cobalt) Behavior:

  • Composition: SmCo₅ or Sm₂Co₁₇ (~25% Sm, 70% Co, 5% Fe)
  • Melting Point: 1490°C — liquid at Stage 7 dwell (1580°C)
  • In molten Fe: Sm dissolves in Fe matrix; Co dissolves completely
  • Partitioning: Sm, Nd, Co report to Fe melt; oxidize to slag at interface

REE Partitioning Thermodynamics: ReactionΔG° at 1580°CEquilibrium ConstantPartitioning ------------ 2Nd + 3FeO ⇌ Nd₂O₃ + 3Fe-180 kJ/molK ≈ 10¹⁵Nd strongly to slag 2Sm + 3FeO ⇌ Sm₂O₃ + 3Fe-165 kJ/molK ≈ 10¹⁴Sm strongly to slag 2Co + 3FeO ⇌ Co₂O₃ + 3Fe-45 kJ/molK ≈ 10³Co partially to slag 2Fe + O₂ ⇌ 2FeO-200 kJ/molK ≈ 10¹⁷FeO stable in slag

Partition Coefficients (L_REE = %REE_in_slag / %REE_in_metal):

  • L_Nd = 100-500 (depends on slag FeO, basicity)
  • L_Sm = 80-400
  • L_Dy = 120-600
  • L_Co = 5-20

3.2 REE Recovery Strategy — Dual-Stream Approach

Stream 1: Fe Bullion (Port 7) — REE in Solid Solution

  • Fe bullion contains 0.1-0.5% Nd, 0.05-0.2% Sm, 0.1-0.3% Co
  • Not recovered at Forge — sent to FOLLOW-15 hydrometallurgy
  • FOLLOW-15: H₂SO₄ pressure leach → solvent extraction (Cyanex 272) → Nd/Sm/Co oxides
  • Recovery target: Nd >90%, Sm >85%, Co >80% from Fe bullion

Stream 2: REE Concentrate (Port 7A) — Slag/Metal Mixture

  • Port 7A at r=250mm, opens at 1500°C (lower than Port 7)
  • Collects REE-rich slag + REE-containing metal droplets
  • Composition: 20-30% Fe, 5-15% Nd₂O₃, 2-8% Sm₂O₃, 1-5% CoO, balance CaO-SiO₂-MgO-Al₂O₃
  • Direct to FOLLOW-15 for higher-grade REE recovery
  • Recovery target: Nd >95%, Sm >90%, Co >85% from this stream

4. Centrifuge Bowl Zones for Fe/REE/Slag Separation

4.1 Zone Architecture — 5-Zone Design for Stage 7

ZoneAxial PositionFunctionTemperatureRPMKey Features ------------------ Z7-1 (Charge/Preheat)600-660 mmCharge feed, preheat to 1200°C1200°C200Feed inlet, FBG, POF level Z7-2 (Cast Iron Melt)660-700 mmCast iron melting (1150-1200°C)1250°C200Early Fe fraction, magnet melting Z7-3 (Main Fe Melt/Dwell)700-750 mmComplete melting, REE dissolution1580°C20040 min dwell, C/Si/Mn control, XRF Z7-4 (Fe Drainage/REE Sep)750-780 mmFe film to Port 7, REE to Port 7A1550°C200Dual ports, slag conditioning Z7-5 (Transition)780-800 mmResidual clearance, Stage 8 prep1600°C200Slag conditioning, atmosphere prep

4.2 Zone 7-3: Main Melt and Dwell — The REE Dissolution Reactor

Process Parameters:

  • Temperature: 1580°C ±10°C
  • Duration: 40 minutes
  • RPM: 200 (G=13.9)
  • Atmosphere: 5% H₂/95% N₂ at 1.2 bar, dew point <-40°C

Carbon/Silicon/Manganese Control Loops: 

C_control: CO/CO₂ injection → p_CO/p_CO₂ → [%C] via XRF feedback (1/min)
Si_control: CaO addition → slag basicity B → L_Si → [%Si] via XRF feedback
Mn_control: FeO in slag (via C_level) → oxygen potential → [%Mn] via XRF

REE Dissolution Kinetics: 

dm_REE/dt = k_diss × A_REE × (C_sat - C_bulk)
k_diss = 2D/δ_diff
D_Nd_in_Fe = 5×10⁻⁹ m²/s at 1580°C
δ_diff = √(D×t) = 0.0011 m at t=2400 s
  • 100 μm REE particle dissolves in ~60 seconds
  • All REEs fully dissolved within first 10 minutes of dwell
  • Remaining 30 minutes: homogenization, slag equilibration, C/Si/Mn tuning

In-Situ Monitoring (Zone 7-3): SensorParameterFrequencyAction on Deviation ------------ FBG (48 sensors)Wall temperature1 kHzPID power adjustment POF Level (2 sensors)Melt height10 HzFeed rate adjustment Inline XRFFe, C, Si, Mn, Nd, Sm, Co1/minC/Si/Mn control, REE tracking Gas Analyzer (MS)H₂, CO, CO₂, H₂O10 HzAtmosphere control, C control Magnetic SensorFe melt level (inductive)100 HzCross-check POF level

4.3 Zone 7-4: Dual-Port Separation

Port 7 (Fe Bullion) — Primary Stream:

  • Aperture: 20 mm at r=280mm
  • Opens at 1550°C (Ti₃AlC₂/ZrO₂ thermal actuator)
  • Continuous Fe stream → ZrO₂ molds (4-position carousel, 50 kg each)
  • N₂ quench: 25 SLPM at 4 bar, target cooling rate 30°C/min

Port 7A (REE Concentrate) — Secondary Stream:

  • Aperture: 15 mm at r=250mm (inward of Port 7)
  • Opens at 1500°C (earlier, captures REE-rich droplets)
  • Intermittent collection → ZrO₂ molds (2-position, 15 kg each)
  • Collects: REE-rich slag droplets + REE-containing metal droplets
  • N₂ quench: 15 SLPM at 3 bar, target cooling rate 20°C/min

Separation Logic: 

Centrifugal equilibrium radius:

    

  • Fe-rich liquid (ρ=7.0): r_eq = 285 mm → Port 7
    • 

  • REE-rich droplets (ρ=7.5-8.0): r_eq = 275-280 mm → Port 7A
    • 

  • Slag liquid (ρ=2.8): r_eq = 195 mm → retained in drum
  • 30 mm radial separation between ports = clean separation
  • Port 7A opens 50°C earlier to capture REE droplets before they mix into main Fe stream

    • 4.4 Zone 7-5: Transition to Stage 8

    Residual Clearance:

    • After Fe bullion casting (4×50 kg = 200 kg) + REE concentrate (2×15 kg = 30 kg)
    • Residual Fe < 5 kg
    • Power taper: 400 → 200 → 100 → 0 kW over 5 min
    • Temperature: 1580 → 1600°C (Stage 8 entry)
    • Atmosphere: 5% H₂/95% N₂ maintained

    Slag Conditioning for Stage 8:

    • Slag composition: CaO 25%, SiO₂ 35%, MgO 12%, Al₂O₃ 8%, REE oxides 2%, FeO 10%, MnO 5%
    • Basicity B = CaO/SiO₂ = 1.2 (target for Stage 8 Zr dissociation)
    • NO additional flux — upstream dross provides MgO/Al₂O₃
    • Stage 8 induction (Zone 8, 1 kHz) takes over heating

    5. Slag Engineering

    5.1 Slag System: CaO-SiO₂-MgO-Al₂O₃-FeO-MnO-REE Oxides

    Target Slag Composition (wt%): ComponentTargetSourceFunction ------------ CaO25%Added (15 kg) + mineral residueBasicity, FeO capacity SiO₂35%Glass fibers, PCB substrateNetwork former MgO12%Stage 4/5 dross (17 kg total)Viscosity, REE capacity Al₂O₃8%Stage 5 dross, anodized AlViscosity, REE capacity FeO10%Fe oxidation, magnet FeREE oxidation driver MnO5%Steel scrap, batteries— REE Oxides2%Magnets, drossProduct value Others (CaF₂, TiO₂, etc.)3%Impurities—

    Slag Properties at 1580°C:

    • Viscosity: 0.5-1.0 Pa·s (target <1.0 for REE diffusion)
    • Liquidus temperature: 1350°C (fully liquid at Stage 7)
    • FeO activity: a_FeO ≈ 0.15 (drives REE oxidation)
    • Basicity: B = CaO/SiO₂ = 1.2
    • MgO/Al₂O₃ ratio: 1.5 (from dross — optimal for REE phosphate/silicate solubility)

    5.2 REE Partitioning to Slag

    Partition Coefficient Definition: 

    L_REE = (%REE_oxide in slag) / [%REE in metal]

    Key Equilibria: 

    2[RE] + 3(FeO) ⇌ (RE₂O₃) + 3[Fe]     log L_REE = (ΔG°/RT) + 3log a_FeO - 3log a_Fe

    Operating Window for High REE Recovery: ParameterTargetEffect on L_REE --------- FeO in slag8-12%Higher FeO → higher L_REE Basicity (CaO/SiO₂)1.1-1.3Optimal for REE phosphate/silicate solubility MgO/Al₂O₃1.0-2.0MgO increases REE capacity; Al₂O₃ decreases Temperature1550-1600°CHigher T → lower L_REE (exothermic oxidation) Oxygen potentialp_O₂ ≈ 10⁻¹² atmControlled by C/FeO equilibrium

    MgO/Al₂O₃ from Upstream Dross — Critical Enabler:

    • Stage 4 dross: 10 kg MgO, 5 kg flux
    • Stage 5 dross: 7 kg MgO/Al₂O₃, 2.5 kg flux
    • Total "free" MgO/Al₂O₃: 17 kg — no purchased flux needed
    • This is a cascade advantage: waste from Stages 4-5 becomes slag former for Stage 7

    7.2 FOLLOW-15 Interface Requirements

    Transfer Protocol: 1. Port 7A molds demold → slime catch → stamp → LIBS → Data Matrix 2. REE concentrate crushed to <5 mm in ZrO₂ jaw crusher (inert atmosphere) 3. Sealed ZrO₂ containers (10 L), N₂ purged, weighed, LIBS spectrum recorded 4. Container UUID linked to batch, Port 7A, Stage 7 temp, Phoenix generation 5. Transfer manifest signed → Machine 113 (Hydro-Refinery) queue

    FOLLOW-15 Process (Hydrometallurgical REE Recovery): 

    REE Concentrate (Port 7A) + Fe Bullion (Port 7, REE-bearing)
    │
    ▼
H₂SO₄ Pressure Leach (150°C, 10 bar, 2h) → REE sulfates in solution
    │
    ▼
Solid/Liquid Separation → Fe residue (to castings) / REE pregnant leach solution
    │
    ▼
Solvent Extraction (Cyanex 272 / D2EHPA):
    ├── Light REE (La, Ce, Pr, Nd) → Nd₂O₃ product
    ├── Middle REE (Sm, Eu, Gd) → Sm₂O₃ product
    ├── Heavy REE (Dy, Ho, Er, Yb) → Dy₂O₃ product
    └── Co → Co(OH)₂ → Co metal
    │
    ▼
Oxalate Precipitation → Calcination (900°C) → REE Oxides (99.9%)

    Recovery Targets (FOLLOW-15 Scope):

    • Nd: >90% from Fe bullion, >95% from REE concentrate
    • Sm: >85% from Fe bullion, >90% from REE concentrate
    • Co: >80% from Fe bullion, >85% from REE concentrate
    • Dy: >80% from both streams

    12. Control System

    12.1 Control Architecture — Stage 7 Specific

    Cascade PID Structure (from PROD-10, extended for Stage 7): 

    STAGE 7 CONTROL HIERARCHY
══════════════════════════
    


    SUPERVISORY (1 Hz)
├── Batch State Machine: CHARGE → PREHEAT → CAST_IRON_MELT → MAIN_MELT → DUAL_PORT_CAST → TRANSITION
├── Recipe Management: Temp profile, RPM, gas, power, C/Si/Mn targets per zone
├── Quality Gate: XRF C/Si/Mn/REE pass/fail before port opening
├── REE Partitioning Monitor: L_REE tracking via XRF slag/metal
└── Phoenix Registry: Slug UUID, grade, downstream route
    


    ZONE 7 PID (1 kHz) — PROD-10 Zone 7
├── Master: Drum wall temp (FBG median, 48 sensors) → Power setpoint
├── Slave 1: Resonance tracking (GaN inverter) → Frequency/phase (ferromagnetic ZVS)
├── Slave 2: POF level (melt height) → Feed rate / drain rate
├── Slave 3: Gas analyzer (H₂, CO, CO₂, dew point) → MFC setpoints
├── Slave 4: XRF composition (C, Si, Mn, Nd, Sm, Co) → C/Si/Mn control loops
├── Slave 5: Magnetic sensor (inductive) → Melt level cross-check
├── Slave 6: Fe bullion mold FBG (6 per mold) → N₂ quench flow
└── Slave 7: REE concentrate mold FBG (6 per mold) → N₂ quench flow
    


    DUAL-PORT CAROUSEL CONTROL (10 Hz)
├── Port 7 (Fe): Valve open at 1550±2°C, fill to 50.0±0.5 kg per mold
├── Port 7A (REE): Valve open at 1500±2°C, fill to 15.0±0.5 kg per mold
├── Cool: N₂ quench profile → mold FBG cooling rate (Fe: 30°C/min, REE: 20°C/min)
├── Demold: Ejector sequence (extend 2s, dwell 0.5s, retract 2s)
├── Stamp: Piezo actuation, vision verify, Data Matrix etch
├── LIBS: Trigger at demold, grade assign, registry write
├── REE Grade: LIBS Nd/Sm/Co → DIRECT_USE (FOLLOW-15) / STOCKPILE
└── Transfer: Conveyor advance, handoff packet to Machine 113
    


    C/Si/Mn CONTROL LOOPS (1 Hz)
├── C_loop: Target [%C] per stream → p_CO/p_CO₂ setpoint → MFC adjust
├── Si_loop: Target [%Si] → CaO feed rate → slag basicity B → L_Si
├── Mn_loop: Target [%Mn] → FeO in slag (via C_level) → oxygen potential
└── REE_loop: Target L_Nd, L_Sm, L_Co → FeO/slag basicity → oxygen potential
    


    SAFETY INTERLOCKS (Hardwired, <10 ms)
├── H₂ >4% LEL → Emergency N₂ purge, power cut
├── CO >500 ppm area → Ventilation max, power cut
├── Temp >1610°C → Power cut, N₂ flood
├── Pressure >1.5 bar → Vent, power cut
├── Vibration >5 G → Power cut (drum bearing failure)
├── FBG comm loss >100 ms → Power cut
├── Carousel position error >1° → E-stop
└── Magnetic sensor loss → Power cut (ferromagnetic coupling lost)

    12.2 Key Control Algorithms

    Carbon Control Algorithm: 

    Target_C = stream_C_target (0.5-4.0% by temperature band)
p_CO/p_CO₂_setpoint = Target_C / (K_equil × a_FeO_slag^0.5)
MEASURED_C = XRF_C_port7
ERROR_C = Target_C - MEASURED_C
IF ERROR_C > 0.2%:
    ADJUST CO/CO₂ MFC ratio by ERROR_C × gain
    LOG adjustment to batch record

    REE Partitioning Verification: 

    L_Nd_measured = (XRF_Nd_slag / 100) / (XRF_Nd_metal / 100)
L_Sm_measured = (XRF_Sm_slag / 100) / (XRF_Sm_metal / 100)
IF L_Nd_measured < 100: INCREASE FeO in slag (reduce C injection), ALERT
IF L_Sm_measured < 80: INCREASE slag basicity (add CaO), ALERT

    Dual-Port Separation Verification: 

    Port_7_Fe_rate = mass_Fe_mold / fill_time
Port_7A_REE_rate = mass_REE_mold / fill_time
IF Port_7A_Fe_content > 30%: Port 7A opening too late → ADVANCE Port 7A trigger to 1490°C
IF Port_7_REE_content > 0.5%: Port 7 opening too early → DELAY Port 7 trigger to 1560°C

    PHYSICAL SEPARATION PRINCIPLE:
• The "Mineral Window": 1600°C (SiO₂ melting) to 2200°C (ZrO₂ sintering, TiO₂ decomposition)
• At 1676°C: ZrSiO₄ → ZrO₂ (solid) + SiO₂ (gas) — KEY DISSOCIATION REACTION
• SiO₂ gas captured at Port 8B condenser → fumed silica product
• ZrO₂ remains solid (MP 2716°C) — concentrated by centrifugal separation
• REE oxides (Nd₂O₃, Sm₂O₃, Y₂O₃) solid — co-concentrate with ZrO₂
• Al₂O₃ (MP 2072°C) partially melts at 2000°C+ — separates by density
• TiO₂ decomposes >2000°C — captured as rutile
• 3Y-TZP synthesis: ZrO₂ + 3 mol% Y₂O₃ → flash sinter 1800°C/5 min → 97% TD, 0.5 μm
• UHTC loop closure: ZrB₂ from Stage 8 → PROD-04 drum material (ZrB₂-SiC)
• Ar/He inert atmosphere prevents: SiO oxidation, ZrN formation, Al₂O₃ reduction
• Centrifugal separation (150 RPM, G=10.4) by oxide density: ZrO₂ (5.68) > Al₂O₃ (3.95) > SiO₂ (2.65)

    Total Feedstock: ~65 kg liquid slag + 5-10 kg solid mineral residue

    Key Feed Characteristic: The Stage 7 slag arrives at 1600°C, fully liquid (liquidus 1350°C at B=1.2), with MgO/Al₂O₃=1.5 from free upstream dross flux. This is the IDEAL feed for zircon dissociation — low viscosity, correct basicity, built-in MgO/Al₂O₃.

    2. Zircon Dissociation at 1676°C

    2.1 Thermodynamics of ZrSiO₄ Dissociation

    Primary Reaction: 

    ZrSiO₄ (s) ⇌ ZrO₂ (s) + SiO₂ (g)      ΔH° = +320 kJ/mol

    Equilibrium Constant: 

    Kp = p_SiO₂ = exp(-ΔG°/RT)
ΔG° = ΔH° - TΔS° = 320,000 - T(85) J/mol

    Dissociation Temperature at p_SiO₂ = 1 atm: 

    T_diss = ΔH°/ΔS° = 320,000/85 = 3765 K = 3492°C

    Dissociation Temperature at p_SiO₂ = 10⁻³ atm (practical): 

    ln(10⁻³) = -ΔG°/RT  →  T = 1676°C (1949 K)

    Operating Window:

    • Target: 1700°C (25°C above dissociation temperature at p_SiO₂ = 10⁻³ atm)
    • p_SiO₂ maintained at 10⁻³ atm by continuous Ar sweep + Port 8B condenser
    • At 1700°C, 30 min dwell: >99% zircon dissociation achieved

    2.2 Dissociation Kinetics

    Rate-Limiting Step: SiO₂ diffusion through ZrO₂ product layer (shrinking core model)

    Kinetic Equation: 

    1 - (1 - X)^(1/3) = k·t
k = k₀·exp(-Ea/RT)
Ea = 420 kJ/mol (ZrO₂ diffusion barrier)
k₀ = 1.2×10⁸ s⁻¹

    At 1700°C (1973 K): 

    k = 1.2×10⁸ × exp(-420,000/(8.314×1973)) = 2.1×10⁻⁴ s⁻¹
t_99% = [1 - (0.01)^(1/3)] / k = 0.54 / 2.1×10⁻⁴ = 2570 s = 43 min

    Practical Dwell: 30 min at 1700°C achieves >95% dissociation (ZrSiO₄ particles <100 μm from AMLS liberation)

    2.3 Zircon Feed Characterization

    ParameterValueSource --------- ZrSiO₄ Content2-5 kg/batchLCD glass (ITO), mineral sand Particle Size (post-AMLS)<100 μmAcoustic liberation >80% ZrO₂ Equivalent1.4-3.5 kg67% ZrO₂ in ZrSiO₄ SiO₂ Gas Yield0.7-1.8 kg33% SiO₂ in ZrSiO₄ ImpuritiesHfO₂ 1-2%, U/Th traceZircon lattice substitution

    Hafnium Management: Hf substitutes for Zr in zircon (1-2%). HfO₂ remains with ZrO₂ product. For nuclear-grade Zr, separate Hf removal required (FOLLOW-32). For 3Y-TZP structural ceramic, Hf <2% is acceptable.

    4. 3Y-TZP Synthesis

    4.1 Flash Sintering Process

    Process Parameters:

    • Temperature: 1800°C (5 min dwell)
    • Pressure: 1.1 bar Ar/He
    • Electric Field: 300 V/cm (DC, applied via ZrO₂ electrodes)
    • Powder Feed: ZrO₂ + 3 mol% Y₂O₃, <0.5 μm (milled in-line)

    Flash Sintering Mechanism: 

    Joule heating: P = σ·E²·V
σ (ZrO₂ at 1800°C) = 10 S/m
E = 300 V/cm = 30,000 V/m
Power density = 10 × 30,000² = 9×10⁹ W/m³
    • Volumetric heating → uniform temperature, no thermal gradients
    • Densification in 5 min vs 2 hr conventional sintering
    • Grain growth suppressed → 0.5 μm final grain size

    • ZrO₂ mold, 10 kg capacity, 100×50×40 mm cavity

    • Cycle time: 8 min/mold, 2-position carousel
    • Stamp: BATCH-YYYYMMDD-NNN-8A-1800-SSSS

    ZrO₂ feed: 3.2 kg
Y₂O₃ addition: 0.17 kg
Total powder: 3.37 kg
Flash sinter yield: 95%
3Y-TZP product: 3.2 kg per batch
Annual (1,200 batches): 3,840 kg 3Y-TZP

    5. Silica Management — Fumed SiO₂ Production

    5.1 SiO₂ Gas Generation and Capture

    SiO₂ Sources: 1. Zircon dissociation: ZrSiO₄ → ZrO₂ + SiO₂(g) — 0.7-1.8 kg/batch 2. Slag SiO₂ volatilization: SiO₂(l) + C(s) → SiO(g) + CO(g) — minor at pO₂ <10⁻¹⁵ 3. Total SiO₂ gas: 1-2 kg/batch

    Condenser Design (Port 8B): 

    SiO₂(g) + ½O₂ → SiO₂(s)  (controlled oxidation at condenser)
    • Water-cooled ZrO₂ condenser, 2 m² surface area
    • Coolant: Water at 20°C, 50 L/min
    • Condenser temperature: 200°C (SiO₂ deposition) → 50°C (collection)
    • Ar/He sweep gas: 20 SLPM carries SiO₂ to condenser

    Fumed Silica Specifications: PropertyTargetStandard --------- Purity (SiO₂)>99.9%ICP-OES Primary Particle Size50 ±10 nmBET/BET Specific Surface Area200 ±20 m²/gBET pH (4% slurry)3.5-4.5ISO 787-9 Loss on Ignition<1.5%1000°C/1hr Fe Content<50 ppmICP-MS Al Content<100 ppmICP-MS

    Applications:

    • Aerogel precursor (FOLLOW-09): Polyimide-silica aerogel, λ=0.010 W/m·K
    • Geopolymer curing (PROD-06): CO₂ stream from PROD-07
    • Commercial sale: Fumed silica market ($8-15/kg)

    Mass Balance — Fumed SiO₂ per Batch: 

    SiO₂ gas captured: 1.5 kg (avg)
Condensation efficiency: 90%
Fumed SiO₂ product: 1.35 kg/batch
Annual (1,200 batches): 1,620 kg fumed SiO₂

    6. Alumina/Titania Separation

    6.1 Al₂O₃ Behavior

    Al₂O₃ in Feed: 5.2 kg (Stage 7 slag) + 2-5 kg (mineral residue) = 7-10 kg/batch

    At 1800-2000°C:

    • Al₂O₃ MP = 2072°C — primarily solid
    • Partial melt at 2000°C+ (eutectics with SiO₂, MgO)
    • Density: 3.95 g/cm³ (solid), 3.0 g/cm³ (liquid)

    Separation Strategy:

    • Centrifugal stratification at 150 RPM (G=10.4)
    • Al₂O₃ particles (ρ=3.95) concentrate at r_eq = 265 mm
    • Separate from ZrO₂ (ρ=5.68, r_eq=285 mm) and SiO₂ (ρ=2.65, r_eq=220 mm)
    • Port 8A (r=250mm): ZrO₂ + REE oxides + Al₂O₃ co-collection
    • Post-separation: Al₂O₃ leached from ZrO₂/REE concentrate (FOLLOW-21)

    α-Al₂O₃ Product (via FOLLOW-21):

    • Target: 99.9% α-Al₂O₃, <0.1 μm
    • Use: MAX Phase Ti₃AlC₂ synthesis (FOLLOW-32), abrasives, substrates

    6.2 TiO₂ Behavior

    TiO₂ in Feed: 0.7 kg (Stage 7 slag) + 1-3 kg (mineral residue) = 2-4 kg/batch

    At >2000°C: 

    2TiO₂ → 2TiO + O₂  (decomposition)
TiO₂ + 2C → TiC + 2CO  (carbothermal)

    Separation Strategy:

    • Rutile (TiO₂) stable to 1800°C — solid particle
    • Density: 4.23 g/cm³ — concentrates at r_eq = 270 mm
    • Port 8A co-collection with ZrO₂/Al₂O₃/REE
    • Post-separation: TiO₂ leached (FOLLOW-21) → Ti₃AlC₂ synthesis (FOLLOW-32)

    7. Centrifuge Bowl Zones for Mineral Separation

    7.1 Zone Architecture — 4-Zone Design for Stage 8

    ZoneAxial PositionFunctionTemperatureRPMKey Features ------------------ Z8-1 (Charge/Preheat)700-740 mmCharge slag, preheat to 1676°C1676°C150Feed inlet, FBG, POF level, pO₂ monitor Z8-2 (Dissociation)740-770 mmZrSiO₄ → ZrO₂ + SiO₂(g)1700°C15030 min dwell, SiO₂ condenser (Port 8B) Z8-3 (3Y-TZP Synthesis)770-785 mmFlash sinter ZrO₂+3Y₂O₃1800°C1505 min flash, electric field, Port 8A molds Z8-4 (Residual/Cool)785-800 mmResidual oxides, cool down1800→1600°C150Al₂O₃/TiO₂/REE separation, Stage 8 complete

    7.2 Zone 8-2: Zircon Dissociation Reactor

    Process Conditions:

    • Temperature: 1700°C ±15°C
    • Duration: 30 minutes
    • RPM: 150 (G=10.4)
    • Atmosphere: Ar/He 95/5, 1.1 bar, pO₂ < 10⁻¹⁵ atm
    • SiO₂ partial pressure: 10⁻³ atm (controlled by condenser sweep)

    Dissociation Monitoring: SensorParameterFrequencyAction ------------ FBG (48)Wall temperature1 kHzPID power MS (SiO₂)p_SiO₂ at condenser10 HzSweep gas adjust PyrometerMelt surface temp100 HzPower adjust XRF (slag)Zr, Si, REE in slag1/minDissociation extent

    Centrifugal Separation During Dissociation:

    • ZrO₂ product (ρ=5.68) → drum wall (r=290-300mm)
    • Slag liquid (ρ=2.8) → inward (r=200-250mm)
    • REE oxides (ρ=5-7) → co-concentrate with ZrO₂
    • No separate port — ZrO₂/REE remain in drum for Zone 8-3

    Flash Sintering Cell (Integrated in Drum):

    Flash Sintering Cycle (5 min): 1. Ramp (0-60s): 1600→1800°C, field 100→300 V/cm 2. Flash (60-120s): Thermal runaway, densification 50→97% TD 3. Hold (120-300s): 1800°C, 300 V/cm, grain stabilization 4. Cool (300-600s): Field off, N₂ quench 10°C/min

    Port 8A Mold Fill:

    • 3Y-TZP powder flows directly from flash cell to mold
    • 2 molds × 10 kg = 20 kg per batch (2 cycles)
    • N₂ quench, stamp, LIBS, Data Matrix per PROD-08

    7.4 Zone 8-4: Residual Separation and Cool Down

    Residual Stream Composition (after ZrO₂/3Y-TZP removal):

    • Al₂O₃: 7-10 kg
    • TiO₂: 2-4 kg
    • REE oxides: 1.3 kg (minus Y₂O₃ used)
    • Cr₂O₃: 0.3 kg
    • MgO: 7.8 kg (unchanged)
    • CaO/SiO₂ slag: 15-20 kg (depleted in SiO₂)
    • FeO/MnO: reduced by carbon
    • Carbon: 1-3 kg

    Separation at 150 RPM:

    • TiO₂ (ρ=4.23) → r_eq = 270 mm
    • Al₂O₃ (ρ=3.95) → r_eq = 265 mm
    • REE oxides (ρ=5-7) → r_eq = 280 mm
    • Slag (ρ=2.8) → r_eq = 200 mm

    Final Outputs:

    • Port 8A (final): Al₂O₃/TiO₂/REE concentrate → FOLLOW-21 hydromet
    • Drum residue: CaO-SiO₂-MgO slag + FeO/MnO → Phoenix Protocol stockpile

    8. UHTC Composite Integration — Drum Material Loop Closure

    8.1 ZrB₂ Synthesis (Carbothermal)

    Reaction: 

    ZrO₂ + B₂O₃ + 5C → ZrB₂ + 5CO    ΔH° = +850 kJ/mol at 1800°C

    Process (FOLLOW-32 scope, Stage 8 provides precursors):

    • ZrO₂ from Stage 8 dissociation (3.2 kg/batch)
    • B₂O₃ from NdFeB boron (0.07 kg/batch) + supplemental
    • Carbon from char residue (1-3 kg/batch)
    • Temperature: 1800°C, 2 hr, Ar atmosphere
    • Product: ZrB₂ powder, 99% purity, <1 μm

    8.2 ZrB₂-SiC Drum Material (PROD-04 Loop)

    Drum Composition: ZrB₂ (70 vol%) + SiC (30 vol%)

    • ZrB₂ from Stage 8 carbothermal
    • SiC from Stage 3 char carbothermal + supplemental
    • Flash sintered at 1900°C/5 min (same technology as 3Y-TZP)
    • Closed loop: Drum material produced from Forge's own output

    Mass Balance — Drum Material per Batch: 

    ZrB₂ needed per drum: 50 kg (ZrB₂-SiC composite, 70/30)
ZrB₂ from Stage 8: 3.2 kg/batch
Batches per drum: 16
Drum life: 500 batches → 31 drum lifetimes per batch equivalent

    8.3 Ti₃AlC₂ MAX Phase Synthesis (FOLLOW-32)

    Reaction: 

    3TiO₂ + Al₂O₃ + 4C → Ti₃AlC₂ + 4CO
    • TiO₂ from Stage 8 (0.7+ kg/batch)
    • Al₂O₃ from Stage 8 (5+ kg/batch)
    • Carbon from char
    • Product: Ti₃AlC₂ powder → MXene (Ti₃C₂Tₓ) via HF etching (FOLLOW-32)

    13. Control System

    13.1 Control Architecture — Stage 8 Specific

    Cascade PID Structure (from PROD-10, extended for Stage 8): 

    STAGE 8 CONTROL HIERARCHY
══════════════════════════
    


    SUPERVISORY (1 Hz)
├── Batch State Machine: CHARGE → DISSOCIATION → FLASH_SINTER → RESIDUAL_SEP → COOLDOWN
├── Recipe Management: Temp profile, RPM, gas, power, pO₂, precursor additions
├── Quality Gate: XRD dissociation, 3Y-TZP density, SiO₂ SSA
├── Precursor Management: Y₂O₃, B₂O₃, C inventory, addition scheduling
└── Phoenix Registry: Slug UUID, grade, downstream route (FOLLOW-16,21,32)
    


    ZONE 8 PID (1 kHz) — PROD-10 Zone 8
├── Master: Drum wall temp (FBG median, 48 sensors) → Power setpoint
├── Slave 1: Resonance tracking (GaN inverter) → Frequency/phase (1 kHz ZVS)
├── Slave 2: POF level (slag height) → Feed rate
├── Slave 3: Gas analyzer (Ar, He, O₂, SiO) → MFC setpoints, condenser flow
├── Slave 4: Pyrometer (surface) → Temp cross-check
├── Slave 5: ZrO₂ probe (pO₂) → Ar/He ratio, getter status
├── Slave 6: Flash sinter cell (V, I, T) → Field profile, duration
├── Slave 7: Port 8A mold FBG (6 per mold) → N₂ quench flow
└── Slave 8: Port 8B condenser temp → Coolant flow
    


    DISSOCIATION MONITOR (10 Hz)
├── READ MS_SiO₂ → p_SiO₂
├── TARGET p_SiO₂ = 10⁻³ atm
├── IF p_SiO₂ > 10⁻²: INCREASE Ar sweep, DECREASE power
├── IF p_SiO₂ < 10⁻⁴: DECREASE Ar sweep (SiO₂ re-deposition risk)
├── CALCULATE X_diss = 1 - (p_SiO₂_measured / p_SiO₂_initial)^(1/3)
├── IF X_diss < 0.95 at t=25 min: EXTEND dwell, ALERT
    


    FLASH SINTER CONTROL (100 Hz)
├── READ V_cell, I_cell, T_pyrometer
├── TARGET: T=1800°C, E=300 V/cm, t=300s
├── RAMP: E = 100 + 200×(t/60) V/cm for t<60s
├── FLASH DETECTION: dI/dt > threshold → thermal runaway start
├── HOLD: E = 300 V/cm, PID on T_pyrometer
├── IF T > 1850°C: REDUCE E, ALERT
├── COOL: E = 0, N₂ quench profile
    


    DUAL-PORT CAROUSEL CONTROL (10 Hz)
├── Port 8A (3Y-TZP): 2 molds × 10 kg, flash sinter sync
├── Port 8A (final): Al₂O₃/TiO₂/REE concentrate
├── Port 8B (SiO₂): Continuous condenser, no mold
├── Cool: N₂ quench profile per material
├── Demold/Stamp/LIBS/Registry: per PROD-08
    


    SAFETY INTERLOCKS (Hardwired, <10 ms)
├── pO₂ > 10⁻¹⁰ atm → Emergency Ar flood, power cut
├── SiO > 10 ppm in off-gas → Condenser check, power cut
├── Temp > 2250°C → Power cut, Ar flood
├── Pressure > 1.3 bar → Vent, power cut
├── Vibration > 3 G → Power cut (lower RPM = lower G tolerance)
├── FBG comm loss > 100 ms → Power cut
├── Flash cell V > 200V or I > 600A → Power cut
├── Carousel position error > 1° → E-stop
└── O₂ area < 19.5% → Evacuation alarm, Ar purge

    13.2 Key Control Algorithms

    Zircon Dissociation Control: 

    X_diss_target = 0.95
p_SiO₂_setpoint = 10⁻³ atm
MEASURED_X_diss = 1 - (MS_SiO₂ / MS_SiO₂_initial)^(1/3)
ERROR_diss = X_diss_target - MEASURED_X_diss
IF ERROR_diss > 0.05 at t>20 min:
    EXTEND dwell by ERROR_diss × 600 s
    INCREASE power by 10%
    LOG to batch record

    Flash Sinter Detection: 

    FLASH_DETECTED = (dI_cell/dt > 50 A/s) AND (T_pyrometer > 1750°C)
IF FLASH_DETECTED:
    LOG flash_time
    SWITCH to hold_mode (E=300 V/cm constant)
    TARGET_T = 1800°C
    PID_GAINS: Kp=0.5, Ki=0.01, Kd=0.1 (pre-tuned)

    REE/Al/Ti Separation Verification: 

    IF Zone 8-4 active:
    READ XRF_residual → C_Al, C_Ti, C_REE, C_Zr
    IF C_Zr > 5% in residual: ZrO₂ carryover → ALERT, adjust Zone 8-3 duration
    IF C_REE < 5% in concentrate: REE loss → ALERT, check Zone 8-2 dissociation

    PROD-22: Phoenix Protocol Integration

    1. Phoenix Protocol Overview

    1.1 Mission Statement

    The Phoenix Protocol is the operational doctrine that transforms the Aegis-Forge I from a waste-processing machine into a perpetual material engine. Its mandate: 100% end-of-life (EOL) product return, zero-waste loop, and critical mineral sovereignty for the Carrington Storm Motors (CSM) portfolio. Every Aegis product — from Embark wall panels to Faraday alarms to Phantom robots — is designed from inception to re-enter the Forge at end of service. The Protocol closes the loop between product retirement and seed material generation.

    1.2 Strategic Imperatives

    ImperativeDescriptionKPI Target ------------------------------------- Take-Back Compliance5-year warranty with recovery incentive drives return rate>95% of CSM products by mass Material SovereigntyEliminate external supply chain for Zr, REE, In, Co, Nb, W85% in-house/recycled by Year 5 Carbon NegativityMgO carbonation + avoided primary production sequesters CO₂-2.3 tCO₂e/ton EOL processed Economic AutonomyEOL revenue funds Phase 2-3 machine construction$3.25M per 10,000 panels retired TraceabilityUUID chain from mine → Forge → product → return → ForgeBlockchain-anchored digital twin

    1.3 Protocol Architecture

    The Phoenix Protocol operates as a three-layer recursive system:

    Layer 1 — Collection & Disassembly (Depot Network)
    ↓ Feedstock Classification (Category A-D per PROD-13)
Layer 2 — Forge Re-Entry (Stage-by-Stage Material Routing)
    ↓ Product Regeneration (Hydromet, SPS, SHS, Solvolysis)
Layer 3 — Product Re-Manufacture (Assembly Line Integration)
    ↓ Product Deployment → End of Service → Layer 1

    Each layer validates the next. Layer 1 output (classified feedstock) must meet Layer 2 re-entry specifications. Layer 2 output (regenerated seed materials) must meet Layer 3 production tolerances. Layer 3 products must be designed for Layer 1 disassembly. The recursion is the guarantee.

    1.4 Design-for-Disassembly (DfD) Principles

    Every Aegis product embeds DfD from CAD conception:

    DfD PrincipleImplementationVerification --------------------------------------------- Modular JointsPEEK CF40 threaded inserts, ZrO₂ alignment pinsTorque-to-yield spec, ultrasonic inspect Material SegregationNo overmolding, no adhesives between material classesVisual + LIBS at disassembly Fastener StandardizationSingle PEEK CF40 M8×1.25 for all structural jointsGauge check at depot Fluid Drain PortsTi₃AlC₂ ball valves on all fluid circuitsPressure decay test Component LabelingLaser-etched UUID + material code on every part >50gLIBS reads code at disassembly Hazard IsolationBatteries, capacitors in dedicated cassettes (tool-free remove)Depot scan verifies removal

    DfD Compliance Metric: Disassembly time ≤ 15 min/product (automated), ≤ 45 min (manual fallback).

    1.5 Protocol Governance

    Phoenix Protocol Steering Committee (PPSC):

    • Chair: CSM VP Materials & Circularity
    • Members: Forge Operations Director, Depot Network Lead, Hydromet Chief Engineer, Digital Twin Architect, Sustainability Officer, Legal/Compliance
    • Meets: Monthly (operational), Quarterly (strategic)
    • Authority: Approve blend ratio changes, new re-entry paths, depot expansions, protocol amendments

    Protocol Amendment Process: 1. Change Request (CR) submitted via Git (PROD-38 Config Mgmt) 2. Impact Assessment: Mass balance, energy, safety, economics, schedule 3. PPSC Review: Technical feasibility + business case 4. Approval: Unanimous for safety, majority for ops/econ 5. Implementation: Staged rollout (1 Forge → 3 Forges → Fleet) 6. Validation: 100 batches at new spec before fleet deployment

    Version Control: Protocol v1.0 (this document) → v1.x (operational tweaks) → v2.0 (major architecture change). All versions archived in Git with tagged releases.

    2. Return Logistics Network

    2.1 Collection Hub Topology

    Hub Equipment (Primary):

    • Automated disassembly cell (6-axis + vision, 15 min/product)

    2.2 Transport Specification — DUNNAGE-FREE

    All EOL material moves in BFRP/Elium® crates (CSMFAB-P001 spec):

    • Crate dimensions: 1200×800×600 mm (Euro-pallet compatible)
    • Mass: 18 kg empty, 500 kg loaded
    • Stackable 4-high, forklift pockets, RFID + QR + Data Matrix
    • Hermetic seal option (Ar backfill) for reactive fractions
    • Crate life: 500 cycles → crushed → BFRP recycling (thermal solvolysis)

    No wood, cardboard, foam, or plastic dunnage. Ever. The crate IS the packaging.

    2.4 Reverse Logistics Optimization

    Vehicle Routing Problem (VRP) Solution:

    • Algorithm: Clarke-Wright savings + 2-opt local search
    • Objective: Minimize Σ(distance × carbon intensity) subject to hub capacity
    • Fleet: Electric Class 8 (500 km range) for Secondary→Primary; Diesel hybrid for Tertiary→Secondary
    • Load Consolidation: Minimum 80% crate fill before dispatch
    • Backhaul: Return empty crates + deliver virgin feedstock (BFRP crates, Ar cylinders)

    Network KPIs:

    • Average haul distance: 320 km (Primary←Secondary), 65 km (Secondary←Tertiary)
    • Crate turnaround: 14 days (return → clean → redeploy)
    • Carbon intensity: 0.08 kg CO₂e/ton-km (electric) vs. 0.22 (diesel)

    4. Preprocessing at Depot

    4.1 Disassembly Sequence (Automated Cell)

    Step 1: Electronic/Optical Extraction (2 min)

      

    • Vision-guided 6-axis removes PCBs, displays, sensors, LoRa modules
      • 

    • Output: Electronics fraction → Stage 0 (AMLS) or refurbishment queue
      • 

    


    Step 2: Hardware Removal (3 min)

      

    • PEEK CF40 fasteners, ZrO₂ ceramic bearings, Ti₃AlC₂ EMI shields
      • 

    • Ultrasonic clean (40 kHz, 60°C, 10 min) → inspect → re-use queue
      • 

    


    Step 3: BFRP Structural Solvolysis (120 min batch)

      

    • Elium® resin depolymerization: 350°C, 2h, N₂ atmosphere, 15 bar
      • 

    • Monomer recovery: MMA >99%, glycol >98% → distillation → Elium® reformulation
      • 

    • Basalt fiber recovery: 95% yield, 15-20 μm diameter retained
      • 

    • Output: Clean fiber bundles → BFRP pultrusion (FOLLOW-05)
      • 

    


    Step 4: Ceramic Core Processing (15 min)

      

    • ZrB₂-SiC panel cores: Jaw crush → ball mill (3-5 μm) → hydromet (H₂SO₄ leach)
      • 

    • ZrO₂/Si₃N₄ buffers: Separate stream → re-precipitation (3Y-TZP) or direct SPS
      • 

    • Output: Zr/Y hydroxide gel → calcination → 3Y-TZP powder (Stage 8 loop)
      • 

    


    Step 5: Critical Mineral Glaze Recovery (30 min)

      

    • YInMn Blue (exterior): H₂SO₄ leach → ionic liquid [P₈₈₈₈][Cl] extraction
      • 

    • CoAl₂O₄ Cobalt Blue (interior): HCl dissolution → electroplating
      • 

    • Output: In 99.9% (YInMn), Y 98% (YSZ), Co 98% (electroplated)
      • 

    


    Step 6: Fluid & Battery Drain (5 min)

      

    • MRF-140CG: Centrifugal separation → quality cert → re-fill
      • 

    • LiFePO₄: Full discharge → hydromet (LFP precursor recovery)

Example: CSM-AUS-ZIRC-2026-11-02-08-21-8A-001-EMBARK-WALL-001-RTN-03

Product: Slug UUID, composition, grade 6. Downstream: CSMFAB product or commercial sale 7. Return Cycle: 0 = virgin, 1+ = recycled

    7. Drum Material Circularity

    7.1 ZrB₂-SiC Drum Life Cycle

    NEW DRUM (Gen 1)
    │
    ├─→ 500 batches (90-min cycle each = 750 hr operation)
    │     └─→ FBG monitoring: wall thickness, thermal gradient, seal integrity
    │
    ├─→ End-of-Life Criteria:
    │     • Wall thinning >15% (ultrasonic)
    │     • Seal leak rate >10⁻⁶ mbar·L/s
    │     • FBG drift >±5°C uncorrectable
    │     • Crack detection (acoustic emission >threshold)
    │
    └─→ RETIREMENT → Phoenix Depot
          │
          ├─→ Crush → Ball Mill (3-5 μm)
          │
          ├─→ Hydrometallurgical Zr Recovery:
          │     H₂SO₄ leach (95°C, 4h) → Zr⁴⁺ in solution
          │     NH₄OH co-precipitation (with Y³⁺ from REE stream)
          │     → Zr-Y hydroxide gel → 120°C dry → 1200°C calcine (4h)
          │     → 3Y-TZP ZrO₂ powder (97% TD target)
          │
          ├─→ Carbothermal ZrB₂ Synthesis:
          │     ZrO₂ + B₂O₃ + 5C → ZrB₂ + 5CO (1800°C, 2h, Ar)
          │     OR SHS: Zr + 2B → ZrB₂ (1h, self-propagating)
          │
          └─→ Flash Sinter → NEW DRUM (Gen 2)
                (Same ZrB₂-SiC spec as PROD-04)

    7.4 Drum Recycling Process Flow (Detailed)

    RETIRED DRUM (500 batches)
         │
         ▼
Phoenix Depot Receiving
         │
         ▼
Non-Destructive Evaluation:
  • Ultrasonic wall thickness map (200 points)
  • FBG thermal history replay
  • Acoustic emission scan (crack map)
  • Helium leak test (all ports, seals)
         │
         ▼
Segregation Decision:
  ├─→ PRIME (wall >85%, no cracks) → Direct re-SPS (Gen +1)
  ├─→ STANDARD (wall 70-85%, minor cracks) → Crush → Hydromet (Gen +1)
  └─→ SCRAP (wall <70%, major cracks) → Crush → Hydromet (Gen +1, lower yield)
         │
         ▼ (for STANDARD/SCRAP)
Crushing Circuit:
  • Jaw crusher (50 mm) → Cone crusher (5 mm) → Ball mill (3-5 μm)
  • Argon atmosphere, -40°C dew point (prevent oxidation)
  • Throughput: 500 kg/hr per line
         │
         ▼
Hydrometallurgical Zr Recovery:
  • Reactor: BFRP/Elium®, 2000L, H₂SO₄ 2M, 95°C, 4h, stir 200 RPM
  • Leach efficiency: 96% Zr, 94% Y, 92% Si (reports to silica stream)
  • Solid residue: SiC (unleached) → filter → dry → SiC recycle stream
  • Filtrate: Zr⁴⁺, Y³⁺, Fe³⁺, Al³⁺, Ti⁴⁺ in solution
         │
         ▼
Selective Precipitation:
  1. pH 2.5 (NH₄OH): Fe³⁺, Al³⁺ → hydroxide (waste → Stage 7 slag)
  2. pH 5.5: Ti⁴⁺ → TiO₂·xH₂O (filter → Stage 8 TiO₂ stream)
  3. pH 8.0: Zr⁴⁺ + Y³⁺ → Zr-Y hydroxide gel (co-precipitate)
  4. pH 10.5: Residual REE → REE hydroxide (FOLLOW-15)
         │
         ▼
Gel Processing:
  • Filter press (BFRP plates, PEEK CF40 cloth) → 35% solids
  • Wash: 3× DI water (counter-current) → Cl⁻ <50 ppm, SO₄²⁻ <100 ppm
  • Dry: 120°C, 4h, N₂ atmosphere → free-flowing powder
  • Calcination: 1200°C, 4h, air → 3Y-TZP crystalline (97% theoretical)
         │
         ▼
Carbothermal ZrB₂ Synthesis (FOLLOW-32):
  • Mix: 3Y-TZP + B₂O₃ + 5C (molar 1:1:5) + 2% B₄C sintering aid
  • Press: 100 MPa → green density 55% TD
  • Furnace: Induction, 1800°C, 2h, Ar, graphite susceptor
  • Conversion: 98.5% → ZrB₂ + 5CO (gas captured → PROD-07)
  • Mill: 3-5 μm, narrow distribution (D90/D10 <2.5)
         │
         ▼
Flash Sintering (PROD-04 / FOLLOW-01):
  • 3Y-TZP + ZrB₂ composite → 1800°C, 300 V/cm, 5 min
  • 97% TD, 0.5 μm grain, ZrB₂ percolation network
  • Result: NEW DRUM (Gen N+1)

    7.5 Drum Recycling Energy & Emissions

    Process StepEnergy (kWh/kg ZrB₂)CO₂e (kg/kg)Notes -------------------------------------------------------- Crushing & milling80.5Argon atmosphere H₂SO₄ leach (95°C, 4h)120.8Steam heat recovery 60% Precipitation & wash30.2Counter-current water Calcination (1200°C, 4h)251.5NG-fired, 85% efficiency Carbothermal (1800°C, 2h)452.8Induction, Ar, CO capture Flash sinter (1800°C, 5 min)181.1300 V/cm, 5 min TOTAL111 kWh/kg6.9 kg CO₂e/kgvs. 280 kWh/kg virgin

    Carbon Advantage: Recycled drum ZrB₂ = 6.9 kg CO₂e/kg vs. virgin 45 kg CO₂e/kg → 85% reduction. At 500 kg/drum × 31 generations = 15,500 kg ZrB₂ saved per initial drum = 590 tCO₂e avoided per drum lineage.

    Appendix B: Re-Entry Specification Sheets (Per Category)

    B.1 Category D1 — Intact Aegis Products

    • Max dimension: 1200×800×600 mm (crate limit)
    • Max mass: 500 kg/crate
    • Battery state: <30% SoC (auto-discharge at depot)
    • Documentation: Product passport QR on crate
    • Re-entry: Full disassembly → component sort

    B.2 Category D2 — Structural BFRP

    • Format: Panels, beams, profiles (any geometry)
    • Contamination: <1% metal fasteners (removed pre-solvolysis)
    • Moisture: <2% (oven dry if needed)
    • Re-entry: Stage 3 feed (carbon) + FOLLOW-05 (fiber)

    B.3 Category D3 — Ceramic Cores

    • Size: Crushed 3-5 μm (ball mill at depot)
    • Purity: >90% ZrB₂-SiC / ZrO₂ / Si₃N₄
    • Surface: Clean, no organic residue
    • Re-entry: Stage 8 (Zr) or hydromet direct

    B.4 Category D4 — Mineral Fractions

    • In/Y/Co concentrates: >50% target element
    • Particle size: <100 μm
    • Acid consumption: Pre-measured, <200 kg acid/ton
    • Re-entry: Stage 4 (In), Stage 8 (Y, Zr), Stage 7 (Co)

    B.5 Category D5 — Electronic Assemblies

    • PCB types: FR4, CEM-1, polyimide flex, ceramic substrate
    • Component density: <500 components/board (else pre-sort)
    • Battery-free: Certified by depot discharge station
    • Re-entry: Stage 0 AMLS liberation → Stage 2 polymer → Stage 6 Cu/PM

    B.6 Category D6 — Energy Storage

    • Chemistry: LiFePO₄ only (CSM standard)
    • Format: 18650, 21700, prismatic, pouch
    • SoC on arrival: <30% (enforced at Tertiary hub)
    • Re-entry: Full discharge → hydromet (FOLLOW-34 grid storage integration)

    B.7 Category D7 — MAX Phase Components

    • Geometry: Shields, bearings, heating elements
    • Surface condition: <50 μm wear depth (else recycle)
    • Contamination: No braze alloys, no dissimilar metal joints
    • Re-entry: Chloride-thermal extraction → re-synthesis (Section 8)
