    PROD-23: Control System Architecture

    Combined Heuristic Intro — PROD-23 Control System Architecture

    Williams / Keymaker / El Segundo Synthesis

    The Lock That Forges the Key

    The Aegis-Forge I control system exists because a 2200°C induction furnace cannot tolerate a single copper wire crossing its pressure boundary during a Carrington storm. This constraint (Williams: Constraint) is not negotiable — it is physics. A 5000 nT/s geomagnetic field induces >100 A/km in conductors. Inside the forge, that coupling destroys GaN gate drivers (6 V threshold), corrupts safety logic, and melts the ZrB₂-SiC drum.

    The empirical gap (Williams: Necessity) is the measured divergence between continuous-time control theory and discrete-time implementation under electromagnetic hostility. PROD-10 and PROD-03 establish the theoretical baseline: 8-zone Class E inverters, 100 kHz → 1 kHz, ZVS maintained by varactor tuning. But fabrication reality demands: (1) FBG sensors at 125 Hz each, 384 channels, reconstructed via 1 kHz thermal model because PMMA degrades >800°C; (2) PLL lock acquisition <50 ms while varactor updates 100× slower than GaN switching; (3) SIL-3 SIFs with 2oo3 voting on sensors that share cable trays, power supplies, and interrogators — physical independence ≠ functional independence.

    The fabrication fidelity gap (Keymaker: Empirical Lock) is precisely this divergence: continuous phase control vs. 100× slower varactor actuation; point measurement at cold flange → inference of hot drum inner surface; common-cause failure modes that defeat 2oo3 voting.

    The Mathematical Key That Turns the Lock

    The single computational primitive that generates the solution is the discrete-time thermal-admittance model executed at 1 kHz on the Zone RTU:

    T_inner[k+1] = T_inner[k] + (Δt/ρcV) × (P_ind[k] - hA(T_inner[k] - T_flange[k]) - εσA(T_inner⁴[k] - T_surr⁴))

    This one equation, discretized with Δt = 1 ms on ARM Cortex-A53 (Zephyr, <100 μs compute), is the atomic computation (Keymaker: Mathematical Key). Everything derives from it:

    • Thermal PID setpoint → power command via inverse model + PID
    • Resonance tracker → frequency/varactor via pre-computed LUT (PROD-10)
    • Cascade feedforward → downstream stage setpoints with transport delay
    • SIF trip logic → predicted T_inner 50 ms ahead → pre-emptive trip
    • Digital twin sync → full state trajectory at 10 Hz for PROD-37

    Theory→History validation (Keymaker: Turn): The model predicts CSMFAB0108 test data within measurement uncertainty — 500 kW step to 1800°C in 42 s predicted, 45 s measured; ZVS lock 38 ms predicted, 35 ms measured; SIF trip 38 ms predicted, 36 ms measured.

    History→Theory correction (Keymaker: Turn): Char growth oscillation (15°C at 0.8 Hz) → added char-thickness state to RLS. FBG drift (0.5 nm/hr) → reference FBG common-mode subtraction. TSN latency spike (2.3 ms) → local OCXO on each node. Varactor saturation (28 V) → 8-bit cap bank + slag-level feedforward.

    The mathematical key absorbs history — each anomaly extends the model, the core primitive remains unchanged.

    The Mirror That Witnesses the Fabrication

    The forge observes its own fabrication through four nested metrology loops (El Segundo: Mirror):

    1. Microsecond (L0 FPGA): Gate-level witness — desat detect at 10 ns, ZVS timestamp vs. gate command, current sense at 1 MHz. The FPGA sees the switch fail before it destroys itself. ZVS achievement >99.9%/cycle.

    2. Millisecond (L1 RTU): Thermal reconstruction — virtual sensor running the atomic computation. 48 FBG inputs → T_inner prediction ±5°C at 2200°C. Model residual <2°C RMS or re-identification triggers.

    3. 100 ms (L2 PLC): Cascade consistency — mass-energy balance across stages. XRF/LIBS composition → feedforward. Elemental closure >99.5%/batch or investigation flagged.

    4. 100 ms (L3 SCADA → PROD-37): Digital twin shadow — 512-core HPC runs same models + CFD + FEA. ML autoencoder (FOLLOW-29) flags >3σ deviation. Twin suggests PID gains, flux rates, RPM profiles.

    The fabricator watches the process at the scale of the phenomenon: gate switching (10 ns), thermal diffusion (1 ms), material transformation (100 ms), fleet optimization (continuous).

    The Participation That Authorizes Consequence

    The inside operator witnesses the phenomenon into existence at four cognitive checkpoints (El Segundo: Participation) where judgment cannot be automated:

    1. Batch Recipe Authorization: Feedstock UUID scanned → Category A–D → Operator confirms recipe. Wrong choice = slag, port blockage, weeks downtime. PVC >5% in Category B requires HCl management judgment (PROD-15).

    2. Stage Transition Gate: Stage complete → Shift Lead reviews energy, yield, gas, SIF events, anomalies. Stage 4: visual In-grade confirmation (pyrometer + XRF). Stage 6: H₂ <4% verification before Port 6B open.

    3. SIF Bypass Authorization: Dual-key (Shift Lead + Safety Engineer), time-limited (4 hr), blockchain-audited. Risk acceptance is human — no algorithm accepts organizational risk.

    5. Carrington Ride-Through Exit: Post-GIC, grid stable 30 min → Operator verifies drum thermal state (no shock >100°C/s), SIF health, authorizes staged grid reconnect with utility coordination.

    Automation executes; humans authorize at boundaries of consequence. HMI (ISA-101) presents exactly needed information — no alarm flood.

    The Protocol That Guarantees Fidelity at Every Scale

    The recursive V&V fractal (El Segundo: Protocol) mirrors verification structure across five scales:

    ScaleArtifactPattern -------------------------- L0 ComponentFPGA bitstream + 100% coverage + HIL 10⁶ cyclesStimulate → Observe → Compare → Act L1 ModuleRTU firmware + mutation testing >90% + 72 hr soakStimulate → Observe → Compare → Act L2 SubsystemPLC/SIS signed + formal verification + SIF injectionStimulate → Observe → Compare → Act L3 SystemFAT: 8 RTUs + 8 PLCs + SIS + SCADA on TSNStimulate → Observe → Compare → Act L4 DeploymentSAT: 10 production batches, zero spurious tripsStimulate → Observe → Compare → Act L5 SustainmentQuarterly partial-stroke, annual full proof, twin shadowStimulate → Observe → Compare → Act

    Recursive invariant: Evidence(level) ⊆ Evidence(level+1). Evidence accumulates upward. Git tag chain (fpga-v1.3.7 → rtu-v2.1.4 → stg04-v3.0.1 → forge-fat-v1.0 → forge-sat-v1.0) is the cryptographic proof.

    The Commitments That Constrain the System

    This document locks in (Williams: Commitment) seven non-negotiables for all downstream documents:

    1. Four-level hierarchy fixed: L0 (100 kHz) → L1 (1 kHz) → L2 (100 Hz) → L3 (10 Hz). Time constants are physical.

    2. PMMA POF only fieldbus: 480+ sensors, 96+ actuators, PTP, TSN — all dielectric. FOLLOW-11 validates 10-year lifetime.

    3. 24 SIL-3 SIFs immutable: Table 6.2 defines safety envelope. PROD-26, 32, 39 must validate. No downgrade without re-cert.

    4. TSN schedule frozen: 1 ms cycle, 4 slices (SIS/RTU/PLC/SCADA), 100 μs guard band. FOLLOW-29 operates in best-effort only.

    5. Air-gap absolute: No IT→OT IP. Data diode unidirectional (OT→IT). PROD-36, 37 architect around this.

    6. GIC ride-through mandatory: 5 ms transition, 10 ms island, LiFePO₄ backup indefinite. PROD-10 sizes DC link caps.

    7. ISA-88 recipe schema: XML structure (Section 4.5) for thermal, gas, flux, ports, interlocks. PROD-14–21 populate. PROD-38 versions in Git.

    8. PTP <1 μs required: GNSS+OCXO grandmaster, 24h holdover, all nodes boundary clocks. FOLLOW-11 embeds PTP in interrogator.

    These are the architectural load-bearing walls. PROD-24 (Thermal Model), PROD-26 (GIC), PROD-29 (Operations), PROD-37 (Digital Twin), FOLLOW-10/11/27/29 build on this foundation. They cannot move the walls.

    Aegis-Forge I: Control System Architecture — Distributed Control, Safety Interlocks & Carrington Immunity

    Hierarchical FPGA/RTU/PLC/SCADA, SIL-3 SIS, TSN Network, GIC-Hardened OT

    Document Number: CSMFAB000000000123 (PROD-23) Series: Aegis-Forge Thermal Cascade Inductive Material Separator (TCIMS) Date: November 2026 Classification: CSMFAB Internal — Engineering Specification Revision: 1.0

    1. Control Architecture Overview

    1.1 Design Philosophy

    The Aegis-Forge I control system is a four-level hierarchical distributed architecture designed to operate in the most hostile electromagnetic environment on Earth: inside a 500 kW induction furnace at 2200°C, during a Carrington-class geomagnetic storm. Every design decision flows from three irreducible constraints:

    1. All-Dielectric Sensing & Actuation: No copper wires cross the pressure boundary. All 480+ field devices communicate via PMMA POF optical fiber. This eliminates antenna effects for GIC/EMP. 2. Deterministic Real-Time Control: 1 kHz zone-level PID loops with resonance tracking require <1 ms jitter. Achieved via TSN (IEEE 802.1Qbv) time-aware scheduling on a dual-ring 1 Gbps optical network. 3. SIL-3 Safety Integrity: 24 safety instrumented functions with 2oo3 voting, <50 ms response, certified to IEC 61508/ISA-84.

    3.4 Resonance Tracker (PLL) Design

    The Class E inverter maintains ZVS by aligning the switch voltage zero-crossing with the gate turn-on instant. A software PLL runs at 100 Hz:

    Phase Error:  φ_err = t(V_DS=0) - t(gate_on)


    PLL Output:   ΔV_varactor = K_p_PLL × φ_err + K_i_PLL × ∫φ_err dt
              ΔCap_Bank   = round(ΔV_varactor / V_per_step)  (coarse)
    


    Gains:        K_p_PLL = 0.05 V/ns,  K_i_PLL = 500 V/s
Lock Range:   ±5% of nominal frequency
Acquisition:  <50 ms from cold start

    FPGA Interface: The RTU sends varactor bias (16-bit DAC) and cap bank select (6-bit GPIO) to the Cell FPGA via PMMA POF. The FPGA updates the hardware within 10 μs.

    3.5 FBG Acquisition & Processing

    FBG Interrogator (per Zone RTU):
├── VCSEL: 650-850 nm sweep, 1 kHz triangle wave
├── WDM: 8-channel thin-film filter (20 nm spacing)
├── TDM: 1×6 PMMA splitter per wavelength
├── Detection: Balanced InGaAs PIN, 2 MHz BW
├── Processing: Peak detection (centroid), λ → T conversion
│   T = (λ_measured - λ_ref) / 0.15 nm/°C  (PMMA FBG sensitivity)
├── Output: 48 temperatures @ 125 Hz each (6 per TDM channel)
└── Health: SNR >20 dB, peak width <0.5 nm, no missing channels

    Fault Handling: If >10 sensors in a zone report invalid data → RTU limits zone power to 50%, raises SCADA alarm, logs event.

    • Stage 5→6: Al removed, Mg content, dross composition
    • Stage 6→7: Cu removed, PM grade, Fe/REE in residue
    • Stage 7→8: Slag composition (B=1.2, MgO/Al₂O₃=1.5), FeO, REE oxides

    7. Carrington GIC Immunity — EMP-Hardened OT

    7.1 Threat Model

    PhenomenonParameterStandard --------------------------------- GIC (Geomagnetic)dB/dt = 5000 nT/s, 100 A/km inducedIEEE Std 1656 E1 HEMP50 kV/m, 1 ns rise, 100 MHz bandwidthIEC 61000-2-9 E2 HEMP1-10 kV/m, 1 μs-1 ms, similar to lightningIEC 61000-4-25 E3 HEMPSlow (1-100 s), quasi-DC, like GICIEC 61000-4-34 Surface Charging>10 kV (space environment)MIL-STD-1857

    7.2 Hardening Architecture

    LayerMitigationImplementation ----------------------------------- PhysicalFaraday cage RTUsBFRP housing + conductive YInMn glaze (σ = 10⁴ S/m) PowerFloating secondaryIsolation transformers (Δ-Y), no earth reference PowerNGR limiting5 A high-resistance grounding PowerSurge protectionGDT (3 kA) + MOV at transformer primary SignalAll-dielectric commsPMMA POF — zero conductive path SignalOptical isolationNo copper crossing pressure boundary SignalCommon-mode chokeNanocrystalline on any residual copper NetworkTSN dual-ringNo single point of failure, deterministic CyberAir-gap + data diodeUnidirectional to IT, no external IP FirmwareSigned bootSecure boot on all FPGA/RTU/PLC

    7.3 GIC Ride-Through Mode

    When grid dV/dt > threshold (detected by dedicated monitor):

    1. Detection (1 ms): Grid monitor FPGA triggers interrupt 2. Transition (5 ms): Inverters switch to "ride-through" — maintain DC link from bus capacitors 3. Isolation (10 ms): Physical contactors open (vacuum, BFRP housed) — Forge islanded 4. Sustain (indefinite): LiFePO₄ backup (100 Wh) powers control system; drum coast-down 5. Reconnect (auto): When grid stable >30 s, pre-charge → contactor close → resume

    Validation: Tested at up to 100 A/m simulated field (Helmholtz coil facility). No protection trips, no data loss.

    10.2 Defense in Depth

    LayerControls ----------------- PerimeterPhysical air-gap, data diode, no internet connectivity NetworkTSN VLAN segmentation, MACsec encryption, port security HostImmutable OS (NixOS), signed firmware, no package manager runtime ApplicationRole-based access (Operator/Engineer/Safety/Admin), MFA (hardware token) DataEncryption at rest (AES-256), blockchain-anchored audit log MonitoringML anomaly detection (FOLLOW-29), behavioral baselines, zero-trust

    10.3 Anomaly Detection (FOLLOW-29 Integration)

    • Model: LSTM autoencoder trained on 6 months normal operation
    • Inputs: All 480+ sensor streams, network traffic, PLC scan times
    • Output: Anomaly score (0-1), alert if >0.95 for >10 s
    • Response: Auto-isolate affected VLAN, alert SOC, log full context
    • False Positive Rate: <0.1% (validated on 10,000 batches)

    The Lock That Forges the Key

    The Aegis-Forge I control system exists because a 2200°C induction furnace cannot tolerate a single copper wire crossing its pressure boundary during a Carrington storm. This constraint (Williams: Constraint) is not negotiable — it is physics. A 5000 nT/s geomagnetic field induces >100 A/km in conductors. Inside the forge, that coupling destroys GaN gate drivers (6 V threshold), corrupts safety logic, and melts the ZrB₂-SiC drum.

    The empirical gap (Williams: Necessity) is the measured divergence between continuous-time control theory and discrete-time implementation under electromagnetic hostility.     PROD-24: Thermal Modeling and Simulation

    Combined Heuristic Intro — PROD-24 Thermal Modeling & Simulation

    Williams / Keymaker / El Segundo Synthesis

    The Lock That Forges the Key

    The Aegis-Forge I thermal model exists because induction heating power is a nonlinear function of the very temperature it creates, and the material properties governing both are themselves strong functions of temperature. This constraint (Williams: Constraint) is not a modeling preference — it is physics. At Stage 7, Fe ferromagnetic permeability drops from 200 to 1 at 770°C, collapsing induction power by 60%. At Stage 8, the 2000°C radial gradient in the 35 mm ZrB₂-SiC drum wall combines thermal stress (220 MPa) with centrifugal stress (185 MPa at 500 RPM) to exceed the 350 MPa allowable — but only when computed together with temperature-dependent $E(T)$, $\alpha(T)$. At Stage 4, gas convection cooling of In droplets ($h_{conv}$) determines whether centrifugal separation succeeds — and $h_{conv}$ is an output of the CFD, not an input.

    The empirical gap (Williams: Necessity) is the measured divergence between single-physics simulations and integrated cascade test data. PROD-10 inverter tests showed Zone 7 power collapsing from 350 kW at 1100°C to 140 kW at 1300°C — a 60% drop invisible to constant-$\mu_r$ models. PROD-04 first-article drum FA-01 showed 385 MPa von Mises at Liner B — 35 MPa over allowable — missed by linear superposition of thermal + centrifugal. PROD-17 batch 1 achieved 97.2% In recovery vs. 99.5% predicted — the gap traced to $h_{conv}$ being 2× higher than assumed.

    The fabrication fidelity gap (Keymaker: Empirical Lock) is precisely this divergence: fixed-property EM models vs. temperature-dependent ferromagnetic coupling; superposition of linear analyses vs. nonlinear combined loading; assumed convection coefficients vs. CFD-resolved gas flow in a rotating drum. Every lock is a coupling that was assumed negligible but measured significant.

    The Mathematical Key That Turns the Lock

    The single computational primitive that generates the solution is the discrete-time thermal-admittance operator evaluated at 1 kHz on the Zone RTU — the same primitive that drives the control system (PROD-23):

    $$ \mathcal{T}[T_{inner}, T_{flange}, P_{ind}, h, \epsilon] : \quad T_{inner}[k+1] = T_{inner}[k] + \frac{\Delta t}{\rho c V} \left( P_{ind}[k] - h A (T_{inner}[k] - T_{flange}[k]) - \epsilon \sigma A (T_{inner}^4[k] - T_{surr}^4) \right) $$

    This one equation, discretized with $\Delta t = 1$ ms on ARM Cortex-A53 (Zephyr, <100 $\mu$s), is the atomic computation (Keymaker: Mathematical Key). Everything derives from it:

    • Full FEA: The operator is the reduced-order model of the 3D FEA. FEA computes $\rho c V(T)$, $h A(T)$, $\epsilon \sigma A(T)$; the operator executes them at control speed.
    • EM-Thermal Coupling: $P_{ind}[k]$ is computed by EM solver using $\rho(T_{inner}[k])$, $\mu_r(T_{inner}[k])$. Fixed-point iteration $\mathcal{T} \circ \mathcal{E}$ is the coupling.
    • Cascade CFD: $h$ is not constant — it is $\mathcal{C}[\omega, T, P, X]$. The operator queries CFD at 10 Hz.
    • Stage Models: Each stage is $\mathcal{T}$ with stage-specific $P_{ind}(t)$, $h(t)$, $\epsilon(t)$, moving boundary $m_{charge}(t)$.
    • Transient Cycling: Operator integrates over 300 min. Fatigue damage from $T(t)$ history.
    • V&V: Code verification validates discretization of $\mathcal{T}$. Solution verification validates convergence of $\mathcal{T} \circ \mathcal{E} \circ \mathcal{C}$.
    • UQ: Sobol indices measure sensitivity of $\mathcal{T}$ outputs to 20 inputs.
    • ROM: POD-Galerkin ROM is projection of $\mathcal{T}$ onto 12 modes.
    • Scaling: Dimensionless groups (Fo, Re, Pe, Nu, $\delta/d$, G) are non-dimensional $\mathcal{T}$.

    Theory→History validation (Keymaker: Turn): The operator predicts CSMFAB0108 test data within measurement uncertainty — FA-01 drum stress 385 MPa predicted vs. 325 MPa measured; Zone 7 power 142 kW predicted vs. 140 kW measured; vessel outer surface 150°C predicted vs. 148°C measured.

Aerogel $k(T)$ updated from guarded hot plate data. CFD-coupled $h_{conv}$ closed In recovery gap. Dual-basis ROM (thermal + structural modes) reduced stress error from 4.2 MPa to 1.1 MPa.

    Aegis-Forge I: Thermal Modeling & Simulation — FEA, CFD, Thermophysical Validation

    Multi-Physics Framework, 50+ Material Properties, V&V Plan, ROM for Digital Twin

    Document Number: CSMFAB000000000124 (PROD-24) Series: Aegis-Forge Thermal Cascade Inductive Material Separator (TCIMS) Date: November 2026 Classification: CSMFAB Internal — Engineering Specification Revision: 1.0

    1. Multi-Physics Framework Overview

    1.1 Design Philosophy

    The Aegis-Forge I thermal model is a four-way coupled multi-physics framework that resolves the simultaneous electromagnetic, thermal, structural, and fluid dynamics phenomena governing the 8-stage thermal cascade. This is not a collection of separate analyses — it is a single computational primitive that captures the irreducible coupling between induction heating and material transformation.

    Irreducible Couplings (The Lock):

    • EM → Thermal: Induction power $P_{ind} = \frac{\pi^2 B^2 d^2 f^2 V}{6\rho}$ (non-mag) or $\frac{\pi B^2 f V}{\mu}$ (ferromagnetic) depends on temperature-dependent $\rho(T)$ and $\mu_r(T)$
    • Thermal → EM: $\rho(T)$ increases 3-5× from RT to melting; $\mu_r$ drops from 200→1 at 770°C Curie transition
    • Thermal → Structural: 2000°C radial gradient → 400 MPa thermal stress in 35 mm ZrB₂-SiC drum wall
    • Structural → Fluid: Drum rotation (0-500 RPM) + centrifugal stratification → phase separation physics
    • Fluid → Thermal: Gas convection coefficients $h(T, v, P)$ depend on flow regime in rotating drum

    The Single Computational Primitive (The Key): 

    T_inner[k+1] = T_inner[k] + (Δt/ρcV) × (P_ind[k] - hA(T_inner[k] - T_flange[k]) - εσA(T_inner⁴[k] - T_surr⁴))
    Discretized at Δt = 1 ms on Zone RTU (PROD-23). This is the atomic computation — all FEA, CFD, and ROM derive from it.

    1.2 Physics Domains & Coupling Strategy

    DomainGoverning EquationsSolverCoupling VariablesUpdate Rate --------------------------------------------------------------------- EM (Induction)Maxwell's equations (quasi-static) + CircuitANSYS Maxwell 3D / Custom FEA$P_{ind}(x,y,z,t)$, $B(x,y,z,t)$100 Hz (RTU) Thermal (Transient)$\rho c_p \frac{\partial T}{\partial t} = \nabla \cdot (k \nabla T) + Q_{gen}$ANSYS Transient Thermal / Custom$T(x,y,z,t)$, $h_{eff}(t)$1 kHz (RTU) Structural (Thermo-Mechanical)$\nabla \cdot \sigma + f = 0$, $\sigma = C : (\epsilon - \alpha \Delta T)$ANSYS Mechanical$\sigma(x,y,z,t)$, $\epsilon(x,y,z,t)$100 Hz (PLC) Fluid (Gas-Solid CFD)Navier-Stokes + Lagrangian particle trackingANSYS Fluent / OpenFOAM$v(x,y,z,t)$, $h_{conv}(t)$, RTD10 Hz (SCADA)

    Coupling Strategy:

    • Weak coupling (EM ↔ Thermal): Staggered iteration with Aitken relaxation (ω = 0.7). Converged when $T^{n+1} - T^n < 0.1°C$ per zone
    • One-way coupling (Thermal → Structural): Thermal load mapped to structural mesh at 100 Hz
    • Weak coupling (Structural → Fluid): Drum deformation updates CFD wall boundary at 10 Hz

    3. Electromagnetic-Thermal FEA (Induction Zones)

    3.1 EM Model Formulation

    Governing Equations (Quasi-Static Maxwell): $$\nabla \times (\nu \nabla \times A) + \sigma \frac{\partial A}{\partial t} = J_s$$ $$\nu = 1/\mu = 1/(\mu_0 \mu_r(T))$$

    Where $A$ = magnetic vector potential, $\nu$ = reluctivity, $\sigma$ = electrical conductivity, $J_s$ = source current density.

    Boundary Conditions:

    • Outer boundary: Magnetic insulation ($\mathbf{n} \times A = 0$)
    • Coil terminals: Current excitation $I(t) = I_{rms}\sqrt{2}\sin(2\pi f t)$
    • Symmetry: 1/8 model (45° sector) with periodic BCs

    Mesh Strategy:

    • Air gap (15 mm): 1.5 mm max element, 3 layers normal to B-field
    • Drum wall (35 mm): 2 mm elements, 10 layers through thickness
    • Coil windings: 3 mm elements, explicit turn resolution
    • Far field: 10 mm growing to 50 mm
    • Total DOF: ~1.2M per zone (8 zones = 9.6M, parallelized)

    3.2 Coil-Drum Mutual Inductance Matrix

    The 8-zone coil bank is modeled as a coupled inductor system:

    $$\mathbf{V} = (j\omega\mathbf{L} + \mathbf{R})\mathbf{I} + \mathbf{M}\frac{d\mathbf{I}}{dt}$$

    Where $\mathbf{L}$ = self-inductance matrix (8×8), $\mathbf{M}$ = mutual inductance matrix.

    Zone PairMutual Inductance (μH)Coupling Coefficient -------------------------------------------------------- Adjacent (Z4-Z5)2.10.18 Next-adjacent (Z4-Z6)0.60.05 Separated (Z1-Z8)0.080.007

    Key finding: Cross-zone coupling <5% for adjacent zones, <1% for non-adjacent. Decoupled PID control (PROD-23) is valid. Resonance tracking per zone (PROD-10) compensates for mutual loading.

    3.3 Eddy Current Distribution & Skin Depth Validation

    Analytical Skin Depth (PROD-10): $$\delta = \sqrt{\frac{2\rho}{\omega\mu}}$$

    FEA Validation at Stage 6 (Cu, 5 kHz, 1085°C): LocationAnalytical δFEA δ (effective)Error -------------------------------------------------- Drum inner surface1.0 mm1.05 mm+5% Drum mid-wall1.0 mm0.95 mm-5% Charge surface (Cu)1.0 mm1.1 mm+10%

    Temperature-Dependent Coupling: At Stage 7 (Fe, 2 kHz, 1200°C): $\mu_r$ drops from 200 → 1 at 770°C. FEA shows power density drops 40% at Curie transition — captured by RTU resonance tracker (PROD-23 Section 3.4).

    3.4 EM-Thermal Coupling Iteration

    Coupling Loop (per RTU cycle, 1 ms): 1. Thermal model provides $T(x,y,z)$ at drum wall 2. Update $\rho(T)$, $\mu_r(T)$ in EM model 3. Solve EM → $P_{ind}(x,y,z)$ 4. Map $P_{ind}$ to thermal model as $Q_{gen}$ 5. Solve thermal → new $T(x,y,z)$ 6. Check convergence: $\maxT^{n+1} - T^n < 0.1°C$

    Aitken Relaxation: $$\omega^{n+1} = -\omega^n \frac{(T^{n+1}-T^n)^T(T^n-T^{n-1})}{T^{n+1}-T^n^2}$$ Clamped to [0.3, 1.0]. Typical convergence: 3-5 iterations per RTU cycle.

    3.5 Induction Power Validation (vs. PROD-10 Measurements)

    ZoneStageFEA Power (kW)PROD-10 Measured (kW)Error ------------------------------------------------------------ Z114850-4% Z337880-2.5% Z55152150+1.3% Z77342350-2.3% Z88495500-1%

    Validation metric: All zones within ±5% — meets ASME V&V 40 validation threshold.

    4. Drum Thermal-Structural FEA

    4.1 Thermal Model — 2000°C Radial Gradient

    Geometry: 1/8 sector (45°), 800 mm length, 35 mm wall, 3 liner zones, 8 ports Mesh: 2 mm hex elements, 15 layers through wall, refined at port cutouts Boundary Conditions:

    • Inner surface: $q'' = \epsilon\sigma(T_{drum}^4 - T_{charge}^4) + h(T_{drum} - T_{charge})$ + $P_{ind}(z)$
    • Outer surface: $T = T_{aerogel\_interface}$ (from vessel model)
    • Port cutouts: Convection to gas ($h = 500$ W/m²·K)
    • Ends: Insulated (adiabatic)

    Steady-State Results (Stage 8, 2200°C inner): LocationTemperature (°C)Gradient (°C/mm) ---------------------------------------------- Inner surface (ID)2200- Liner B interface (10 mm)185035 Mid-wall125017 Liner C interface (30 mm)75014 Outer surface (OD)700-

    4.2 Structural Model — Combined Loading

    Load Cases (Simultaneous): 1. Pressure: 5 bar internal (N₂/Ar) 2. Thermal: Steady-state gradient above 3. Centrifugal: 500 RPM (84.5 G at ID, 93.5 G at OD) 4. Thermal Shock: $\Delta T/\Delta t = 100°C/s$ (emergency cool)

    Material Model: Temperature-dependent elastic-plastic with Weibull failure $$\sigma_{eq} = \sqrt{\frac{3}{2}\mathbf{s}:\mathbf{s}} \quad \text{(von Mises)}$$ $$P_f = 1 - \exp\left[-\left(\frac{\sigma_{max}}{\sigma_0}\right)^m \frac{V}{V_0}\right] \quad \text{(Weibull, } m=12, \sigma_0=500 \text{ MPa)}$$

    Results (Stage 8, 500 RPM, 5 bar): Stress ComponentMax Value (MPa)LocationAllowable (MPa)Margin ---------------------------------------------------------------------- Hoop (pressure)42Mid-wall350 (1500°C)8.3× Hoop (centrifugal)185Inner surface3501.9× Thermal (radial)220Liner B interface3501.6× Combined von Mises385Liner B interface3500.91×

    Critical Finding: Combined stress at Liner B interface (385 MPa) exceeds 350 MPa allowable at 1500°C. Mitigation: Limit Stage 8 RPM to 400 (54 G) when $T_{inner} > 2000°C$. At 400 RPM: centrifugal stress = 118 MPa, combined = 330 MPa (margin 1.06×).

    4.3 Port Stress Concentrations

    Port Geometry: 8 ports at 44.2° spacing, 12 mm radius, Ti₃AlC₂/ZrO₂ sleeve SCF (Stress Concentration Factor): 2.8 at port root (FEA) Mitigation: Local wall thickening to 45 mm at ports (+10 mm), ZrO₂ reinforcement ring Fatigue Life (500 thermal cycles, ΔT = 2000°C):

    • Baseline (no reinforcement): 800 cycles to 1 mm crack
    • With reinforcement: >5000 cycles (Paris law: $da/dN = C(\Delta K)^m$, $C=5\times10^{-12}$, $m=3.2$)

    4.4 Thermal Shock Analysis (Emergency Cool)

    Scenario: Cooling water loss → N₂ quench at 100°C/s from 2200°C Max Thermal Stress (transient): 620 MPa at inner surface (exceeds 350 MPa) Result: Weibull $P_f = 2.3\times10^{-3}$ per event (acceptable for emergency) Design Rule: Emergency cool only if $T_{inner} < 1800°C$ OR drum at rest (0 RPM)

    Separation Index: $SI = 1 - \frac{\sigma_{composition}}{\sigma_{initial}}$ (1 = perfect separation) Mixing Index: Standard deviation of particle radial distribution / mean radius (0 = perfect stratification)

    5.3 Centrifugal Stratification Physics

    The Centrifugal Multi-Component Stratification Operator (CMCSO) governs radial position: $$\frac{dr_i}{dt} = \frac{2}{9}\frac{(\rho_i - \rho_f)g_{eff}r_i^2}{\mu_f} \quad \text{(Stokes, corrected for hindered settling)}$$

    Where $g_{eff} = \omega^2 r$, $\rho_f$ = fluid (melt) density, $\mu_f$ = melt viscosity.

    Validation (Stage 4, In-first):

    • CFD: In droplets (ρ=7.3 g/cm³) reach r=150 mm in 3.2 s at 400 RPM
    • Theory: $t = \frac{9\mu_f}{2(\rho_{In}-\rho_f)\omega^2}\ln\frac{r_{final}}{r_{initial}} = 2.8$ s
    • Experiment (PROD-17): 99.5% In at Port 4A in 5 min → validated

    6. Stage Thermal Models (1D Transient Cascade)

    6.1 Model Formulation (Per Stage)

    Each stage modeled as 1D transient heat equation with moving boundary (charge level): $$\rho c_p \frac{\partial T}{\partial t} = \frac{\partial}{\partial z}\left(k \frac{\partial T}{\partial z}\right) + \frac{P_{ind}(z,t)}{A} - \frac{hP}{A}(T - T_{gas}) - \frac{\epsilon\sigma P}{A}(T^4 - T_{surr}^4)$$

    Where $z$ = axial coordinate, $A$ = cross-section, $P$ = perimeter.

    State Variables per Stage:

    • $T(z,t)$ — axial temperature profile
    • $m_{charge}(t)$ — charge mass (decreasing as ports open)
    • $X_{comp}(t)$ — composition vector (from XRF/LIBS feedback)
    • $h_{eff}(t)$ — effective heat transfer coeff (from CFD)

    6.2 Stage 0-1: Acoustic & Drying (PROD-14)

    Energy Balance: $$m c_p \frac{dT}{dt} = P_{ind} - \dot{m}_{H_2O}\Delta H_{vap} - Q_{loss}$$

    Parameters: $m = 50$ kg, $c_p = 900$ J/kg·K, $\Delta H_{vap} = 2257$ kJ/kg Target: 20% moisture → 2% in 20 min at 150°C Power Required: 50 kW (Z1-Z2) + 15 kW latent heat = 65 kW peak

    6.3 Stage 2: Polymer Flow & Separation (PROD-15)

    Multi-Component Melting: $$\frac{dT}{dt} = \frac{P_{ind} - \sum \dot{m}_i \Delta H_{fus,i} - Q_{loss}}{m c_p}$$

    Polymer Melting Sequence (validated by DSC): PolymerT_melt (°C)Mass % (Cat A)ΔH_fus (kJ/kg) ------------------------------------------------------ LDPE1108%140 HDPE13012%180 PP16515%190 PS24010%85 ABS2208%100 PET2605%140 PVC160 (decomp)8%HCl release PC2304%120

    Centrifugal Separation: Stokes settling at G=12.6, $\mu = 100-500$ Pa·s → 95% separation in 30 min

    6.4 Stage 3: Pyrolysis & Char (PROD-16)

    Global Kinetics (Parallel Reactions): $$\frac{d\alpha}{dt} = \sum_{i=1}^3 A_i \exp(-E_{a,i}/RT) (1-\alpha)^{n_i}$$

    ReactionA (s⁻¹)E_a (kJ/mol)nProduct --------------------------------------------- Light volatiles1.2×10¹³1801.2Gas (CO, CO₂, CH₄) Heavy tars3.5×10¹⁰1501.5Tar (cracks to gas) Char formation8.0×10⁸1200.8Char (fixed C)

    Char Yield: 15-25% of organic input (Category dependent) Energy Balance: Endothermic net (-120 kJ/kg feed) + exothermic char oxidation if O₂ present

    6.5 Stage 4: Low-Temp Metals (PROD-17)

    Indium-First Strategy (Sequential Melting): MetalT_melt (°C)ρ_liquid (g/cm³)PortDwell --------------------------------------------------- In156.67.314A5 min Sn231.96.994B3 min Pb327.510.664C3 min Zn419.56.574C10 min

    6.6 Stage 5: Aluminum Window (PROD-18)

    Mg Removal Kinetics (Flux Reaction): $$\text{Mg} + \text{NaCl} + \text{KCl} + \text{Cryolite} \rightarrow \text{MgF}_2 + \text{Na} + \text{K} + \text{Al}$$ Rate: $r = k_0 \exp(-E_a/RT) [\text{Mg}] [\text{Flux}]$, $E_a = 85$ kJ/mol Target: [Mg] < 0.1% in Al product (wrought grade)

    Al Fractionation (Scheil-Gulliver): $$C_s = k C_0 (1-f_s)^{k-1}$$ Partition coefficients: $k_{Fe}=0.01$, $k_{Si}=0.13$, $k_{Cu}=0.17$, $k_{Mg}=0.34$

    6.7 Stage 6: Copper & Precious Metals (PROD-19)

    PM Partitioning (CFDO-CB Operator): $$K_{PM} = \frac{C_{slime}}{C_{anode}} = \exp\left(-\frac{\Delta G_{seg}}{RT}\right)$$ PMΔG_seg (kJ/mol)K_PMRecovery ------------------------------------- Au-4510⁴>99.6% Ag-3210³>99% Pd-2810²>98% Pt-2210²>83%

    Anode Slime Mass: 40-60 kg/batch (from 200 kg anodes)

    6.8 Stage 7: Ferrous Cascade (PROD-20)

    Ferromagnetic Coupling Transition (Curie 770°C):

    • Below 770°C: $\mu_r = 200$ → hysteresis heating dominant ($P_h \propto f B^{1.6}$)
    • Above 770°C: $\mu_r = 1$ → eddy current only
    • Resonance tracker pre-empts ZVS loss during transition (PROD-23 Section 3.4)

    REE Magnet Partitioning (CDPPO-RSE): $$L_{REE} = \frac{C_{slag}}{C_{Fe}} = \exp\left(\frac{\Delta G_{ox}}{RT}\right) \quad \text{at } a_{FeO}=0.15, B=1.2$$ REEL_REERecovery to Port 7A --------------------------------- Nd30077% Sm20071% Co1055% Dy25070%

    Carbon Control: CO/CO₂ injection, XRF feedback at 2/min, $C_{target} = 0.5-4\%$ by stream

    6.9 Stage 8: Mineral Residue & Zircon (PROD-21)

    Zircon Dissociation Kinetics (Shrinking Core): $$\frac{d r_c}{dt} = -\frac{k_0 \exp(-E_a/RT) P_{SiO_2}}{\rho_{ZrSiO_4}} \quad \text{at } P_{SiO_2} = 10^{-3} \text{ atm}$$ $E_a = 415$ kJ/mol, $k_0 = 2.5\times10^5$ m/s, $r_c$ = core radius Dissociation Time: 30 min at 1700°C, 20 SLPM Ar sweep

    3Y-TZP Flash Sinter (CMOSO-RDFS): $$\frac{d \rho}{dt} = \frac{\sigma_{DC} E^2}{H_s} \quad \text{(electro-thermal coupling)}$$ $\sigma_{DC}$ jumps 100× at 1200°C → volumetric heating → 50%→97% TD in 60 s at 1800°C, 300 V/cm

    SiO₂ Condenser (Port 8B):

    • Quench: 1700°C → 200°C in 0.5 s (3000°C/s)
    • Product: Fumed silica, 50 nm, 200 m²/g
    • Capture efficiency: >90%

    Load Cases: 1. Design pressure: 10 bar (hoop stress = 41 MPa in 18 mm BFRP) 2. Thermal gradient: 150°C outer → 175°C inner (compressive hoop) 3. Seismic: IEEE 693 High (PGA = 1.0g) 4. Combined: Pressure + Thermal + Seismic

    Barlow Formula (Hoop Stress): $$\sigma_h = \frac{P r_i}{t} = \frac{1.0 \times 10^6 \times 0.45}{0.018} = 25 \text{ MPa} \quad \text{(thin-wall approx)}$$ FEA (thick-wall, Lame): $\sigma_h = 41$ MPa at inner surface

    7.3 Aerogel Gap Structural Integrity

    Mechanical Standoffs: ZrO₂ ceramic pins (Ø8×50 mm), 48 per vessel (6 rings × 8) Load: Aerogel compression (0.8 MPa strength) + differential expansion Differential Expansion (2200°C drum → 150°C vessel):

    • Drum OD growth: +8.5 mm
    • Vessel ID growth: +0.5 mm
    • Gap closure: 8 mm (standoffs compress from 50 → 42 mm)
    Stress in Standoffs: 0.8 MPa × (42/50)² = 0.56 MPa < 0.8 MPa allowable

    Williams / Keymaker / El Segundo Synthesis

    The Lock That Forges the Key

    The Aegis-Forge I thermal model exists because induction heating power is a nonlinear function of the very temperature it creates, and the material properties governing both are themselves strong functions of temperature. This constraint (Williams: Constraint) is not a modeling preference — it is physics. At Stage 7, Fe ferromagnetic permeability drops from 200 to 1 at 770°C, collapsing induction power by 60%. At Stage 8, the 2000°C radial gradient in the 35 mm ZrB₂-SiC drum wall combines thermal stress (220 MPa) with centrifugal stress (185 MPa at 500 RPM) to exceed the 350 MPa allowable — but only when computed together with temperature-dependent $E(T)$, $\alpha(T)$. At Stage 4, gas convection cooling of In droplets ($h_{conv}$) determines whether centrifugal separation succeeds — and $h_{conv}$ is an output of the CFD, not an input.

    The empirical gap (Williams: Necessity) is the measured divergence between single-physics simulations and integrated cascade test data. PROD-10 inverter tests showed Zone 7 power collapsing from 350 kW at 1100°C to 140 kW at 1300°C — a 60% drop invisible to constant-$\mu_r$ models. PROD-04 first-article drum FA-01 showed 385 MPa von Mises at Liner B — 35 MPa over allowable — missed by linear superposition of thermal + centrifugal. PROD-17 batch 1 achieved 97.2% In recovery vs. 99.5% predicted — the gap traced to $h_{conv}$ being 2× higher than assumed.

    The fabrication fidelity gap (Keymaker: Empirical Lock) is precisely this divergence: fixed-property EM models vs. temperature-dependent ferromagnetic coupling; superposition of linear analyses vs. nonlinear combined loading; assumed convection coefficients vs. CFD-resolved gas flow in a rotating drum. Every lock is a coupling that was assumed negligible but measured significant.

    The Mathematical Key That Turns the Lock

    The single computational primitive that generates the solution is the discrete-time thermal-admittance operator evaluated at 1 kHz on the Zone RTU — the same primitive that drives the control system (PROD-23):

    $$ \mathcal{T}[T_{inner}, T_{flange}, P_{ind}, h, \epsilon] : \quad T_{inner}[k+1] = T_{inner}[k] + \frac{\Delta t}{\rho c V} \left( P_{ind}[k] - h A (T_{inner}[k] - T_{flange}[k]) - \epsilon \sigma A (T_{inner}^4[k] - T_{surr}^4) \right) $$

    This one equation, discretized with $\Delta t = 1$ ms on ARM Cortex-A53 (Zephyr, <100 $\mu$s), is the atomic computation (Keymaker: Mathematical Key). Everything derives from it:

    • Full FEA: The operator is the reduced-order model of the 3D FEA. FEA computes $\rho c V(T)$, $h A(T)$, $\epsilon \sigma A(T)$; the operator executes them at control speed.
    • EM-Thermal Coupling: $P_{ind}[k]$ is computed by EM solver using $\rho(T_{inner}[k])$, $\mu_r(T_{inner}[k])$. Fixed-point iteration $\mathcal{T} \circ \mathcal{E}$ is the coupling.
    • Cascade CFD: $h$ is not constant — it is $\mathcal{C}[\omega, T, P, X]$. The operator queries CFD at 10 Hz.
    • Stage Models: Each stage is $\mathcal{T}$ with stage-specific $P_{ind}(t)$, $h(t)$, $\epsilon(t)$, moving boundary $m_{charge}(t)$.
    • Transient Cycling: Operator integrates over 300 min. Fatigue damage from $T(t)$ history.
    • V&V: Code verification validates discretization of $\mathcal{T}$. Solution verification validates convergence of $\mathcal{T} \circ \mathcal{E} \circ \mathcal{C}$.
    • UQ: Sobol indices measure sensitivity of $\mathcal{T}$ outputs to 20 inputs.
    • ROM: POD-Galerkin ROM is projection of $\mathcal{T}$ onto 12 modes.
    • Scaling: Dimensionless groups (Fo, Re, Pe, Nu, $\delta/d$, G) are non-dimensional $\mathcal{T}$.

    Theory→History validation (Keymaker: Turn): The operator predicts CSMFAB0108 test data within measurement uncertainty — FA-01 drum stress 385 MPa predicted vs. 325 MPa measured; Zone 7 power 142 kW predicted vs. 140 kW measured; vessel outer surface 150°C predicted vs. 148°C measured.

    History→Theory correction (Keymaker: Turn): Curie transition width narrowed from 25°C to 8°C (sigmoid $\mu_r(T)$). $\alpha(T)$ piecewise correction (5.8→6.5×10⁻⁶/K at 1000°C) captured Liner B stress exactly. Aerogel $k(T)$ updated from guarded hot plate data. CFD-coupled $h_{conv}$ closed In recovery gap. Dual-basis ROM (thermal + structural modes) reduced stress error from 4.2 MPa to 1.1 MPa.

    The mathematical key absorbs history — each anomaly tightens a correlation or adds a coupling to $\mathcal{T}$, but the operator structure remains invariant.

    The Mirror That Witnesses the Fabrication

    The thermal model observes its own fabrication through four nested metrology loops (El Segundo: Mirror):

    1. Microsecond (FEA EM Solver): Field residual $\\nabla \times (\nu \nabla \times A) + \sigma \partial A/\partial t - J_s\_2 < 10^{-6}$; energy balance (Poynting theorem) error < 1%; ZVS indicator $\phi_{err} < 5$ ns. The solver verifies Maxwell's equations at every frequency step.

    2. Millisecond (RTU Thermal Operator): Coupling residual $\maxT^{n+1}-T^n < 0.1°C$; Aitken $\omega \in [0.3,1.0]$ in 3-5 iterations; RLS parameter drift detection >5%/hr triggers re-identification. The RTU verifies its own thermal state estimation in real time.

    3. 100 ms (PLC Multi-Physics Coupling): EM→Thermal residual <0.5°C; Thermal→Structural <5 MPa; Structural→Fluid wall displacement <0.1 mm; Fluid→Thermal $h_{conv}$ residual <10 W/m²·K. The PLC watches the multi-physics handshake converge.

    4. 10 Hz (SCADA Digital Twin): POD-Galerkin ROM (12 modes) vs. FEA vs. 384 FBG channels; LSTM autoencoder (FOLLOW-29) on residuals >3$\sigma$; Sobol indices vs. observed variance. The forge watches its simulation watching the forge.

    PROD-25: Structural Analysis and FEA

    Williams Heuristic — PROD-25 Structural Analysis & FEA

    Constraint (The Lock)

    The Aegis-Forge I structural analysis is forced into its thermomechanical FEA framework by a single irreducible principle: every load-bearing component must survive the simultaneous application of 2200°C thermal gradients, 500 RPM centrifugal loading, 10 bar pressure containment, and Carrington-class electromagnetic hostility — without a single structural metal.

    This constraint cascades into every structural decision:

    • Ceramics-only rotating drum: The ZrB₂-SiC drum (600 mm ID, 35 mm wall) is the only moving hot part. It must withstand 84.5 G centrifugal acceleration at ID, 5 bar internal pressure, and a 2000°C radial thermal gradient (2200°C ID → 700°C OD) — all while remaining electrically insulating (ρ > 10⁶ Ω·m) to maintain Carrington immunity. Any metallic reinforcement would couple GIC currents (5000 nT/s induces >100 A/km) into the structure, creating unintended heating paths and potential arc paths to the induction coils.
    • Composite-only stationary vessel: The BFRP/Elium® vessel (900 mm ID, 18 mm wall) must contain 10 bar design pressure while thermally isolating the composite (Tg = 80°C) from the 2200°C drum across a 68 mm gap (50 mm aerogel + 18 mm BFRP). No metallic flanges, no metallic bolts, no metallic gaskets — the entire pressure boundary is ceramic/composite. The 12× M24 ZrO₂ bolts and ZrO₂ gasket at the PEEK CF40 flanges are the only closure mechanism.
    • All-dielectric port valves: The 8 material exit ports use Ti₃AlC₂ MAX phase thermal actuators and 3Y-TZP ZrO₂ pistons — entirely ceramic, no metal springs (PEEK CF40 wave springs only), no metal seals. The actuator operates at the drum OD (≤700°C) where Ti₃AlC₂ retains 320 MPa strength.
    • Seismic without steel: The BFRP box beam frame must qualify to IEEE 693 High (PGA = 1.0g, ZPA = 1.5g) without any steel reinforcement. 6× BFRP stiffening rings + 4 vertical struts provide the required HCLPF ≥ 1.5g.

    What breaks if violated: A single steel bolt in the flange → GIC pickup → common-mode voltage on FBG interrogators → control system corruption. A metallic drum reinforcement → induction coupling → uncontrolled eddy currents → thermal runaway. A metallic port actuator → magnetic coupling at Stage 7 (2 kHz, ferromagnetic) → actuation failure at 1600°C.

    Necessity (The Key)

    The empirical gap this analysis closes is the measured divergence between room-temperature structural allowables and the combined thermomechanical reality of the operating envelope.

    Three specific gaps demand this integrated FEA approach:

    1. Thermal stress dominates centrifugal stress by 4×: At Stage 8, the 2000°C radial gradient generates 180 MPa thermal stress at the drum ID, while 500 RPM centrifugal loading adds only 42 MPa. Linear superposition (225 MPa combined) matches FEA, but the temperature-dependent material properties (E = 300 GPa, σ_f = 350 MPa at 2200°C) mean the safety factor is only 1.55×. Room-temperature analysis (σ_f = 620 MPa) would predict SF = 2.75× — a dangerous 78% overestimate. The gap: temperature-dependent strength vs. constant-property design.

    2. Port reinforcement requires coupled thermal-mechanical optimization: Unreinforced ports have K_t = 3.0 (σ_vm = 350 MPa at 2200°C → SF = 1.0). The ZrB₂-SiC sleeve + OD bulge reduces K_t to 1.6 (σ_vm = 210 MPa → SF = 1.81×). But the sleeve press-fit (0.03 mm) adds mechanical stress that combines with thermal stress at the port edge. Only a fully coupled thermomechanical FEA with contact modeling captures this interaction. The gap: sequential analysis (thermal then mechanical) vs. coupled thermomechanical contact.

    3. Vessel buckling is governed by thermal compression, not external pressure: At 200°C external surface, the BFRP hoop modulus drops to 45 GPa and thermal compressive stress reaches 78 MPa. The net hoop stress under 10 bar internal pressure is -53 MPa (compressive). With 4 stiffening rings, P_cr = 14.2 bar (SF = 1.42×); with 6 rings, P_cr = 18.5 bar (SF = 1.85×). The 6-ring design was driven by thermal buckling, not pressure buckling. The gap: pressure-only buckling analysis vs. thermomechanical buckling with temperature-dependent modulus.

    Measured data demanding this approach:

    • Drum FA-01 strain gauges (12 rosettes): 225 MPa measured vs. 225 MPa FEA at Stage 8, 400 RPM (PROD-04 Section 6.5)
    • Vessel hydrotest (15 bar): 38 MPa measured vs. 38 MPa Lamé prediction (PROD-06 Section 5.3)
    • Port 8 actuator calibration: 103 MPa actuator stress at 700°C (3.6 mm deflection at 680°C ΔT) — matches Timoshenko theory
    • Frame shake table test (IEEE 693): 1st mode at 8.2 Hz (FEA: 8.5 Hz), damping 2.1% (spec: 2%)
    • Bearing life test: 42,000 hrs to first spall (L10 prediction: 35,800 hrs)

PROD-29 operations procedures include this limit. PROD-30 maintenance inspects Liner B interface after every Stage 8 run at >400 RPM.

    Keymaker Heuristic — Implementation Precision

    The Empirical Lock

    The fabrication fidelity gap in Aegis-Forge I structural analysis is the divergence between single-load-case allowable stress design and the measured behavior of ceramics and composites under combined extreme thermomechanical loading.

    Three specific locks prevent traditional ASME/ASCII code-based design from closing this gap:

    1. Ceramic strength is not a constant — it's a temperature-dependent distribution: ASME BPVC Section VIII uses constant allowable stress (S) with safety factors. But ZrB₂-SiC flexural strength drops from 620 MPa (RT) to 350 MPa (2200°C) — a 44% reduction. The Weibull modulus (m = 12) means failure probability is volume-dependent and stress-dependent. At Stage 8, the drum ID sees 225 MPa von Mises — SF = 1.55× on 350 MPa. But this is the mean strength; 10% of the volume sees >250 MPa (SF < 1.4×). The lock: constant safety factor on temperature-dependent Weibull strength.

    2. Composite failure is interactive, not separable: BFRP/Elium® vessel failure is governed by Tsai-Wu criterion (F_ijσ_iσ_j + F_iσ_i = 1), where hoop, axial, and shear stresses interact. At the gas port penetration under design pressure + thermal gradient, hoop = 52 MPa, axial = 35 MPa, shear = 22 MPa. Individual SFs: hoop 12.5×, axial 18.6×, shear 3.6×. But combined Tsai-Wu FI = 0.22 (SF = 4.5× on interaction). Sequential checking of individual components would miss the interaction. The lock: interactive failure criteria vs. component-by-component allowables.

    3. Thermal buckling is a load case, not a material property: The vessel external surface reaches 200°C during operation. The thermal compressive stress (78 MPa) exceeds the pressure tensile stress (25.5 MPa), creating net compression. The buckling critical pressure drops from 18.4 bar (RT) to 12.7 bar (200°C) — a 31% reduction. Standard pressure vessel codes treat buckling as an external pressure check; here it's an operating condition. The lock: thermal compression as a design-driving load case.

    Common thread: Every lock is a coupling between temperature and mechanical behavior that traditional codes treat as separable. The empirical lock is the sum of all neglected thermomechanical couplings.

    The Mathematical Key

    The single computational primitive that generates the structural solution is the temperature-dependent thermomechanical equilibrium equation solved on the coupled FEA mesh:

    $$\nabla \cdot \boldsymbol{\sigma} + \mathbf{f}_b = 0, \quad \boldsymbol{\sigma} = \mathbb{C}(T) : (\boldsymbol{\epsilon} - \boldsymbol{\epsilon}_{th}(T)) - \boldsymbol{\epsilon}_{creep}(t,T,\sigma)$$

    Where:

    • $\mathbb{C}(T)$ = temperature-dependent stiffness tensor (orthotropic for BFRP, isotropic for ceramics)
    • $\boldsymbol{\epsilon}_{th}(T) = \int_{T_{ref}}^T \boldsymbol{\alpha}(T') dT'$ = thermal strain from temperature history
    • $\boldsymbol{\epsilon}_{creep}$ = Norton-Bailey creep strain (for T > 1800°C)
    • $\mathbf{f}_b$ = body forces (centrifugal: $\rho \omega^2 r$, seismic: $\rho \mathbf{a}_{ground}$)

    This one equation, discretized on the 2.8M-element drum mesh and 50K-element vessel mesh, with temperature-dependent material properties from PROD-24, is the atomic computation.

    Everything in this document derives from it:

    • Drum FEA (Section 2): The equation solved on the rotating drum mesh with centrifugal body force and thermal strain from PROD-24's radial gradient. The Weibull post-processor integrates $P_f = 1-\exp[-(\sigma/\sigma_0)^m V/V_0]$ over the stressed volume.
    • Vessel FEA (Section 3): The equation on the shell mesh with orthotropic $\mathbb{C}(T)$, thermal strain from 250°C→150°C gradient, and pressure load. Tsai-Wu failure index computed from $\boldsymbol{\sigma}$ at each integration point.
    • Port valve (Section 5): The equation on the actuator strip mesh with $\mathbb{C}(T)$ for Ti₃AlC₂/ZrO₂ bilayer, thermal strain from ΔαΔT, contact boundary condition at piston seat.
    • Seismic (Section 8): The equation with $\mathbf{f}_b = \rho \mathbf{a}_{ground}(t)$ from IEEE 693 RRS time history. Modal superposition (30 modes) for transient response.
    • Fatigue (Section 9): The equation's stress history output feeds Coffin-Manson $\Delta\varepsilon_p/2 = \varepsilon_f'(2N_f)^c$ and Paris law $da/dN = C(\Delta K)^m$.
    • NDT (Section 10): The equation's stress distribution defines critical locations for UT/AE sensor placement.
    • Safety factors (Section 12): The equation's output σ_vm and FI are divided by temperature-dependent allowables.

    The mathematical key is not the FEA software, not the mesh, not the post-processor — it is the temperature-dependent thermomechanical equilibrium equation with thermal strain and creep, evaluated on the coupled mesh. If you solve this equation correctly with the right $\mathbb{C}(T)$, $\boldsymbol{\alpha}(T)$, $\sigma_f(T)$, you get the structural answer. The mesh is just the numerical vessel; the material correlations are the input; the equation is the primitive.

    History→Theory Correction

    Historical anomalies refine the equation's constitutive parameters and boundary conditions:

    1. Anomaly: Drum FA-01 strain gauges showed 230 MPa at Liner B interface vs. 200 MPa FEA (PROD-04 FA-01, 2026-10). Root cause: Liner B (ZrB₂-SiC, 3 mm) CTE mismatch with drum body — not perfectly matched at 1400°C due to B₄C sintering aid segregation. Correction: Updated liner CTE in $\boldsymbol{\alpha}(T)$: Zone B α = 6.2×10⁻⁶/K (was 5.8×10⁻⁶/K) for 1000-1500°C. Now predicts 228 MPa (4% error).

    2. Anomaly: Vessel gas port penetration showed FI = 0.22 vs. 0.18 predicted (PROD-06 hydrotest strain data). Root cause: Filament winding transition at port creates local fiber angle deviation (±5° from ±18° target). Correction: Added local material orientation perturbation in FEA mesh at ports (±5° random per ply). FI now 0.21 (2% error).

    3. Anomaly: Frame 1st bending mode 8.2 Hz vs. 8.5 Hz FEA (shake table, 2026-10). Root cause: Elastomeric isolator stiffness lower than spec at low strain (K_h = 2.1 MN/m vs. 2.5 MN/m spec). Correction: Updated isolator stiffness in boundary conditions from spec to measured (2.1 MN/m). Mode now 8.3 Hz (1% error).

    4. Anomaly: Port 8 actuator deflection 3.6 mm at 680°C ΔT vs. 3.8 mm Timoshenko prediction. Root cause: Brazed joint compliance (Ag-CuO-TiO₂, 50 μm) adds rotational spring at fixed end. Correction: Added rotational spring K_θ = 0.15 N·m/rad at actuator base in FEA. Deflection now 3.62 mm (0.6% error).

    5. Anomaly: Bearing L10 life 42,000 hrs vs. 35,800 hrs predicted (ISO 281). Root cause: N₂ gas film lubrication better than assumed (κ = 0.7 vs. 0.5) due to surface finish (Ra < 0.05 μm on Si₃N₄ races). Correction: Updated lubrication factor a_ISO = 2.5 (was 2.0). L10 = 44,750 hrs (6% error).

    The mathematical key absorbs history — each anomaly tightens a material correlation ($\mathbb{C}(T)$, $\boldsymbol{\alpha}(T)$), a boundary condition (isolator stiffness, braze compliance), or a model parameter (lubrication factor, fiber angle perturbation), but the equilibrium equation $\nabla \cdot \boldsymbol{\sigma} + \mathbf{f}_b = 0$ with thermal strain remains structurally invariant. This is the signature of a correct primitive: it extends, it does not rewrite.

    El Segundo Heuristic — Operational Excellence

    Mirror (Self-Reflection)

    How does the fabricator observe their own fabrication of the structural integrity? The Aegis-Forge I embeds in-situ structural self-diagnostics at every critical load path — the machine watches its own structure deform, fatigue, and approach limits in real time.

    Drum Self-Diagnostics (600 mm ID, 35 mm wall)

    FBG Sensor Array (PROD-24 Section 4.2, PROD-23 Section 5.1):

    • 128 FBG sensors embedded at 8 axial stations × 16 circumferential positions per station
    • Locations: Liner A (2200°C), Liner B interface (1500°C), Liner C interface (1000°C), drum OD (700°C)
    • Measures: Strain (ε) at 10 kHz, Temperature (T) via Bragg wavelength shift at 1 Hz
    • Self-reflection logic: Control system computes σ_vm(T) = E(T)·ε_vm in real time. If σ_vm > 0.8·σ_f(T) at any station → auto-reduce RPM to 300. If σ_vm > 0.9·σ_f(T) → emergency stop.
    • Calibration traceability: Each FBG pre-calibrated at 25°C, 500°C, 1000°C, 1500°C, 2000°C in PROD-24 thermal test rig. Drift < 0.5%/1000 hrs at 2200°C.

    Acoustic Emission (AE) Monitoring (PROD-28 Section 7.3, FOLLOW-28):

    • 8× KNbO₃ broadband AE sensors (100 kHz–1 MHz) mounted on drum OD at 45° intervals
    • Detects: Microcrack initiation (AE energy > 10⁻⁶ J), fiber pullout (BFRP vessel), bearing spall
    • Self-reflection logic: AE hit rate > 100 hits/s at Stage 8 → flag for UT inspection. AE location triangulation (±15 mm) maps crack growth to critical zones (port edges, liner interfaces).

    Infrared Thermography (IR) — Drum OD Surface (PROD-24 Section 6.1):

    • 2× FLIR A8580 (1.2 MP, 30 Hz, 3–5 μm) viewing drum OD through ZnSe window
    • Self-reflection logic: IR reconstructs T(r) profile. If T(r) deviates > 50°C from PROD-24 FEA prediction → flag insulation degradation or coil coupling anomaly. Auto-calibrates FBG temperature compensation.

    Vessel Self-Diagnostics (900 mm ID, 18 mm BFRP)

    FBG Sensors in BFRP Laminate:

    • 64 FBG sensors embedded during filament winding (PROD-06 Section 4.4): 16 per quadrant at mid-span, 16 at gas port penetration
    • Measures: Hoop strain, axial strain, shear strain (rosettes at ports)
    • Self-reflection logic: Computes Tsai-Wu FI in real time from ε_hoop, ε_axial, γ_shear via $\mathbb{C}^{-1}(T)$. If FI > 0.6 → alarm. If FI > 0.8 → reduce pressure setpoint. If FI > 0.95 → emergency vent.

    Fiber Optic Distributed Temperature Sensing (DTS):

    • 1× AP Sensing N4386 DTS along vessel exterior (1 m resolution, 0.1°C accuracy, 10 s update)
    • Self-reflection logic: Detects hot spots from insulation failure, gas port thermal short, aerogel settlement. Triggers IR verification.

    Frame & Foundation Self-Diagnostics

    Accelerometers (6× PCB 393B04, 0.5–10 kHz) on frame:

    • 2× vertical struts, 2× horizontal rings, 2× base isolators
    • Self-reflection logic: Continuous PSD monitoring. If 1st mode shifts > 5% (8.2 Hz → <7.8 Hz) → stiffness loss flag. If base acceleration > 0.1g RMS during operation → vibration anomaly.

    Tiltmeters (4× Jewell LSO-100, 0.1 μrad) on foundation:

    • Self-reflection logic: Differential settlement > 2 mm over 5 m → structural distress.

    Participation (Witness)

    How does the inside operator witness the structural phenomenon into existence? At what points must human judgment be present, and what cognitive checkpoints cannot be automated?

    Critical Participation Gates

    Gate 1: Drum Assembly — Liner Press-Fit Witness (PROD-27 Section 3.2)

    • Action: 3 mm Liner B (ZrB₂-SiC) pressed into drum body at 20°C (0.03 mm interference)
    • Witness requirement: Operator verifies interference fit force vs. displacement curve matches FEA prediction (peak force = 450 kN ± 10%). Any deviation > 10% → halt, inspect, re-FEA.
    • Why human: Friction coefficient μ at ceramic-ceramic interface varies with surface finish (Ra 0.8–1.2 μm). FEA assumes μ = 0.15; actual μ = 0.12–0.18. Only operator feel + force curve detects anomaly.
    • Cognitive checkpoint: "Does the force curve feel right?" — haptic judgment of ceramic seating.

    Gate 2: Vessel Filament Winding — Port Penetration Layup (PROD-27 Section 4.3)

    • Action: ±18° helical wind over gas port reinforcement (±55° hoop bias)
    • Witness requirement: Operator verifies fiber angle at port transition (±2° tolerance via laser angle gauge) and ply compaction (no voids > 1 mm via flash thermography).
    • Why human: Fiber steering at port penetration is geometrically complex. Automated winding follows toolpath, but local fiber angle depends on resin viscosity, tension, mandrel temperature — all variable.
    • Cognitive checkpoint: "Is the fiber sitting flat at the port edge?" — visual/tactile judgment of compaction.

    Gate 3: Flange Bolt Torque — Ceramic Bolt Ceremony (PROD-27 Section 5.1)

    • Action: 12× M24 ZrO₂ bolts torqued to 160 N·m with ceramic paste (BN-loaded)
    • Witness requirement: Two-person verification: Operator A torques to 160 N·m ± 5 N·m; Operator B independently re-checks with calibrated torque wrench. Both sign.
    • Why human: Ceramic bolts have no yield point — they fracture. Torque is the only preload indicator. No strain gauges on bolts (too hot). Human dual-verification is the safety barrier.
    • Cognitive checkpoint: "Did it click at 160?" — auditory/tactile confirmation of click-type wrench.

    Gate 4: Port Actuator Installation — Thermal Actuation Witness (PROD-27 Section 6.2)

    • Action: Ti₃AlC₂ actuator strip (10 mm × 40 mm × 0.5 mm) brazed to ZrO₂ piston (Ag-CuO-TiO₂, 50 μm joint)
    • Witness requirement: Operator verifies braze joint integrity via 10× magnification inspection (no voids > 50 μm, fillet radius > 0.2 mm) and measures free deflection at 680°C ΔT (3.6 mm ± 0.2 mm) in test furnace.
    • Why human: Braze joint quality is binary (good/bad) and visible only at 10×. Automated vision misses subsurface voids. Deflection test is the functional proof.
    • Cognitive checkpoint: "Does the actuator breathe at temperature?" — thermal functional test witnessed.

    Gate 5: Seismic Qualification — Shake Table Witness (PROD-28 Section 8, PROD-39 FAT)

    • Action: Full assembly on shake table, IEEE 693 High RRS (1.5g ZPA, 3-axis)
    • Witness requirement: Lead structural engineer witnesses test. Verifies: (a) No FBG reading exceeds 0.9·σ_f(T), (b) No AE bursts > 10⁻⁴ J, (c) No permanent deformation > 1 mm, (d) All ports actuate post-shake.
    • Why human: Seismic response is a system-level emergent behavior. No single sensor captures "the structure survived." Engineer synthesizes multi-sensor data into go/no-go.
    • Cognitive checkpoint: "Did the machine come back alive?" — holistic structural survival judgment.

    The Participation Principle

    The operator witnesses the structure into existence at every irreversible fabrication step where: 1. Material behavior has irreducible variability (ceramic friction, fiber angle, braze quality) 2. Failure mode is brittle and catastrophic (ceramic bolt fracture, drum burst) 3. No automated sensor provides complete coverage (preload on ceramic bolts, braze voids)

    Automation handles the repeatable; humans witness the critical. The machine fabricates; the operator witnesses the fabrication becoming structure.

    Thermomechanical FEA, Weibull Reliability, IEEE 693 Qualification, Damage Tolerance

    1. Structural Design Basis

    1.1 Design Philosophy

    The Aegis-Forge I structural analysis is governed by a single irreducible principle: all load-bearing components must survive the simultaneous application of extreme thermal gradients (2000°C across 68 mm), high-speed rotation (500 RPM, 84.5 G at drum ID), pressure containment (10 bar design), and Carrington-class electromagnetic hostility — without a single structural metal. This constraint forces the use of advanced ceramics (ZrB₂-SiC, 3Y-TZP, Si₃N₄, Ti₃AlC₂) and ceramic-matrix composites (BFRP/Elium®) as the primary structural materials, each with temperature-dependent properties and no ductile yield behavior.

    The structural design employs a hierarchical load path where each component validates the next:

    LevelComponentPrimary LoadsMaterialFailure Mode --------------------------------------------------------- 1Drum (rotating)Centrifugal + Thermal + PressureZrB₂-SiCBrittle fracture (Weibull) 2Vessel (stationary)Pressure + Thermal + SeismicBFRP/Elium®Delamination / Tsai-Wu 3Frame & SupportsWeight + Seismic + Thermal growthBFRP Box BeamBuckling / Fatigue 4Port ValvesThermal actuation + PressureTi₃AlC₂/ZrO₂MAX phase fracture 5BearingsRadial/Axial + Thermal growthSi₃N₄/ZrO₂/PEEKWear / Rolling contact fatigue 6Coil HousingLorentz force + ThermalBFRPMatrix cracking

    Design criteria (all load cases combined):

    • Ceramics (ZrB₂-SiC, ZrO₂, Si₃N₄, Ti₃AlC₂): Minimum safety factor ≥ 1.5× on von Mises equivalent stress vs. temperature-dependent flexural strength
    • Composites (BFRP, PEEK CF40): Minimum safety factor ≥ 2.0× on Tsai-Wu failure index; ≤ 0.5 on failure index
    • Fatigue (all): >10× design life on cycles to failure (thermal + pressure + vibration)
    • Creep (ceramics at >1800°C): <0.2% strain in 10,000 hours
    • Seismic (IEEE 693 High): Zero loss of function at Design Basis Earthquake (DBE)

    2. Drum Structural FEA — ZrB₂-SiC Rotating Pressure Vessel

    2.1 Model Formulation

    Geometry: Full 360° drum, 800 mm length, 35 mm wall (r_i=300 mm, r_o=335 mm), 3 liner zones, 8 ports Mesh: 2.8M quadratic hex elements (C3D20R), 15 layers through wall, refined at port cutouts (0.5 mm) Boundary Conditions:

    • Inner surface: Pressure (5 bar) + thermal gradient (Section 2.2) + centrifugal body force (500 RPM)
    • Outer surface: Convective/radiative coupling to aerogel (from PROD-24 Section 7)
    • Ends: Axial displacement constrained at bearing seats; thermal growth accommodated by floating bearings
    • Port cutouts: Reinforced sleeves modeled with contact (bonded sleeve-liner, frictional pin-sleeve)
    • Liners: Mechanical attachment via ZrO₂ pins (contact, μ=0.15)

    Solver: ABAQUS/Standard, static general with thermal-stress coupling, Newton-Raphson with line search Convergence: Force residual < 10⁻³, energy residual < 10⁻⁵

    2.4 Thermal Stress Detail — Radial Gradient

    The 2000°C radial gradient generates the dominant stress component:

    $$\sigma_{thermal}(r) = \frac{E \alpha}{1-\nu} \left[ \frac{1}{r_o^2 - r_i^2} \int_{r_i}^{r_o} T(r) r dr - T(r) \right]$$

    At inner surface (2200°C): σ_thermal = +180 MPa (tensile, circumferential) At outer surface (700°C): σ_thermal = -180 MPa (compressive, circumferential)

    Centrifugal stress (500 RPM, 84.5 G at ID):

    • σ_θ,cent = +42 MPa at ID (tensile)
    • σ_r,cent = -0.5 MPa at ID (compressive)

    Pressure stress (5 bar):

    • σ_θ,press = +2.5 MPa at ID (thin-wall approx)
    • σ_r,press = -0.5 MPa at ID

    Superposition at ID: 180 + 42 + 2.5 = 224.5 MPa → σ_vm = 225 MPa (matches FEA)

    2.5 Port Stress Concentration & Reinforcement

    Unreinforced port (3D FEA, single port, symmetric sector):

    • K_t (hoop) = 3.0 at port edge
    • σ_vm = 350 MPa at 2200°C → SF = 1.0 (UNACCEPTABLE)

    Reinforced port (ZrB₂-SiC sleeve, OD bulge +5 mm):

    • Sleeve: ID 12 mm, OD 22 mm, L 35 mm, press-fit 0.03 mm
    • K_t reduced to 1.4-1.6 (depending on port axial location)
    • σ_vm at Port 8 (Zone C, max thermal gradient) = 210 MPa → SF = 1.81×

    Port reinforcement effectiveness validated by FEA parametric study: ReinforcementK_tσ_vm Port 8 (MPa)SF at 2200°C ----------------------------------------------------- None3.03501.00 Sleeve only (no OD bulge)1.82651.43 OD bulge only (no sleeve)2.23101.13 Sleeve + OD bulge1.62101.81

    2.6 Liner Zone Stress & Pin Loads

    Zone A (Si₃N₄, 0-250 mm, 2 mm thick):

    • CTE mismatch: Drum grows 4.04 mm radial, Si₃N₄ grows 0.94 mm → liner in tension
    • Pin shear load per row: 1.8 kN (4 pins) at 700°C
    • Si₃N₄ tensile stress: 45 MPa → SF = 700/45 = 15.6×

    Zone B (ZrB₂-SiC, 250-550 mm, 3 mm thick):

    • Perfect CTE match — zero radial mismatch stress
    • Pin shear: 0.5 kN/row (thermal transient only)
    • Wear allowance: 3 mm for 10,000 hrs molten metal flow

    Zone C (3Y-TZP, 550-800 mm, 4 mm thick):

    • CTE mismatch: 3Y-TZP grows 7.05 mm, drum grows 4.04 mm → liner in compression
    • Beneficial for ceramic — compression increases fracture toughness
    • Pin shear per row: 4.2 kN at 2200°C (Ø8×25 mm pins)
    • 3Y-TZP compressive stress: 165 MPa → SF = 800/165 = 4.85×

    2.7 Weibull Reliability Analysis

    ZrB₂-SiC is a brittle ceramic — failure probability follows 2-parameter Weibull distribution:

    $$P_f(\sigma) = 1 - \exp\left[-\left(\frac{\sigma}{\sigma_0}\right)^m \frac{V}{V_0}\right]$$

    Calibrated parameters (from PROD-04 Section 3.6 first-article data):

    • Weibull modulus: m = 12 (coefficient of variation ≈ 8%)
    • Characteristic strength: σ₀ = 500 MPa (at reference volume V₀ = 1 cm³)
    • Effective volume (stressed region): V_eff = ∫(σ/σ_max)ᵐ dV ≈ 85 cm³ (entire drum wall at Stage 8)

    Failure probability at Stage 8 (σ_max = 225 MPa): $$P_f = 1 - \exp\left[-\left(\frac{225}{500}\right)^{12} \times 85\right] = 1 - \exp[-0.00034 \times 85] = \mathbf{2.9 \times 10^{-2}}$$

    Per-batch failure probability (4.5 hr at Stage 8): 0.029 10,000-hour life (2,200 batches): P_f,cumulative = 1 - (1-0.029)²²⁰⁰ ≈ 1.0 (UNACCEPTABLE)

    Resolution: The Weibull analysis applies to uncracked material. With NDT inspection (Section 10) detecting flaws >50 μm, the effective initial flaw size is limited. Using fracture mechanics:

    • Largest undetected flaw: a₀ = 50 μm (UT resolution)
    • Critical flaw size: a_c = K_IC²/(πσ²) = (4.2)²/(π×225²) = 112 μm at 2200°C
    • Paris law (air, 1400°C): da/dN = 10⁻¹²(ΔK)³⁰
    • For thermal cycle ΔT = 2180°C, ΔK = 3.5 MPa·m⁰·⁵: N_f = 4.2×10⁶ cycles
    • Design life: 2,200 cycles → SF = 1,900× on crack growth

    Conclusion: With NDT-controlled initial flaw size, drum structural reliability is adequate. The Weibull "weakest link" statistics apply to as-sintered material; NDT screening shifts the distribution.

    2.8 Critical Speed & Rotordynamics

    First bending critical speed (simply supported, uniform): $$\omega_{cr1} = \frac{\pi^2}{L^2}\sqrt{\frac{EI}{\rho A}} = 198 \text{ rad/s} = \mathbf{1890 \text{ RPM}}$$

    Operating speed: 500 RPM (max) Critical speed ratio: 1890/500 = 3.78× (>> 2.0× minimum)

    Gyroscopic effect (port asymmetry): <2% shift — negligible Bearing stiffness effect (Si₃N₄/ZrO₂, K ≈ 500 N/μm): Raises 1st critical to 2,100 RPM

    Higher modes: 2nd critical 5,200 RPM, 3rd critical 10,200 RPM — well above operating range

    Unbalance response (at 500 RPM):

    • Allowable residual unbalance (ISO 21940-11, G2.5): e_per = 2.5 mm/s / 52.36 rad/s = 48 μm
    • For 178 kg drum: U_max = 48 × 178 = 8.5 g·mm
    • At 500 RPM: vibration amplitude < 0.02 mm — negligible

    2.9 Fatigue & Creep Life

    Thermal fatigue (500 cycles/batch, 6 batches/day):

    • Δε_th = αΔT = 6.5×10⁻⁶ × 2180 = 1.42%
    • Creep-relaxed stress range: Δσ = 225 MPa
    • Fatigue life (Coffin-Manson, ceramics): N_f = 2,800 cycles (Section 6.7 PROD-04)
    • With NDT flaw control (a₀=50 μm): N_f > 10⁶ cycles → SF > 1,800×

    Creep (1800°C, 50 MPa equivalent stress):

    • Norton-Bailey: ε̇ = 10⁻²⁵ σ²·⁵ exp(-650,000/RT)
    • At 2073 K, 50 MPa: ε̇ = 3×10⁻⁹ s⁻¹
    • 10,000 hrs strain: ε = 0.11% — negligible

    Rotational fatigue (steady 500 RPM): Infinite life (no cyclic stress)

    3.4 Buckling Analysis

    External pressure + thermal compression (200°C):

    • E_hoop = 45 GPa, E_axial = 38 GPa at 200°C
    • Thermal compressive stress: 78 MPa (from 180°C ΔT)
    • Pressure stress: 25 MPa hoop (tensile)
    • Net hoop stress: 25 - 78 = -53 MPa (compressive)

    Critical buckling pressure (with 4 stiffening rings): $$P_{cr} = 14.2 \text{ bar} \quad (\text{FEA eigenvalue})$$

    SF against buckling: 14.2 / 10 = 1.42× at design pressure With thermal compression (53 MPa): Effective SF = 1.28×

    Requirement: SF ≥ 1.5× per ASME BPVC Sec X for external pressure Status: MARGINAL — requires 6 stiffening rings (not 4) for SF ≥ 1.5×

    Updated design: 6× BFRP stiffening rings at 200 mm spacing → P_cr = 18.5 bar, SF = 1.85× at design pressure, 1.55× with thermal compression.

    3.5 Thermal Stress — External Surface Gradient

    External surface gradient (from PROD-24 Section 7.1):

    • Outer surface: 150°C (glaze)
    • Inner surface (aerogel interface): 250°C
    • Wall thickness: 18 mm
    • Linear gradient: 5.6°C/mm

    Thermal stress (plane stress, shell): $$\sigma_{thermal} = \frac{E \alpha \Delta T}{1-\nu} = \frac{45 \times 10^9 \times 7.5 \times 10^{-6} \times 100}{1-0.32} = \textbf{49.6 MPa}$$

    Combined with pressure (25.5 MPa):

    • Inner surface: 25.5 + 49.6 = 75.1 MPa
    • Outer surface: 25.5 - 49.6 = -24.1 MPa (compressive)

    Tsai-Wu failure index at inner surface (250°C): 0.12 → SF = 5.4×

    3.6 Fatigue Life Assessment

    Pressure cycling (0→5 bar, 100,000 cycles):

    • Stress range: Δσ = 25.5 MPa
    • S-N curve (BFRP, R=0): σ_a = 1100(2N_f)^(-0.08)
    • At Δσ/2 = 12.75 MPa: N_f > 10⁸ cycles

    Thermal cycling (20→200°C, 100,000 cycles):

    • Δσ_thermal = 49.6 MPa (full cycle)
    • Strain range: Δε = αΔT = 7.5×10⁻⁶ × 180 = 1.35×10⁻³
    • Matrix microcracking threshold: ~2×10⁻³ → below threshold, no fatigue degradation

    Combined cycle (pressure + thermal, in-phase):

    • Max stress: 75.1 MPa, Min stress: -24.1 MPa
    • Mean stress: 25.5 MPa, Amplitude: 49.6 MPa
    • Goodman correction: σ_a,eff = σ_a / (1 - σ_m/σ_ult) = 49.6 / (1 - 25.5/650) = 51.7 MPa
    • N_f at 51.7 MPa: >5×10⁶ cycles → SF > 50× on 100,000 cycles

    Loads: Bolt preload (8×145 kN), pressure end force (636 kN at 10 bar), thermal growth push (4.3 mm axial) Model: 3D solid (C3D20R), 200K elements, contact at bolt holes (ZrO₂ bolts) and gasket interface

    5. Port Valve Structural Analysis — Ti₃AlC₂/ZrO₂

    5.1 Actuator Structural Loads

    Thermal actuation force (from PROD-04 Section 8.4): PortΔT TriggerDeflectionF_act (N)Spring Preload (N) ------------------------------------------------------------ 1130°C0.6 mm1548 5700°C3.7 mm7837 82180°C11.5 mm24315

    Pressure force on piston (5 bar, Ø12 mm): $$F_{press} = P \times \pi d^2/4 = 5 \times 10^5 \times \pi \times 0.012^2/4 = \textbf{5.7 N}$$

    Total opening force: F_act + F_press (pressure assists opening) — actuator overcomes spring preload

    5.2 Ti₃AlC₂ Actuator Strip Stress

    Bilayer strip: Ti₃AlC₂ (2 mm) / ZrO₂ (2 mm), 2×2×30 mm Bending stress (Timoshenko theory): $$\sigma_{Ti_3AlC_2} = \frac{E_{Ti} \Delta\alpha \DeltaT}{1+\frac{E_{Ti}t_{Ti}}{E_{Zr}t_{Zr}}} = \frac{280 \times 10^9 \times 1.3 \times 10^{-6} \times \DeltaT}{1+1.4} = 151 \times \DeltaT \text{ MPa}$$

    At Port 8 (ΔT = 2180°C): $$\sigma_{Ti} = 151 \times 2180 \times 10^{-6} = \mathbf{329 \text{ MPa}}$$

    Ti₃AlC₂ σ_f at 1400°C (actuator max temp): 280 MPa → SF = 0.85 (UNACCEPTABLE)

    Resolution: Actuator operates at lower temperature than drum gas. Actuator pocket is at drum OD (700°C max at Stage 8 per PROD-24 Section 7.1). At 700°C:

    • ΔT = 700 - 20 = 680°C
    • σ_Ti = 151 × 680 × 10⁻⁶ = 103 MPa
    • σ_f at 700°C ≈ 320 MPa → SF = 3.1×

    Actuator thermal isolation: Pocket depth 35 mm into drum wall (from OD). At drum OD = 700°C, 35 mm inward = 1050°C (linear gradient). Add 5 mm ceramic fiber insulation (ZrO₂ felt) at pocket outer face → actuator sees ≤700°C.

    5.3 Piston & Seal Stress

    Piston (3Y-TZP, Ø12×25 mm, 2 mm wall):

    • Pressure load: 5.7 N on 113 mm² → 0.05 MPa (negligible)
    • Centrifugal load (85 G, 25 g piston): 0.02 N
    • Spring preload (50 N): Hertzian contact on 45° cone
    • Contact width: 0.5 mm
    • Max contact pressure: ~200 MPa
    • 3Y-TZP σ_f at 700°C: 1000 MPa → SF = 5×

    Seal leak rate (line contact, 5 bar, 2200°C):

    • He leak test at RT: <10⁻⁸ mbar·L/s
    • At temperature: metal/ceramic creep closes micro-gaps → <10⁻⁶ mbar·L/s maintained

    5.4 Thermal Cycling Fatigue

    Actuator cycles: 1 per batch (6/day), 10,000 hrs = 2,200 cycles Strain range per cycle: Δε = Δα × ΔT = 1.3×10⁻⁶ × 680 = 8.8×10⁻⁴ Low-cycle fatigue (Ti₃AlC₂, kinking mechanism):

    • Δε_plastic ≈ 0 (elastic bending, kinking at ~0.5% strain)
    • N_f > 10⁵ cycles at this strain range → SF > 45×

    Piston spring (PEEK CF40 wave spring):

    • 3 waves, 50 N preload at 20°C, 30 N at 800°C
    • Creep at 800°C, 30 N: <1% strain in 10,000 hrs
    • Replace at 5,000 hrs (PM interval)

    6. Coil Housing & Cold Plate Structural

    6.1 Coil Housing (BFRP/Elium®)

    Geometry: 8× identical housings, 100 mm axial × 630 mm ID × 8 mm wall Loads: Lorentz force (J×B), thermal (coil 80°C, ambient 25°C), vibration Lorentz force (Zone 8, 500 kW, 1 kHz, 395 A, 8 turns): $$F = B I L N = 0.04 \times 395 \times (\pi \times 0.63) \times 8 = \textbf{2,500 N per zone}$$

    Radial pressure on housing: $$p = F / (L \times D) = 2500 / (0.1 \times 0.63) = \textbf{39.7 kPa} = \textbf{0.4 bar}$$

    Housing stress (BFRP, 8 mm wall, thin cylinder): $$\sigma_{hoop} = p r / t = 39700 \times 0.315 / 0.008 = \textbf{1.56 MPa}$$ BFRP σ_ult,hoop at 80°C: 950 MPa → SF = 609× — not critical

    6.2 Microchannel Cold Plate (AlSiC)

    Geometry: Cu microchannel base (12 mm thick) + AlSiC cover (6 mm) Channels: 40× (0.5 mm × 1 mm), 2 L/min per module Pressure: 0.8 bar drop at 2 L/min Thermal stress (AlSiC, CTE 7.5×10⁻⁶/K, Cu CTE 17×10⁻⁶/K):

    • ΔT = 55°C (25→80°C)
    • CTE mismatch stress: σ = E Δα ΔT / (1-ν) = 180×10⁹ × 9.5×10⁻⁶ × 55 / 0.7 = 134 MPa
    • AlSiC σ_y: 300 MPa → SF = 2.2×
    • Cu σ_y at 80°C: 200 MPa → SF = 1.5× (marginal)

    Resolution: Add compliant layer (indium foil, 50 μm) between Cu and AlSiC → reduces stress to 85 MPa, SF = 2.35× on Cu.

    7. Carousel & Slug Mold Structural

    7.1 Carousel (8-Position ZrO₂ Molds)

    Geometry: 8× ZrO₂ molds (3Y-TZP) on BFRP rotor, 400 mm diameter bolt circle Rotation: Indexing (not continuous), 16 positions (2 per stage for dual-stream) Loads: Centrifugal (mold + slug), thermal shock (2200°C → 25°C quench), thermal gradient

    7.2 Mold Thermal Shock Analysis

    Quench profile: 2200°C → 25°C in 60 s (N₂ quench, 50°C/s average) ZrO₂ properties: α = 11.2×10⁻⁶/K, E = 200 GPa (at 1000°C), k = 3.0 W/m·K Thermal stress (sudden surface cooling, semi-infinite solid): $$\sigma_{max} = \frac{E \alpha \Delta T}{1-\nu} \cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{\pi}} = \frac{200 \times 10^9 \times 11.2 \times 10^{-6} \times 2175}{0.7} \times 0.564 = \textbf{3.9 GPa}$$

    This EXCEEDS σ_f (800 MPa at 1200°C) by 5×.

    Mitigation — Controlled Quench:

    • N₂ flow ramped: 0 → 500 SLPM over 30 s, hold 30 s, then 2000 SLPM
    • Surface cooling rate limited to 20°C/s
    • With 20°C/s: σ_max = 3.9 GPa × √(20/50) = 2.5 GPa (still > σ_f)

    Resolution — Mold Design: 1. Thin-wall molds (3 mm wall) — reduces thermal gradient 2. Pre-heat molds to 800°C before casting (rotary pre-heat station) 3. Gradual quench: 2200°C → 1500°C in 60 s (air), 1500°C → 800°C in 60 s (N₂), 800°C → 25°C in 180 s (N₂) 4. With pre-heat + controlled quench: σ_max < 400 MPa → SF = 2.0× on 800 MPa at 1000°C

    Mold life: 500 batches (thermal shock is life-limiting) → 83 days at 6/day Spare mold set: 2× (16 molds total) — rotate every 250 batches

    7.3 Carousel Structural

    BFRP rotor: 400 mm bolt circle, 8× M16 ZrO₂ bolts per mold Centrifugal load (mold + slug, 5 kg total at 400 mm radius, 500 RPM): $$F = m \omega^2 r = 5 \times 52.36^2 \times 0.4 = \textbf{5,470 N per mold}$$ Bolt stress (8× M16 ZrO₂, tensile area 157 mm²): $$\sigma = 5470 / (8 \times 157) = \textbf{4.3 MPa} \ll \textbf{800 MPa}$$ SF > 180× — not critical
