    Heuristic Intro (Combined): PROD-25

    Combined Heuristic Introduction — PROD-25 Structural Analysis & FEA

    Williams Heuristic — Architectural Clarity

    Constraint (The Lock)

    The Aegis-Forge I structural analysis is forced into its thermomechanical FEA framework by a single irreducible principle: every load-bearing component must survive the simultaneous application of 2200°C thermal gradients, 500 RPM centrifugal loading, 10 bar pressure containment, and Carrington-class electromagnetic hostility — without a single structural metal.

    This constraint cascades into every structural decision:

    • Ceramics-only rotating drum: The ZrB₂-SiC drum (600 mm ID, 35 mm wall) is the only moving hot part. It must withstand 84.5 G centrifugal acceleration at ID, 5 bar internal pressure, and a 2000°C radial thermal gradient (2200°C ID → 700°C OD) — all while remaining electrically insulating (ρ > 10⁶ Ω·m) to maintain Carrington immunity. Any metallic reinforcement would couple GIC currents (5000 nT/s induces >100 A/km) into the structure, creating unintended heating paths and potential arc paths to the induction coils.
    • Composite-only stationary vessel: The BFRP/Elium® vessel (900 mm ID, 18 mm wall) must contain 10 bar design pressure while thermally isolating the composite (Tg = 80°C) from the 2200°C drum across a 68 mm gap (50 mm aerogel + 18 mm BFRP). No metallic flanges, no metallic bolts, no metallic gaskets — the entire pressure boundary is ceramic/composite. The 12× M24 ZrO₂ bolts and ZrO₂ gasket at the PEEK CF40 flanges are the only closure mechanism.
    • All-dielectric port valves: The 8 material exit ports use Ti₃AlC₂ MAX phase thermal actuators and 3Y-TZP ZrO₂ pistons — entirely ceramic, no metal springs (PEEK CF40 wave springs only), no metal seals. The actuator operates at the drum OD (≤700°C) where Ti₃AlC₂ retains 320 MPa strength.
    • Seismic without steel: The BFRP box beam frame must qualify to IEEE 693 High (PGA = 1.0g, ZPA = 1.5g) without any steel reinforcement. 6× BFRP stiffening rings + 4 vertical struts provide the required HCLPF ≥ 1.5g.

    What breaks if violated: A single steel bolt in the flange → GIC pickup → common-mode voltage on FBG interrogators → control system corruption. A metallic drum reinforcement → induction coupling → uncontrolled eddy currents → thermal runaway. A metallic port actuator → magnetic coupling at Stage 7 (2 kHz, ferromagnetic) → actuation failure at 1600°C.

    Necessity (The Key)

    The empirical gap this analysis closes is the measured divergence between room-temperature structural allowables and the combined thermomechanical reality of the operating envelope.

    Three specific gaps demand this integrated FEA approach:

    1. Thermal stress dominates centrifugal stress by 4×: At Stage 8, the 2000°C radial gradient generates 180 MPa thermal stress at the drum ID, while 500 RPM centrifugal loading adds only 42 MPa. Linear superposition (225 MPa combined) matches FEA, but the temperature-dependent material properties (E = 300 GPa, σ_f = 350 MPa at 2200°C) mean the safety factor is only 1.55×. Room-temperature analysis (σ_f = 620 MPa) would predict SF = 2.75× — a dangerous 78% overestimate. The gap: temperature-dependent strength vs. constant-property design.

    2. Port reinforcement requires coupled thermal-mechanical optimization: Unreinforced ports have K_t = 3.0 (σ_vm = 350 MPa at 2200°C → SF = 1.0). The ZrB₂-SiC sleeve + OD bulge reduces K_t to 1.6 (σ_vm = 210 MPa → SF = 1.81×). But the sleeve press-fit (0.03 mm) adds mechanical stress that combines with thermal stress at the port edge. Only a fully coupled thermomechanical FEA with contact modeling captures this interaction. The gap: sequential analysis (thermal then mechanical) vs. coupled thermomechanical contact.

    3. Vessel buckling is governed by thermal compression, not external pressure: At 200°C external surface, the BFRP hoop modulus drops to 45 GPa and thermal compressive stress reaches 78 MPa. The net hoop stress under 10 bar internal pressure is -53 MPa (compressive). With 4 stiffening rings, P_cr = 14.2 bar (SF = 1.42×); with 6 rings, P_cr = 18.5 bar (SF = 1.85×). The 6-ring design was driven by thermal buckling, not pressure buckling. The gap: pressure-only buckling analysis vs. thermomechanical buckling with temperature-dependent modulus.

    Measured data demanding this approach:

    • Drum FA-01 strain gauges (12 rosettes): 225 MPa measured vs. 225 MPa FEA at Stage 8, 400 RPM (PROD-04 Section 6.5)
    • Vessel hydrotest (15 bar): 38 MPa measured vs. 38 MPa Lamé prediction (PROD-06 Section 5.3)
    • Port 8 actuator calibration: 103 MPa actuator stress at 700°C (3.6 mm deflection at 680°C ΔT) — matches Timoshenko theory
    • Frame shake table test (IEEE 693): 1st mode at 8.2 Hz (FEA: 8.5 Hz), damping 2.1% (spec: 2%)
    • Bearing life test: 42,000 hrs to first spall (L10 prediction: 35,800 hrs)

    Commitment (The Turn)

    This document makes the following non-negotiable commitments that constrain all downstream documents:

    1. Drum minimum SF = 1.55× at Stage 8 combined loading — no operating condition may reduce this below 1.5×. PROD-23 control system enforces 400 RPM limit when T_inner > 2000°C. PROD-29 operations procedures include this limit. PROD-30 maintenance inspects Liner B interface after every Stage 8 run at >400 RPM.

    2. 6× vessel stiffening rings + 4 vertical struts are mandatory — required to achieve HCLPF = 1.6g (≥ 1.5g IEEE 693 High). PROD-27 manufacturing must include ring welding/fixture. PROD-28 QA verifies ring attachment. PROD-29 deployment includes strut installation.

    3. 12× M24 ZrO₂ bolts per flange (not 8×) — required for SF = 1.63× on bolt stress (490 MPa vs 800 MPa). PROD-27 manufacturing specifies bolt torque (160 N·m ceramic paste). PROD-28 QA torque audits. PROD-30 maintenance re-torque annually.

    4. NDT inspection interval = 500 batches (3 months) for drum UT — detects flaws >0.5 mm, limits crack growth to <54 μm (vs. critical 112 μm). PROD-28 QA executes. PROD-30 maintenance schedules. PROD-37 digital twin tracks inspection history.

    5. Carousel mold thermal shock controlled by 3-phase quench — 2200°C→1500°C (60s air), 1500°C→800°C (60s N₂), 800°C→25°C (180s N₂). Pre-heat to 800°C mandatory. Limits σ_max < 400 MPa (SF = 2.0× on 800 MPa). PROD-23 control system sequences quench. PROD-27 manufactures pre-heat station. PROD-28 QA validates quench profile.

    6. Port actuator operates at ≤700°C (5 mm ZrO₂ felt insulation at pocket) — ensures Ti₃AlC₂ SF ≥ 3.1×. PROD-04 drum machining specifies pocket insulation. PROD-27 manufacturing installs insulation. PROD-28 QA verifies temperature at actuator.

    7. Seismic capacity governed by vessel buckling (HCLPF = 1.6g) — frame and drum have higher margins. PROD-27 manufactures 6 stiffening rings. PROD-28 QA shake table tests. PROD-29 deployment verifies strut installation.

    8. All structural materials use PROD-24 temperature-dependent correlations — no "room temperature" properties in analysis. PROD-23 control uses E(T), σ_f(T) for real-time stress estimation. PROD-37 digital twin uses same correlations.

    These commitments are the structural load-bearing walls. PROD-27 (Manufacturing), PROD-28 (QA), PROD-29 (Deployment), PROD-30 (Maintenance), PROD-32 (Compliance), PROD-37 (Digital Twin), PROD-39 (T&E), FOLLOW-04/05/07/25 build on this foundation. They cannot move the walls.

    Keymaker Heuristic — Implementation Precision

    The Empirical Lock

    The fabrication fidelity gap in Aegis-Forge I structural analysis is the divergence between single-load-case allowable stress design and the measured behavior of ceramics and composites under combined extreme thermomechanical loading.

    Three specific locks prevent traditional ASME/ASCII code-based design from closing this gap:

    1. Ceramic strength is not a constant — it's a temperature-dependent distribution: ASME BPVC Section VIII uses constant allowable stress (S) with safety factors. But ZrB₂-SiC flexural strength drops from 620 MPa (RT) to 350 MPa (2200°C) — a 44% reduction. The Weibull modulus (m = 12) means failure probability is volume-dependent and stress-dependent. At Stage 8, the drum ID sees 225 MPa von Mises — SF = 1.55× on 350 MPa. But this is the mean strength; 10% of the volume sees >250 MPa (SF < 1.4×). The lock: constant safety factor on temperature-dependent Weibull strength.

    2. Composite failure is interactive, not separable: BFRP/Elium® vessel failure is governed by Tsai-Wu criterion (F_ijσ_iσ_j + F_iσ_i = 1), where hoop, axial, and shear stresses interact. At the gas port penetration under design pressure + thermal gradient, hoop = 52 MPa, axial = 35 MPa, shear = 22 MPa. Individual SFs: hoop 12.5×, axial 18.6×, shear 3.6×. But combined Tsai-Wu FI = 0.22 (SF = 4.5× on interaction). Sequential checking of individual components would miss the interaction. The lock: interactive failure criteria vs. component-by-component allowables.

    3. Thermal buckling is a load case, not a material property: The vessel external surface reaches 200°C during operation. The thermal compressive stress (78 MPa) exceeds the pressure tensile stress (25.5 MPa), creating net compression. The buckling critical pressure drops from 18.4 bar (RT) to 12.7 bar (200°C) — a 31% reduction. Standard pressure vessel codes treat buckling as an external pressure check; here it's an operating condition. The lock: thermal compression as a design-driving load case.

    Common thread: Every lock is a coupling between temperature and mechanical behavior that traditional codes treat as separable. The empirical lock is the sum of all neglected thermomechanical couplings.

    The Mathematical Key

    The single computational primitive that generates the structural solution is the temperature-dependent thermomechanical equilibrium equation solved on the coupled FEA mesh:

    $$\nabla \cdot \boldsymbol{\sigma} + \mathbf{f}_b = 0, \quad \boldsymbol{\sigma} = \mathbb{C}(T) : (\boldsymbol{\epsilon} - \boldsymbol{\epsilon}_{th}(T)) - \boldsymbol{\epsilon}_{creep}(t,T,\sigma)$$

    Where:

    • $\mathbb{C}(T)$ = temperature-dependent stiffness tensor (orthotropic for BFRP, isotropic for ceramics)
    • $\boldsymbol{\epsilon}_{th}(T) = \int_{T_{ref}}^T \boldsymbol{\alpha}(T') dT'$ = thermal strain from temperature history
    • $\boldsymbol{\epsilon}_{creep}$ = Norton-Bailey creep strain (for T > 1800°C)
    • $\mathbf{f}_b$ = body forces (centrifugal: $\rho \omega^2 r$, seismic: $\rho \mathbf{a}_{ground}$)

    This one equation, discretized on the 2.8M-element drum mesh and 50K-element vessel mesh, with temperature-dependent material properties from PROD-24, is the atomic computation.

    Everything in this document derives from it:

    • Drum FEA (Section 2): The equation solved on the rotating drum mesh with centrifugal body force and thermal strain from PROD-24's radial gradient. The Weibull post-processor integrates $P_f = 1-\exp[-(\sigma/\sigma_0)^m V/V_0]$ over the stressed volume.
    • Vessel FEA (Section 3): The equation on the shell mesh with orthotropic $\mathbb{C}(T)$, thermal strain from 250°C→150°C gradient, and pressure load. Tsai-Wu failure index computed from $\boldsymbol{\sigma}$ at each integration point.
    • Port valve (Section 5): The equation on the actuator strip mesh with $\mathbb{C}(T)$ for Ti₃AlC₂/ZrO₂ bilayer, thermal strain from ΔαΔT, contact boundary condition at piston seat.
    • Seismic (Section 8): The equation with $\mathbf{f}_b = \rho \mathbf{a}_{ground}(t)$ from IEEE 693 RRS time history. Modal superposition (30 modes) for transient response.
    • Fatigue (Section 9): The equation's stress history output feeds Coffin-Manson $\Delta\varepsilon_p/2 = \varepsilon_f'(2N_f)^c$ and Paris law $da/dN = C(\Delta K)^m$.
    • NDT (Section 10): The equation's stress distribution defines critical locations for UT/AE sensor placement.
    • Safety factors (Section 12): The equation's output σ_vm and FI are divided by temperature-dependent allowables.

    The mathematical key is not the FEA software, not the mesh, not the post-processor — it is the temperature-dependent thermomechanical equilibrium equation with thermal strain and creep, evaluated on the coupled mesh. If you solve this equation correctly with the right $\mathbb{C}(T)$, $\boldsymbol{\alpha}(T)$, $\sigma_f(T)$, you get the structural answer. The mesh is just the numerical vessel; the material correlations are the input; the equation is the primitive.

    History→Theory Correction

    Historical anomalies refine the equation's constitutive parameters and boundary conditions:

    1. Anomaly: Drum FA-01 strain gauges showed 230 MPa at Liner B interface vs. 200 MPa FEA (PROD-04 FA-01, 2026-10). Root cause: Liner B (ZrB₂-SiC, 3 mm) CTE mismatch with drum body — not perfectly matched at 1400°C due to B₄C sintering aid segregation. Correction: Updated liner CTE in $\boldsymbol{\alpha}(T)$: Zone B α = 6.2×10⁻⁶/K (was 5.8×10⁻⁶/K) for 1000-1500°C. Now predicts 228 MPa (4% error).

    2. Anomaly: Vessel gas port penetration showed FI = 0.22 vs. 0.18 predicted (PROD-06 hydrotest strain data). Root cause: Filament winding transition at port creates local fiber angle deviation (±5° from ±18° target). Correction: Added local material orientation perturbation in FEA mesh at ports (±5° random per ply). FI now 0.21 (2% error).

    3. Anomaly: Frame 1st bending mode 8.2 Hz vs. 8.5 Hz FEA (shake table, 2026-10). Root cause: Elastomeric isolator stiffness lower than spec at low strain (K_h = 2.1 MN/m vs. 2.5 MN/m spec). Correction: Updated isolator stiffness in boundary conditions from spec to measured (2.1 MN/m). Mode now 8.3 Hz (1% error).

    4. Anomaly: Port 8 actuator deflection 3.6 mm at 680°C ΔT vs. 3.8 mm Timoshenko prediction. Root cause: Brazed joint compliance (Ag-CuO-TiO₂, 50 μm) adds rotational spring at fixed end. Correction: Added rotational spring K_θ = 0.15 N·m/rad at actuator base in FEA. Deflection now 3.62 mm (0.6% error).

    5. Anomaly: Bearing L10 life 42,000 hrs vs. 35,800 hrs predicted (ISO 281). Root cause: N₂ gas film lubrication better than assumed (κ = 0.7 vs. 0.5) due to surface finish (Ra < 0.05 μm on Si₃N₄ races). Correction: Updated lubrication factor a_ISO = 2.5 (was 2.0). L10 = 44,750 hrs (6% error).

    The mathematical key absorbs history — each anomaly tightens a material correlation ($\mathbb{C}(T)$, $\boldsymbol{\alpha}(T)$), a boundary condition (isolator stiffness, braze compliance), or a model parameter (lubrication factor, fiber angle perturbation), but the equilibrium equation $\nabla \cdot \boldsymbol{\sigma} + \mathbf{f}_b = 0$ with thermal strain remains structurally invariant. This is the signature of a correct primitive: it extends, it does not rewrite.

    El Segundo Heuristic — Operational Excellence

    Mirror (Self-Reflection)

    How does the fabricator observe their own fabrication of the structural integrity? The Aegis-Forge I embeds in-situ structural self-diagnostics at every critical load path — the machine watches its own structure deform, fatigue, and approach limits in real time.

    Drum Self-Diagnostics (600 mm ID, 35 mm wall)

    FBG Sensor Array (PROD-24 Section 4.2, PROD-23 Section 5.1):

    • 128 FBG sensors embedded at 8 axial stations × 16 circumferential positions per station
    • Locations: Liner A (2200°C), Liner B interface (1500°C), Liner C interface (1000°C), drum OD (700°C)
    • Measures: Strain (ε) at 10 kHz, Temperature (T) via Bragg wavelength shift at 1 Hz
    • Self-reflection logic: Control system computes σ_vm(T) = E(T)·ε_vm in real time. If σ_vm > 0.8·σ_f(T) at any station → auto-reduce RPM to 300. If σ_vm > 0.9·σ_f(T) → emergency stop.
    • Calibration traceability: Each FBG pre-calibrated at 25°C, 500°C, 1000°C, 1500°C, 2000°C in PROD-24 thermal test rig. Drift < 0.5%/1000 hrs at 2200°C.

    Acoustic Emission (AE) Monitoring (PROD-28 Section 7.3, FOLLOW-28):

    • 8× KNbO₃ broadband AE sensors (100 kHz–1 MHz) mounted on drum OD at 45° intervals
    • Detects: Microcrack initiation (AE energy > 10⁻⁶ J), fiber pullout (BFRP vessel), bearing spall
    • Self-reflection logic: AE hit rate > 100 hits/s at Stage 8 → flag for UT inspection. AE location triangulation (±15 mm) maps crack growth to critical zones (port edges, liner interfaces).

    Infrared Thermography (IR) — Drum OD Surface (PROD-24 Section 6.1):

    • 2× FLIR A8580 (1.2 MP, 30 Hz, 3–5 μm) viewing drum OD through ZnSe window
    • Self-reflection logic: IR reconstructs T(r) profile. If T(r) deviates > 50°C from PROD-24 FEA prediction → flag insulation degradation or coil coupling anomaly. Auto-calibrates FBG temperature compensation.

    Vessel Self-Diagnostics (900 mm ID, 18 mm BFRP)

    FBG Sensors in BFRP Laminate:

    • 64 FBG sensors embedded during filament winding (PROD-06 Section 4.4): 16 per quadrant at mid-span, 16 at gas port penetration
    • Measures: Hoop strain, axial strain, shear strain (rosettes at ports)
    • Self-reflection logic: Computes Tsai-Wu FI in real time from ε_hoop, ε_axial, γ_shear via $\mathbb{C}^{-1}(T)$. If FI > 0.6 → alarm. If FI > 0.8 → reduce pressure setpoint. If FI > 0.95 → emergency vent.

    Fiber Optic Distributed Temperature Sensing (DTS):

    • 1× AP Sensing N4386 DTS along vessel exterior (1 m resolution, 0.1°C accuracy, 10 s update)
    • Self-reflection logic: Detects hot spots from insulation failure, gas port thermal short, aerogel settlement. Triggers IR verification.

    Frame & Foundation Self-Diagnostics

    Accelerometers (6× PCB 393B04, 0.5–10 kHz) on frame:

    • 2× vertical struts, 2× horizontal rings, 2× base isolators
    • Self-reflection logic: Continuous PSD monitoring. If 1st mode shifts > 5% (8.2 Hz → <7.8 Hz) → stiffness loss flag. If base acceleration > 0.1g RMS during operation → vibration anomaly.

    Tiltmeters (4× Jewell LSO-100, 0.1 μrad) on foundation:

    • Self-reflection logic: Differential settlement > 2 mm over 5 m → structural distress.

    Participation (Witness)

    How does the inside operator witness the structural phenomenon into existence? At what points must human judgment be present, and what cognitive checkpoints cannot be automated?

    Critical Participation Gates

    Gate 1: Drum Assembly — Liner Press-Fit Witness (PROD-27 Section 3.2)

    • Action: 3 mm Liner B (ZrB₂-SiC) pressed into drum body at 20°C (0.03 mm interference)
    • Witness requirement: Operator verifies interference fit force vs. displacement curve matches FEA prediction (peak force = 450 kN ± 10%). Any deviation > 10% → halt, inspect, re-FEA.
    • Why human: Friction coefficient μ at ceramic-ceramic interface varies with surface finish (Ra 0.8–1.2 μm). FEA assumes μ = 0.15; actual μ = 0.12–0.18. Only operator feel + force curve detects anomaly.
    • Cognitive checkpoint: "Does the force curve feel right?" — haptic judgment of ceramic seating.

    Gate 2: Vessel Filament Winding — Port Penetration Layup (PROD-27 Section 4.3)

    • Action: ±18° helical wind over gas port reinforcement (±55° hoop bias)
    • Witness requirement: Operator verifies fiber angle at port transition (±2° tolerance via laser angle gauge) and ply compaction (no voids > 1 mm via flash thermography).
    • Why human: Fiber steering at port penetration is geometrically complex. Automated winding follows toolpath, but local fiber angle depends on resin viscosity, tension, mandrel temperature — all variable.
    • Cognitive checkpoint: "Is the fiber sitting flat at the port edge?" — visual/tactile judgment of compaction.

    Gate 3: Flange Bolt Torque — Ceramic Bolt Ceremony (PROD-27 Section 5.1)

    • Action: 12× M24 ZrO₂ bolts torqued to 160 N·m with ceramic paste (BN-loaded)
    • Witness requirement: Two-person verification: Operator A torques to 160 N·m ± 5 N·m; Operator B independently re-checks with calibrated torque wrench. Both sign.
    • Why human: Ceramic bolts have no yield point — they fracture. Torque is the only preload indicator. No strain gauges on bolts (too hot). Human dual-verification is the safety barrier.
    • Cognitive checkpoint: "Did it click at 160?" — auditory/tactile confirmation of click-type wrench.

    Gate 4: Port Actuator Installation — Thermal Actuation Witness (PROD-27 Section 6.2)

    • Action: Ti₃AlC₂ actuator strip (10 mm × 40 mm × 0.5 mm) brazed to ZrO₂ piston (Ag-CuO-TiO₂, 50 μm joint)
    • Witness requirement: Operator verifies braze joint integrity via 10× magnification inspection (no voids > 50 μm, fillet radius > 0.2 mm) and measures free deflection at 680°C ΔT (3.6 mm ± 0.2 mm) in test furnace.
    • Why human: Braze joint quality is binary (good/bad) and visible only at 10×. Automated vision misses subsurface voids. Deflection test is the functional proof.
    • Cognitive checkpoint: "Does the actuator breathe at temperature?" — thermal functional test witnessed.

    Gate 5: Seismic Qualification — Shake Table Witness (PROD-28 Section 8, PROD-39 FAT)

    • Action: Full assembly on shake table, IEEE 693 High RRS (1.5g ZPA, 3-axis)
    • Witness requirement: Lead structural engineer witnesses test. Verifies: (a) No FBG reading exceeds 0.9·σ_f(T), (b) No AE bursts > 10⁻⁴ J, (c) No permanent deformation > 1 mm, (d) All ports actuate post-shake.
    • Why human: Seismic response is a system-level emergent behavior. No single sensor captures "the structure survived." Engineer synthesizes multi-sensor data into go/no-go.
    • Cognitive checkpoint: "Did the machine come back alive?" — holistic structural survival judgment.

    The Participation Principle

    The operator witnesses the structure into existence at every irreversible fabrication step where: 1. Material behavior has irreducible variability (ceramic friction, fiber angle, braze quality) 2. Failure mode is brittle and catastrophic (ceramic bolt fracture, drum burst) 3. No automated sensor provides complete coverage (preload on ceramic bolts, braze voids)

    Automation handles the repeatable; humans witness the critical. The machine fabricates; the operator witnesses the fabrication becoming structure.

    PROD-26: Electrical Safety and GIC Immunity

    Combined Heuristic Introduction — PROD-26 Electrical Safety & GIC Immunity

    Williams Heuristic — Architectural Clarity

    Constraint (The Lock)

    The Aegis-Forge I electrical safety architecture is forced into its all-dielectric topology by a single irreducible principle: no copper conductor may cross the pressure boundary into the 2200°C induction zone during a Carrington-class geomagnetic storm (dB/dt = 5000 nT/s).

    This constraint is not a design preference — it is physics. A 5000 nT/s field induces >100 V/km on conductors. At 50 m cable run: >5 V common-mode. The GaN gate drivers (GS66516T, LMG1210) have 6 V threshold. A single ground loop couples kV from GIC into the gate drive — instant destruction. The FBG interrogators (VCSEL, InGaAs PIN) share the same vulnerability. The isolation transformer secondary is floating — no neutral-earth bond — because a grounded neutral provides the return path for GIC to enter the process electronics.

    The constraint cascades into every electrical decision:

    • All 480+ sensors on PMMA POF: FBG temperature/strain (384), POF level (16), pyrometer (8), mass spec (8), XRF (8), pressure (24), flow (32), vibration (16), encoder (2), E-stop (8) — zero copper
    • All 96+ actuators on PMMA POF: GaN gates (16), varactor bias (32), cap bank (48), MFC (32), port valves (8), carousel (1), flux (8), quench (16), drum drive (1), crane interlock (4)
    • Cooling water: PEX-a tubing (cross-linked PE, ρ>10¹⁴ Ω·m) — no copper pipe, no conductive path to building ground
    • Enclosures: BFRP/Elium® (ρ>10¹² Ω·m) — no steel cabinets, no metallic conduit
    • Penetrations: Al₂O₃/ZrO₂ ceramic bushings only — no metal feedthroughs
    • Power distribution: Isolation transformer (Δ-Y, floating secondary), NGR 5A — no ground reference on process side

    What breaks if violated: A single copper wire for "just the E-stop" → GIC antenna → 5 V common-mode on GaN gate → GaN shoot-through → 500 kW inverter destruction → drum thermal runaway → vessel overpressure → catastrophic failure. The constraint is binary: all-dielectric or dead forge.

    Necessity (The Key)

    The empirical gap this document closes is the measured divergence between standard industrial electrical safety (grounded, copper-wired, EMC-compliant) and the verified behavior of the Aegis-Forge I under combined Carrington GIC + 500 kW induction + 2200°C thermomechanical loading.

    Three specific gaps demand this architecture:

    1. Standard grounding creates the GIC antenna: IEEE 142 / NFPA 70 require equipment grounding conductors. But in a 5000 nT/s event, the ground conductor is the antenna. The measured GIC on Hydro-Québec 1989 was 100 A on neutral conductors. A grounded forge would see 100 A flowing through its "safety ground" into the GaN gate drivers. The gap: grounding for safety vs. grounding as GIC antenna.

    2. Standard EMC assumes copper shielding: CISPR 11 / IEC 61000-4 assume metallic enclosures and shielded cables. But in the forge, a steel cabinet at 2200°C ambient (radiative coupling) with 500 kW of 1–100 kHz magnetic fields becomes a Faraday cage that concentrates eddy currents. The measured field inside PROD-03 coil housing is 39.6 mT at Z8. A steel enclosure would see 50 kW of eddy current heating. The gap: metallic shielding vs. dielectric transparency.

    3. Standard SIL-3 assumes independent channels: IEC 61508 2oo3 voting assumes physical separation. But in the forge, all 3 FBG sensors per zone share: same interrogator, same POF cable tray, same 24 VDC supply, same RTU. A single interrogator failure = common cause = all 3 channels lost. The gap: independent channels vs. shared infrastructure in constrained volume.

    Measured data demanding this approach:

    • PROD-23 GIC ride-through test: 100 A/m Helmholtz field, 30 min — zero spurious trips, zero data loss
    • PROD-10 EMC test: CISPR 11 Class A passed with 20 dB margin — no metal shielding
    • PROD-23 SIS proof test (CT-04): 24 SIL-3 SIFs, PFDavg = 2.3×10⁻³ — meets <10⁻²
    • PROD-25 megger test: All 50+ penetrations >1 GΩ at 500 VDC — no conductive leakage
    • PROD-10 arc flash calc: 0.3 cal/cm² at 18" (process) vs 4.2 cal/cm² (grid) — Cat 0 PPE

    Commitment (The Turn)

    This document makes the following non-negotiable commitments that constrain all downstream documents:

    1. PMMA POF is the only fieldbus — 480+ sensors, 96+ actuators, TSN, PTP, SIS. No copper, no wireless, no powerline. PROD-27 manufacturing must qualify POF draw ($0.08–0.15/m). PROD-28 QA verifies attenuation <0.2 dB/m. PROD-29 operations includes POF inspection. PROD-36/37 architect around this.

    2. Floating secondary + NGR 5A is mandatory — no neutral-earth bond on process side. PROD-27 specifies isolation transformer (Δ-Y, BFRP, 10 kV BIL). PROD-28 verifies ground fault <5 A. PROD-29 includes NGR monitoring. PROD-32 permits require this.

    3. PEX-a for all coolant — no copper pipe, no conductive water path. DI water 18 MΩ·cm maintained. PROD-27 specifies PEX-a circuit. PROD-28 verifies resistivity. PROD-29 includes DI polisher.

    4. 24 SIL-3 SIFs immutable — Table in Appendix C defines safety envelope. PROD-27 manufactures dedicated SIS FPGA boards. PROD-28 executes CT-04 proof tests. PROD-32 requires SIL-3 cert. PROD-39 FAT includes SIF injection. No downgrade without full re-certification.

    5. TSN schedule frozen — 1 ms cycle, 4 slices (SIS/RTU/PLC/SCADA), 100 μs guard band. PROD-27 manufactures TSN switches (BFRP). PROD-28 verifies latency <100 μs. PROD-37 twin sync depends on this.

    6. Air-gap absolute — no IT→OT IP path. Data diode unidirectional (OT→IT) only. PROD-27 installs hardware diode. PROD-28 verifies no reverse traffic. PROD-36/37 architect around this.

    7. PTP <1 μs required — GNSS+OCXO grandmaster, 24h holdover, all nodes boundary clocks. PROD-27 manufactures grandmaster (BFRP). PROD-28 verifies sync. PROD-10/23 resonance tracking depends on this.

    8. BFRP/YInMn Blue glaze as conductive bleed — SRI=115 glaze provides static dissipation path (1 MΩ to earth). PROD-06 specifies glaze. PROD-28 verifies surface resistivity. PROD-25 seismic qualifies glaze adhesion.

    These commitments are the electrical load-bearing walls. PROD-27 (Manufacturing), PROD-28 (QA), PROD-29 (Deployment), PROD-30 (Maintenance), PROD-32 (Compliance), PROD-36 (Cyber-Physical), PROD-37 (Digital Twin), PROD-39 (T&E), FOLLOW-10/11/27/29 build on this foundation. They cannot move the walls.

    Keymaker Heuristic — Implementation Precision

    The Empirical Lock

    The fabrication fidelity gap in Aegis-Forge I electrical safety is the divergence between IEC 61508 / NFPA 70E compliant design and the measured behavior of an all-dielectric control system inside a 500 kW induction furnace at 2200°C during a Carrington storm.

    Three specific locks prevent traditional electrical safety engineering from closing this gap:

    1. Grounding is the vulnerability, not the protection: Every industrial standard (IEEE 142, NFPA 70, IEC 60364) mandates equipment grounding conductors for fault current return and shock protection. But in the forge, the ground conductor becomes the GIC antenna. 5000 nT/s induces >100 V/km. A 50 m ground wire = 5 V common-mode. The GaN gate driver threshold is 6 V. The "safety ground" destroys the safety system. The lock: safety ground as GIC antenna.

    2. EMC shielding requires conductivity — the forge forbids it: CISPR 11 / IEC 61000-4 assume metallic enclosures (steel, aluminum) for radiated emission containment and immunity. But at 2200°C with 500 kW of 1–100 kHz magnetic fields, a steel cabinet becomes an induction heater. The measured B-field at Z8 is 39.6 mT. Eddy current heating in 2 mm steel: P = π²B²f²d²V/6ρ ≈ 50 kW. The cabinet would melt. The lock: metallic shielding as induction heater.

    3. SIL-3 independence assumes no shared infrastructure: IEC 61508 2oo3 voting requires physical separation of sensors, logic solvers, and final elements. But the forge has: 3 FBG sensors sharing 1 interrogator, 3 RTUs sharing 1 TSN ring, 3 SIS FPGAs sharing 1 TSN VLAN, all powered from 1 DC bus. A single interrogator failure = common cause = all 3 channels lost. The lock: shared infrastructure as common cause failure.

    Common thread: Every lock is a standard safety practice that becomes a hazard in the forge's unique electromagnetic-thermal environment. The empirical lock is the sum of all safety practices that invert under Carrington + induction + temperature.

    The Mathematical Key

    The single computational primitive that generates the electrical safety solution is the discrete-time thermal-admittance model executed at 1 kHz on the Zone RTU, which doubles as the GIC/SIF prediction engine:

    $$T_{inner}[k+1] = T_{inner}[k] + \frac{\Delta t}{\rho c V} \left( P_{ind}[k] - h A (T_{inner}[k] - T_{flange}[k]) - \epsilon \sigma A (T_{inner}^4[k] - T_{surr}^4) \right)$$

    Where:

    • $T_{inner}$ = Drum inner surface temperature (virtual sensor, reconstructed from 48 FBG/zone)
    • $P_{ind}$ = Induction power command (from thermal PID + feedforward)
    • $h A$ = Convective conductance to flange (identified online)
    • $\epsilon \sigma A$ = Radiative conductance (dominant >800°C, T⁴ nonlinearity)
    • $\Delta t = 1$ ms (RTU cycle time)

    This one equation, discretized on the ARM Cortex-A53 (Zephyr RTOS, <100 μs compute), is the atomic computation.

    Everything in this document derives from it:

    • GIC Ride-Through (Section 3.3): The model predicts $T_{inner}$ 50 ms ahead. If grid dV/dt > threshold → model projects thermal trajectory → if $dT/dt > 100°C/s$ predicted → pre-emptive ride-through initiation. The same model that controls temperature predicts the thermal consequence of grid loss.
    • SIS Pre-Emptive Trip (Section 8): SIF-00-01 (drum over-temp) uses model prediction: if $T_{inner}[k+50] > T_{lim}$ → trip now, not when FBG reads limit. 50 ms prediction horizon matches SIS response requirement.
    • Resonance Tracking (PROD-10/23): The model's $P_{ind}$ output feeds the power-to-frequency LUT. ZVS maintenance requires knowing thermal load → impedance → frequency shift. The model provides the thermal load estimate.
    • Arc Flash Energy (Section 7): The model's $T_{inner}$ trajectory defines the thermal state during fault clearing. Incident energy calculation uses actual $T_{inner}(t)$ not worst-case.
    • Insulation Aging (Section 11): The model's $T_{flange}$ history feeds Arrhenius aging model for PTFE/PEX-a/BFRP. Predictive maintenance triggers at 80% design life.
    • Digital Twin Sync (PROD-37): The model state vector $[T_{inner}, T_{flange}, P_{ind}, f_{res}]$ published at 10 Hz via OPC-UA/Kafka is the twin's boundary condition.

    The mathematical key is not the PID, not the PLL, not the SIS logic — it is the thermal-admittance model that unifies temperature control, GIC survival, SIS pre-emption, resonance tracking, and digital twin synchronization. If you execute this model correctly at 1 kHz with the right $hA(T)$, $\epsilon\sigma A(T)$, $\rho c V(T)$, you get electrical safety. The SIL-3 logic is just the trip condition on the model output.

    The Turn (Both Directions)

    Theory→History Validation

    The thermal-admittance model predicts historical test data from the CSMFAB0108 development program:

    History→Theory Correction

    Historical anomalies refine the model's constitutive parameters and boundary conditions:

    1. Anomaly: Char growth oscillation at 0.8 Hz, ±15°C (PROD-16 Stage 3, 2026-10). Root cause: Char layer thickness changes thermal resistance → modulates $hA$ → modulates $T_{inner}$ → modulates pyrolysis rate → modulates char growth. Correction: Added char thickness state $\delta_{char}[k]$ to RLS (Recursive Least Squares) estimator. $\delta_{char}[k+1] = \delta_{char}[k] + \alpha (T_{inner}[k] - T_{pyro}) \Delta t$. Model residual dropped from 8°C to 1.2°C RMS.

    2. Anomaly: FBG wavelength drift 0.5 nm/hr at 2200°C (PROD-24 FA-01, 2026-09). Root cause: PMMA FBG annealing at >800°C. Not sensor failure — material physics. Correction: Added reference FBG (unstrained, same thermal path) per zone. Common-mode subtraction: $\Delta\lambda_{meas} = \Delta\lambda_{sense} - \Delta\lambda_{ref}$. Drift reduced to <0.05 nm/hr. Model uses corrected $\Delta\lambda$.

    3. Anomaly: TSN latency spike 2.3 ms during Stage 7 transition (PROD-20, 2026-10). Root cause: PLC SFC transition caused TSN queue congestion on shared VLAN. Correction: Moved SIS to dedicated VLAN 10 with 200 μs time slice. PLC/SCADA on VLAN 20/30. Added local OCXO on each RTU (100 ppb stability). Latency now <80 μs max.

    4. Anomaly: Varactor saturation at 28 V (Z7/Z8 high power) — tuning range exhausted (PROD-10, 2026-10). Root cause: At 350–500 kW, tank impedance shift requires >28 V varactor bias for ZVS. Correction: Added 8-bit switched capacitor bank (coarse) + varactor (fine). Cap bank steps cover 80% of range, varactor covers ±5%. ZVS maintained 99.9% cycles.

    5. Anomaly: PEX-a coolant resistivity drop from 18 MΩ·cm to 2 MΩ·cm after 500 hrs (PROD-10, 2026-10). Root cause: Copper ion leaching from microchannel cold plate (Ni-P coating defect). Correction: Upgraded cold plate to AlSiC with indium foil TIM (PROD-25 Section 6.2). Resistivity stable >15 MΩ·cm at 1000 hrs.

    The mathematical key absorbs history — each anomaly tightens a model parameter ($hA$, $\epsilon\sigma A$, $\rho c V$), adds a state ($\delta_{char}$, reference FBG), or restructures a boundary condition (TSN VLAN, cap bank, cold plate material). The primitive $T_{inner}[k+1] = f(T_{inner}[k], P_{ind}[k], \text{params}[k])$ remains structurally invariant. This is the signature of a correct primitive: it extends, it does not rewrite.

    El Segundo Heuristic — Operational Excellence

    Mirror (Self-Reflection)

    How does the fabricator observe their own electrical fabrication? The Aegis-Forge I embeds four nested electrical metrology loops — the machine watches its own electrical integrity at the scale of the phenomenon.

    Level 0 — Gate-Level Witness (FPGA, 100 kHz)

    What the FPGA sees:

    • Desaturation Detect: GaN $V_{DS}$ monitored at 10 ns resolution. If $V_{DS} > 10$ V during on-state → shoot-through → instant leg shutdown (<100 ns). No software, no network — pure hardware.
    • ZVS Timestamp: Switch voltage zero-crossing vs. gate command. Phase error $\phi_{err} = t_{V_{DS}=0} - t_{gate\_on}$. Target: $\phi_{err} < 5$ ns. Logged every cycle (100 kHz).
    • Current Sense: 16-bit ADC at 1 MHz on DC link shunt. Harmonic analysis (FFT 512 pts) → detects bearing wear, coil short, capacitor degradation.
    • Health Output: Per-cycle status word on POF: ZVS_OK DESAT_OKCURRENT_OK TEMP_OK. SCADA aggregates at 10 Hz.

    Self-reflection logic: If ZVS_OK < 99.9% over 1000 cycles → RTU reduces power 10%, logs degradation. If DESAT_OK < 100% → instant SIF trip. The FPGA witnesses its own switching integrity every 10 μs.

    Level 1 — Thermal Reconstruction (RTU, 1 kHz)

    What the RTU sees:

    • 48 FBG Inputs/Zone: 384 temperatures @ 125 Hz each via WDM+TDM. Wavelength → temperature conversion: $T = (\lambda - \lambda_{ref}) / 0.15$ nm/°C.
    • Virtual Sensor: Runs the thermal-admittance model (Section 2 Mathematical Key) at 1 kHz. Inputs: 48 FBG temps, power command, flange temps. Output: $T_{inner}$ prediction ±5°C at 2200°C.
    • Model Residual: $r[k] = T_{FBG,flange}[k] - T_{model,flange}[k]$. If $r > 2°C$ RMS → re-identification triggered (RLS updates $hA$, $\epsilon\sigma A$).
    • SIF Prediction: Projects $T_{inner}[k+50]$ (50 ms ahead). If predicted > limit → pre-emptive SIF trip.

    Self-reflection logic: The RTU witnesses the thermal state of its zone at 1 ms resolution. It compares measured vs. predicted, identifies model drift, and predicts safety violations before they occur. The model is the mirror — it reflects the zone's thermal reality back to the controller.

    Level 2 — Cascade Consistency (PLC, 100 Hz)

    What the PLC sees:

    • Mass-Energy Balance: $\sum \dot{m}_{in} - \sum \dot{m}_{out} = dM/dt$. XRF/LIBS composition × flow rate = elemental flow. Closure >99.5%/batch or investigation flag.
    • Stage Interlock Status: All 72 SIFs (24 SIL-3, 12 SIL-2, 36 SIL-1) evaluated every 1 ms (SIS) / 10 ms (PLC). Status matrix published on TSN VLAN 10.
    • Recipe Execution: ISA-88 recipe state machine. Current segment, time remaining, setpoint trajectory. Deviation >5% → alarm.
    • Feedforward to Downstream: Elemental composition, gas analysis, thermal state passed to next stage PLC.

    Self-reflection logic: The PLC witnesses the stage's material and energy transformation. It verifies conservation laws hold, checks recipe adherence, and ensures downstream stages receive accurate feedforward. The mass-energy balance is the mirror — it reflects the stage's process reality.

    Level 3 — Digital Twin Shadow (SCADA → PROD-37, 10 Hz)

    What the Twin sees:

    • Full State Vector: 512-core HPC runs same thermal-admittance model + CFD (PROD-24) + FEA (PROD-25) + electromagnetics (PROD-03). Inputs: all 480 sensor streams + 96 actuator commands.
    • ML Autoencoder (FOLLOW-29): Trained on 10,000 nominal batches. Encodes 1000-dimensional state to 32 latent dims. Reconstruction error >3σ → anomaly flag.
    • Predictive Suggestions: Twin simulates next 100 batches with PID gain variations, flux rate adjustments, RPM profiles. Suggests optimal setpoints to SCADA.
    • Fleet Learning: Aggregates across all Forges (PROD-37 fleet twin). Transfers learned corrections.

    Self-reflection logic: The digital twin witnesses the entire forge's electro-thermal-mechanical state. It runs higher-fidelity models than real-time allows, detects anomalies the local controllers miss, and proposes optimizations. The twin is the mirror at system scale.

    Participation (Witness)

    How does the inside operator witness the electrical phenomenon into existence? At what points must human judgment authorize electrical consequence?

    Critical Participation Gates

    Gate 1: Batch Recipe Authorization — Electrical Load Profile (PROD-29 Section 4.1)

    • Action: Feedstock UUID scanned → Category A–D → Operator confirms recipe. Recipe defines 8-zone power profile (0–500 kW each), frequency ladder, thermal ramp rates.
    • Witness requirement: Operator verifies recipe power profile matches feedstock composition. Category A (PCBs) = high Z6/Z7 power. Category C (batteries) = high Z3/Z4 power. Wrong profile = thermal runaway or incomplete separation.
    • Why human: Feedstock composition has irreducible variability (Category A: 15–25% Cu, 5–15% Fe, 0.1–0.5% PM). No sensor measures "Category A-ness" — only composition. Operator judgment maps composition to recipe.
    • Cognitive checkpoint: "Does this power profile match what I see in the feed?" — pattern recognition of feedstock vs. recipe.

    Gate 2: Stage Transition Gate — Electrical State Verification (PROD-29 Section 4.3)

    • Action: Stage complete → Shift Lead reviews: energy delivered vs. planned, gas composition vs. setpoint, SIF events, anomaly flags, thermal model residuals.
    • Witness requirement: For Stage 4: visual In-grade confirmation (pyrometer + XRF at Port 4A). For Stage 6: H₂ <4% verification (ZrO₂ pO₂ probe) before Port 6B open. For Stage 8: SiO₂ condenser flow verification (mass spec).
    • Why human: SIF events are recorded but not interpreted. A "cooling water loss" SIF that self-cleared in 50 s might indicate pump cavitation — operator judges if pump needs replacement. Anomaly flags are data — operator judges significance.
    • Cognitive checkpoint: "Is the electrical state clean for the next stage?" — synthesis of energy, gas, SIF, anomaly data.

    Gate 3: SIF Bypass Authorization — Organizational Risk Acceptance (PROD-29 Section 5.2)

    • Action: Dual-key (Shift Lead + Safety Engineer), time-limited (4 hr max), blockchain-audited (Hyperledger Fabric, PROD-37).
    • Witness requirement: Both signatories review: which SIF, why bypass, compensating measures, risk assessment, expiration time. Blockchain record immutable.
    • Why human: Risk acceptance is organizational, not algorithmic. No mathematical function accepts "we'll run with SIF-00-07 bypassed because NGR monitor is drifting." Human judgment weighs production loss vs. safety margin.
    • Cognitive checkpoint: "Do I accept this risk for this duration with these compensations?" — explicit risk acceptance.

    Gate 4: Carrington Ride-Through Exit — Post-Storm Recovery (PROD-29 Section 5.4)

    • Action: Grid stable 30 min → Operator verifies: drum thermal state (no shock >100°C/s), SIF health (all 24 SIL-3 OK), FBG/PTP/TSN sync, LiFePO₄ charge >80%. Authorizes staged grid reconnect with utility coordination.
    • Witness requirement: Thermal shock check is critical — drum at 2200°C, grid reconnect causes inrush. If drum cooled >100°C/s during island, thermal stress could crack ZrB₂-SiC. Operator verifies model-predicted $dT/dt$ < 100°C/s.
    • Why human: Grid coordination requires utility communication (voice, not data diode). Thermal shock judgment combines model prediction + operator experience. No algorithm coordinates with utility dispatcher.
    • Cognitive checkpoint: "Did the forge survive the storm intact?" — holistic electrical-thermal survival judgment.

    Gate 5: FAT/SAT Sign-Off — Electrical Qualification Acceptance (PROD-39)

    • Action: Lead Electrical Engineer witnesses: CT-01 rotordynamics, CT-02 hydrotest, CT-03 megger/hipot, CT-04 SIF proof, CT-05 resonance, CT-06 FBG cal, CT-07 GIC ride-through, CT-08 thermal cycle, CT-09 seismic, CT-10 integrated run.
    • Witness requirement: Reviews all 10 test reports, signs each. Any deviation from spec → NCR (PROD-28) → root cause → re-test.
    • Why human: Test data is necessary but not sufficient. Engineer judges: "Is the 2.3 ms TSN latency spike in CT-05 acceptable?" (Yes, <100 μs guard band). "Is the 0.5 pC PD on XFMR acceptable?" (Yes, <5 pC limit). Data + judgment = sign-off.
    • Cognitive checkpoint: "Does this electrical system meet spec in the real world?" — professional engineering judgment.

    The Participation Principle

    The operator witnesses the electrical system into existence at every irreversible authorization point where: 1. Composition-to-recipe mapping has irreducible variability (feedstock category → power profile) 2. Risk acceptance is organizational, not algorithmic (SIF bypass, ride-through exit) 3. Multi-party coordination is required (utility reconnect, FAT sign-off) 4. Model prediction needs experiential validation (thermal shock, anomaly significance)

    Automation executes the physics; humans authorize the consequences. The forge controls the electrons; the operator witnesses the electrons becoming safe operation.

    1. Electrical Safety Architecture

    1.1 Design Philosophy

    The Aegis-Forge I electrical safety architecture is governed by a single irreducible principle: no conductive path shall exist between the process zone (2200°C, 500 kW induction, Carrington-class GIC environment) and earth ground. This constraint forces the entire field layer — 480+ sensors, 96+ actuators, 8 GaN inverter modules — to communicate and be powered through all-dielectric media: PMMA plastic optical fiber (POF) for signals, PEX-a tubing for coolant, BFRP housings for enclosures, ceramic bushings for penetrations.

    Three non-negotiable constraints define the architecture:

    ConstraintImplementationVerification ------------------------------------------ Zero conductive penetrationPMMA POF only fieldbus (980 μm core), PEX-a coolant, BFRP enclosures, ZrO₂/Al₂O₃ bushingsMegger >10 GΩ at 500 VDC between process and earth Floating power distributionIsolation transformer (Δ-Y, floating secondary), NGR 5A, no neutral-earth bondGround fault current <5 A under any single fault Carrington GIC immunity5000 nT/s → <1 V induced on POF; ride-through mode (5 ms cap → 10 ms island → LiFePO₄)Helmholtz coil test 100 A/m, no spurious trips

    Consequences of violation: A single copper wire crossing the pressure boundary becomes a GIC antenna. 5000 nT/s induces >100 V/km. At 50 m cable length: >5 V common-mode on a GaN gate driver (6 V threshold) = destruction. At 100 V common-mode on FBG interrogator = permanent damage. The all-dielectric architecture is not a preference — it is the only topology that survives.

    3.3 GIC Ride-Through Mode (PROD-23 Section 7)

    GIC EVENT DETECTION (L3 SCADA + L2 PLC):
  Grid Monitor (dedicated) → dV/dt > 5 V/ms OR NGR current > 2 A
       │
       ▼

  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ 1. DC link capacitors sustain inverter power (100 ms hold)  │
  │ 2. Vacuum contactor opens (10 ms) → island from grid        │
  │ 3. LiFePO₄ backup (100 Wh/module) powers controls           │
  │ 4. All zones ramp to 20% power (thermal hold)               │
  │ 5. SIS remains active (dedicated FPGA + POF)                │
  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
       │
       ▼
  GIC EVENT DURATION (1–10 min):
  • Drum rotation maintained (piezo drive, battery)
  • Gas atmospheres maintained (MFC battery backup)
  • FBG/PTP/TSN fully operational (all-dielectric)
  • No data loss — historian buffers locally
       │
       ▼
  GRID RECOVERY (30 min stable):
  1. Verify grid frequency/voltage stable (PLL lock)
  2. Verify drum thermal state (no shock >100°C/s)
  3. Verify SIF health (all 24 SIL-3 OK)
  4. Operator authorization (Shift Lead + Safety Eng)
  5. Staged reconnect with utility coordination

    9. Grounding & Bonding — IEEE Std 142 / IEEE Std 1100

    9.1 Grounding Philosophy

    Single-Point Ground at Substation Only. No ground reference anywhere in the process zone. All "grounding" inside the forge is equipotential bonding via 1 MΩ bleed resistors for static dissipation only.

    GROUNDING TOPOLOGY:
Utility Substation (Single Point)
       │
       ▼
Isolation Transformer (Δ-Y, Floating Secondary)
       │
       ▼
Neutral Grounding Resistor (5 A, 400 V) → Earth
       │
       ├──► Transformer Tank (BFRP, no metal)
       ├──► Cable Trays (BFRP, 1 MΩ bleed)
       ├──► Enclosures (BFRP, 1 MΩ bleed)
       ├──► Cooling Water (PEX-a, DI water 18 MΩ·cm)
       └──► Structure (BFRP frame, no steel)

    9.2 Equipotential Bonding Network

    ComponentBonding MethodResistance --------------------------------------- BFRP Cable TraysCarbon fiber braid + 1 MΩ to earth1 MΩ BFRP EnclosuresCarbon fiber lug + 1 MΩ to tray1 MΩ Ceramic BushingsNo bonding (inherently insulating)>10¹³ Ω PEX-a PipeNo bonding (inherently insulating)>10¹⁴ Ω PMMA POFNo bonding (inherently insulating)>10¹⁵ Ω Indium Foil (TIM)Local to cold plate only<1 mΩ (thermal)

    9.3 Static Dissipation

    • Charge Generation: Drum rotation (500 RPM), particle flow, gas flow
    • Dissipation Path: YInMn Blue glaze (SRI=115, conductive surface) → BFRP frame → 1 MΩ bleed → earth
    • Maximum Potential: <100 V (verified by ESD test IEC 61000-4-2)
    • Spark Prevention: All ports have ZrO₂ piston with 0.05 mm clearance — no spark gap

    12.4 Secure Boot Chain

    FPGA/RTU/PLC BOOT SEQUENCE:
1. Hardware Root of Trust (eFuse) → Verify Stage 1 Bootloader (RSA-2048)
2. Stage 1 → Verify Stage 2 Firmware (ECDSA-P256)
3. Stage 2 → Verify Config (FRAM/MRAM, SHA256 + HMAC)
4. Stage 2 → Verify Application (Git tag hash, SHA256)
5. All stages → Measure into TPM 2.0 (PCR 0-7)
6. Remote Attestation → SCADA verifies PCR values at startup

    Key Management: HSM (FIPS 140-2 Level 3) at SCADA. Keys rotated annually. Root key offline.

    Combined Heuristic Introduction — PROD-26 Electrical Safety & GIC Immunity

    Williams Heuristic — Architectural Clarity

    Constraint (The Lock)

    The Aegis-Forge I electrical safety architecture is forced into its all-dielectric topology by a single irreducible principle: no copper conductor may cross the pressure boundary into the 2200°C induction zone during a Carrington-class geomagnetic storm (dB/dt = 5000 nT/s).

    This constraint is not a design preference — it is physics. A 5000 nT/s field induces >100 V/km on conductors. At 50 m cable run: >5 V common-mode. The GaN gate drivers (GS66516T, LMG1210) have 6 V threshold. A single ground loop couples kV from GIC into the gate drive — instant destruction. The FBG interrogators (VCSEL, InGaAs PIN) share the same vulnerability. The isolation transformer secondary is floating — no neutral-earth bond — because a grounded neutral provides the return path for GIC to enter the process electronics.

    The constraint cascades into every electrical decision:

    • All 480+ sensors on PMMA POF: FBG temperature/strain (384), POF level (16), pyrometer (8), mass spec (8), XRF (8), pressure (24), flow (32), vibration (16), encoder (2), E-stop (8) — zero copper
    • All 96+ actuators on PMMA POF: GaN gates (16), varactor bias (32), cap bank (48), MFC (32), port valves (8), carousel (1), flux (8), quench (16), drum drive (1), crane interlock (4)
    • Cooling water: PEX-a tubing (cross-linked PE, ρ>10¹⁴ Ω·m) — no copper pipe, no conductive path to building ground
    • Enclosures: BFRP/Elium® (ρ>10¹² Ω·m) — no steel cabinets, no metallic conduit
    • Penetrations: Al₂O₃/ZrO₂ ceramic bushings only — no metal feedthroughs
    • Power distribution: Isolation transformer (Δ-Y, floating secondary), NGR 5A — no ground reference on process side

    What breaks if violated: A single copper wire for "just the E-stop" → GIC antenna → 5 V common-mode on GaN gate → GaN shoot-through → 500 kW inverter destruction → drum thermal runaway → vessel overpressure → catastrophic failure. The constraint is binary: all-dielectric or dead forge.

    Necessity (The Key)

    The empirical gap this document closes is the measured divergence between standard industrial electrical safety (grounded, copper-wired, EMC-compliant) and the verified behavior of the Aegis-Forge I under combined Carrington GIC + 500 kW induction + 2200°C thermomechanical loading.

    Three specific gaps demand this architecture:

    1. Standard grounding creates the GIC antenna: IEEE 142 / NFPA 70 require equipment grounding conductors. But in a 5000 nT/s event, the ground conductor is the antenna. The measured GIC on Hydro-Québec 1989 was 100 A on neutral conductors. A grounded forge would see 100 A flowing through its "safety ground" into the GaN gate drivers. The gap: grounding for safety vs. grounding as GIC antenna.

    2. Standard EMC assumes copper shielding: CISPR 11 / IEC 61000-4 assume metallic enclosures and shielded cables. But in the forge, a steel cabinet at 2200°C ambient (radiative coupling) with 500 kW of 1–100 kHz magnetic fields becomes a Faraday cage that concentrates eddy currents. The measured field inside PROD-03 coil housing is 39.6 mT at Z8. A steel enclosure would see 50 kW of eddy current heating. The gap: metallic shielding vs. dielectric transparency.

    3. Standard SIL-3 assumes independent channels: IEC 61508 2oo3 voting assumes physical separation. But in the forge, all 3 FBG sensors per zone share: same interrogator, same POF cable tray, same 24 VDC supply, same RTU. A single interrogator failure = common cause = all 3 channels lost. The gap: independent channels vs. shared infrastructure in constrained volume.

    Measured data demanding this approach:

    • PROD-23 GIC ride-through test: 100 A/m Helmholtz field, 30 min — zero spurious trips, zero data loss
    • PROD-10 EMC test: CISPR 11 Class A passed with 20 dB margin — no metal shielding
    • PROD-23 SIS proof test (CT-04): 24 SIL-3 SIFs, PFDavg = 2.3×10⁻³ — meets <10⁻²
    • PROD-25 megger test: All 50+ penetrations >1 GΩ at 500 VDC — no conductive leakage
    • PROD-10 arc flash calc: 0.3 cal/cm² at 18" (process) vs 4.2 cal/cm² (grid) — Cat 0 PPE

    Commitment (The Turn)

    This document makes the following non-negotiable commitments that constrain all downstream documents:

    1. PMMA POF is the only fieldbus — 480+ sensors, 96+ actuators, TSN, PTP, SIS. No copper, no wireless, no powerline. PROD-27 manufacturing must qualify POF draw ($0.08–0.15/m). PROD-28 QA verifies attenuation <0.2 dB/m. PROD-29 operations includes POF inspection. PROD-36/37 architect around this.

    2. Floating secondary + NGR 5A is mandatory — no neutral-earth bond on process side. PROD-27 specifies isolation transformer (Δ-Y, BFRP, 10 kV BIL). PROD-28 verifies ground fault <5 A. PROD-29 includes NGR monitoring. PROD-32 permits require this.

    3. PEX-a for all coolant — no copper pipe, no conductive water path. DI water 18 MΩ·cm maintained. PROD-27 specifies PEX-a circuit. PROD-28 verifies resistivity. PROD-29 includes DI polisher.

    4. 24 SIL-3 SIFs immutable — Table in Appendix C defines safety envelope. PROD-27 manufactures dedicated SIS FPGA boards. PROD-28 executes CT-04 proof tests. PROD-32 requires SIL-3 cert. PROD-39 FAT includes SIF injection. No downgrade without full re-certification.

    5. TSN schedule frozen — 1 ms cycle, 4 slices (SIS/RTU/PLC/SCADA), 100 μs guard band. PROD-27 manufactures TSN switches (BFRP). PROD-28 verifies latency <100 μs. PROD-37 twin sync depends on this.

    6. Air-gap absolute — no IT→OT IP path. Data diode unidirectional (OT→IT) only. PROD-27 installs hardware diode. PROD-28 verifies no reverse traffic. PROD-36/37 architect around this.

    7. PTP <1 μs required — GNSS+OCXO grandmaster, 24h holdover, all nodes boundary clocks. PROD-27 manufactures grandmaster (BFRP). PROD-28 verifies sync. PROD-10/23 resonance tracking depends on this.

    8. BFRP/YInMn Blue glaze as conductive bleed — SRI=115 glaze provides static dissipation path (1 MΩ to earth). PROD-06 specifies glaze. PROD-28 verifies surface resistivity. PROD-25 seismic qualifies glaze adhesion.

    These commitments are the electrical load-bearing walls. PROD-27 (Manufacturing), PROD-28 (QA), PROD-29 (Deployment), PROD-30 (Maintenance), PROD-32 (Compliance), PROD-36 (Cyber-Physical), PROD-37 (Digital Twin), PROD-39 (T&E), FOLLOW-10/11/27/29 build on this foundation. They cannot move the walls.

    Keymaker Heuristic — Implementation Precision

    The Empirical Lock

    The fabrication fidelity gap in Aegis-Forge I electrical safety is the divergence between IEC 61508 / NFPA 70E compliant design and the measured behavior of an all-dielectric control system inside a 500 kW induction furnace at 2200°C during a Carrington storm.

    Three specific locks prevent traditional electrical safety engineering from closing this gap:

    1. Grounding is the vulnerability, not the protection: Every industrial standard (IEEE 142, NFPA 70, IEC 60364) mandates equipment grounding conductors for fault current return and shock protection. But in the forge, the ground conductor becomes the GIC antenna. 5000 nT/s induces >100 V/km. A 50 m ground wire = 5 V common-mode. The GaN gate driver threshold is 6 V. The "safety ground" destroys the safety system. The lock: safety ground as GIC antenna.

    2. EMC shielding requires conductivity — the forge forbids it: CISPR 11 / IEC 61000-4 assume metallic enclosures (steel, aluminum) for radiated emission containment and immunity. But at 2200°C with 500 kW of 1–100 kHz magnetic fields, a steel cabinet becomes an induction heater. The measured B-field at Z8 is 39.6 mT. Eddy current heating in 2 mm steel: P = π²B²f²d²V/6ρ ≈ 50 kW. The cabinet would melt. The lock: metallic shielding as induction heater.

    3. SIL-3 independence assumes no shared infrastructure: IEC 61508 2oo3 voting requires physical separation of sensors, logic solvers, and final elements. But the forge has: 3 FBG sensors sharing 1 interrogator, 3 RTUs sharing 1 TSN ring, 3 SIS FPGAs sharing 1 TSN VLAN, all powered from 1 DC bus. A single interrogator failure = common cause = all 3 channels lost. The lock: shared infrastructure as common cause failure.

    Common thread: Every lock is a standard safety practice that becomes a hazard in the forge's unique electromagnetic-thermal environment. The empirical lock is the sum of all safety practices that invert under Carrington + induction + temperature.

    The Mathematical Key

    The single computational primitive that generates the electrical safety solution is the discrete-time thermal-admittance model executed at 1 kHz on the Zone RTU, which doubles as the GIC/SIF prediction engine:

    $$T_{inner}[k+1] = T_{inner}[k] + \frac{\Delta t}{\rho c V} \left( P_{ind}[k] - h A (T_{inner}[k] - T_{flange}[k]) - \epsilon \sigma A (T_{inner}^4[k] - T_{surr}^4) \right)$$

    Where:

    • $T_{inner}$ = Drum inner surface temperature (virtual sensor, reconstructed from 48 FBG/zone)
    • $P_{ind}$ = Induction power command (from thermal PID + feedforward)
    • $h A$ = Convective conductance to flange (identified online)
    • $\epsilon \sigma A$ = Radiative conductance (dominant >800°C, T⁴ nonlinearity)
    • $\Delta t = 1$ ms (RTU cycle time)

    This one equation, discretized on the ARM Cortex-A53 (Zephyr RTOS, <100 μs compute), is the atomic computation.

    Everything in this document derives from it:

    • GIC Ride-Through (Section 3.3): The model predicts $T_{inner}$ 50 ms ahead. If grid dV/dt > threshold → model projects thermal trajectory → if $dT/dt > 100°C/s$ predicted → pre-emptive ride-through initiation. The same model that controls temperature predicts the thermal consequence of grid loss.
    • SIS Pre-Emptive Trip (Section 8): SIF-00-01 (drum over-temp) uses model prediction: if $T_{inner}[k+50] > T_{lim}$ → trip now, not when FBG reads limit. 50 ms prediction horizon matches SIS response requirement.
    • Resonance Tracking (PROD-10/23): The model's $P_{ind}$ output feeds the power-to-frequency LUT. ZVS maintenance requires knowing thermal load → impedance → frequency shift. The model provides the thermal load estimate.
    • Arc Flash Energy (Section 7): The model's $T_{inner}$ trajectory defines the thermal state during fault clearing. Incident energy calculation uses actual $T_{inner}(t)$ not worst-case.
    • Insulation Aging (Section 11): The model's $T_{flange}$ history feeds Arrhenius aging model for PTFE/PEX-a/BFRP. Predictive maintenance triggers at 80% design life.
    • Digital Twin Sync (PROD-37): The model state vector $[T_{inner}, T_{flange}, P_{ind}, f_{res}]$ published at 10 Hz via OPC-UA/Kafka is the twin's boundary condition.

    The mathematical key is not the PID, not the PLL, not the SIS logic — it is the thermal-admittance model that unifies temperature control, GIC survival, SIS pre-emption, resonance tracking, and digital twin synchronization. If you execute this model correctly at 1 kHz with the right $hA(T)$, $\epsilon\sigma A(T)$, $\rho c V(T)$, you get electrical safety. The SIL-3 logic is just the trip condition on the model output.

    The Turn (Both Directions)

    Theory→History Validation

    The thermal-admittance model predicts historical test data from the CSMFAB0108 development program:

    History→Theory Correction

    Historical anomalies refine the model's constitutive parameters and boundary conditions:

    1. Anomaly: Char growth oscillation at 0.8 Hz, ±15°C (PROD-16 Stage 3, 2026-10). Root cause: Char layer thickness changes thermal resistance → modulates $hA$ → modulates $T_{inner}$ → modulates pyrolysis rate → modulates char growth. Correction: Added char thickness state $\delta_{char}[k]$ to RLS (Recursive Least Squares) estimator. $\delta_{char}[k+1] = \delta_{char}[k] + \alpha (T_{inner}[k] - T_{pyro}) \Delta t$. Model residual dropped from 8°C to 1.2°C RMS.

    2. Anomaly: FBG wavelength drift 0.5 nm/hr at 2200°C (PROD-24 FA-01, 2026-09). Root cause: PMMA FBG annealing at >800°C. Not sensor failure — material physics. Correction: Added reference FBG (unstrained, same thermal path) per zone. Common-mode subtraction: $\Delta\lambda_{meas} = \Delta\lambda_{sense} - \Delta\lambda_{ref}$. Drift reduced to <0.05 nm/hr. Model uses corrected $\Delta\lambda$.

    3. Anomaly: TSN latency spike 2.3 ms during Stage 7 transition (PROD-20, 2026-10). Root cause: PLC SFC transition caused TSN queue congestion on shared VLAN. Correction: Moved SIS to dedicated VLAN 10 with 200 μs time slice. PLC/SCADA on VLAN 20/30. Added local OCXO on each RTU (100 ppb stability). Latency now <80 μs max.

    4. Anomaly: Varactor saturation at 28 V (Z7/Z8 high power) — tuning range exhausted (PROD-10, 2026-10). Root cause: At 350–500 kW, tank impedance shift requires >28 V varactor bias for ZVS. Correction: Added 8-bit switched capacitor bank (coarse) + varactor (fine). Cap bank steps cover 80% of range, varactor covers ±5%. ZVS maintained 99.9% cycles.

    5. Anomaly: PEX-a coolant resistivity drop from 18 MΩ·cm to 2 MΩ·cm after 500 hrs (PROD-10, 2026-10). Root cause: Copper ion leaching from microchannel cold plate (Ni-P coating defect). Correction: Upgraded cold plate to AlSiC with indium foil TIM (PROD-25 Section 6.2). Resistivity stable >15 MΩ·cm at 1000 hrs.

    The mathematical key absorbs history — each anomaly tightens a model parameter ($hA$, $\epsilon\sigma A$, $\rho c V$), adds a state ($\delta_{char}$, reference FBG), or restructures a boundary condition (TSN VLAN, cap bank, cold plate material). The primitive $T_{inner}[k+1] = f(T_{inner}[k], P_{ind}[k], \text{params}[k])$ remains structurally invariant. This is the signature of a correct primitive: it extends, it does not rewrite.

    El Segundo Heuristic — Operational Excellence

    Mirror (Self-Reflection)

    How does the fabricator observe their own electrical fabrication? The Aegis-Forge I embeds four nested electrical metrology loops — the machine watches its own electrical integrity at the scale of the phenomenon.

    Level 0 — Gate-Level Witness (FPGA, 100 kHz)

    What the FPGA sees:

    • Desaturation Detect: GaN $V_{DS}$ monitored at 10 ns resolution. If $V_{DS} > 10$ V during on-state → shoot-through → instant leg shutdown (<100 ns). No software, no network — pure hardware.
    • ZVS Timestamp: Switch voltage zero-crossing vs. gate command. Phase error $\phi_{err} = t_{V_{DS}=0} - t_{gate\_on}$. Target: $\phi_{err} < 5$ ns. Logged every cycle (100 kHz).
    • Current Sense: 16-bit ADC at 1 MHz on DC link shunt. Harmonic analysis (FFT 512 pts) → detects bearing wear, coil short, capacitor degradation.
    • Health Output: Per-cycle status word on POF: ZVS_OK DESAT_OKCURRENT_OK TEMP_OK. SCADA aggregates at 10 Hz.

    Self-reflection logic: If ZVS_OK < 99.9% over 1000 cycles → RTU reduces power 10%, logs degradation. If DESAT_OK < 100% → instant SIF trip. The FPGA witnesses its own switching integrity every 10 μs.

    Level 1 — Thermal Reconstruction (RTU, 1 kHz)

    What the RTU sees:

    • 48 FBG Inputs/Zone: 384 temperatures @ 125 Hz each via WDM+TDM. Wavelength → temperature conversion: $T = (\lambda - \lambda_{ref}) / 0.15$ nm/°C.
    • Virtual Sensor: Runs the thermal-admittance model (Section 2 Mathematical Key) at 1 kHz. Inputs: 48 FBG temps, power command, flange temps. Output: $T_{inner}$ prediction ±5°C at 2200°C.
    • Model Residual: $r[k] = T_{FBG,flange}[k] - T_{model,flange}[k]$. If $r > 2°C$ RMS → re-identification triggered (RLS updates $hA$, $\epsilon\sigma A$).
    • SIF Prediction: Projects $T_{inner}[k+50]$ (50 ms ahead). If predicted > limit → pre-emptive SIF trip.

    Self-reflection logic: The RTU witnesses the thermal state of its zone at 1 ms resolution. It compares measured vs. predicted, identifies model drift, and predicts safety violations before they occur. The model is the mirror — it reflects the zone's thermal reality back to the controller.

    Level 2 — Cascade Consistency (PLC, 100 Hz)

    What the PLC sees:

    • Mass-Energy Balance: $\sum \dot{m}_{in} - \sum \dot{m}_{out} = dM/dt$. XRF/LIBS composition × flow rate = elemental flow. Closure >99.5%/batch or investigation flag.
    • Stage Interlock Status: All 72 SIFs (24 SIL-3, 12 SIL-2, 36 SIL-1) evaluated every 1 ms (SIS) / 10 ms (PLC). Status matrix published on TSN VLAN 10.
    • Recipe Execution: ISA-88 recipe state machine. Current segment, time remaining, setpoint trajectory. Deviation >5% → alarm.
    • Feedforward to Downstream: Elemental composition, gas analysis, thermal state passed to next stage PLC.

    Self-reflection logic: The PLC witnesses the stage's material and energy transformation. It verifies conservation laws hold, checks recipe adherence, and ensures downstream stages receive accurate feedforward. The mass-energy balance is the mirror — it reflects the stage's process reality.

    Level 3 — Digital Twin Shadow (SCADA → PROD-37, 10 Hz)

    What the Twin sees:

    • Full State Vector: 512-core HPC runs same thermal-admittance model + CFD (PROD-24) + FEA (PROD-25) + electromagnetics (PROD-03). Inputs: all 480 sensor streams + 96 actuator commands.
    • ML Autoencoder (FOLLOW-29): Trained on 10,000 nominal batches. Encodes 1000-dimensional state to 32 latent dims. Reconstruction error >3σ → anomaly flag.
    • Predictive Suggestions: Twin simulates next 100 batches with PID gain variations, flux rate adjustments, RPM profiles. Suggests optimal setpoints to SCADA.
    • Fleet Learning: Aggregates across all Forges (PROD-37 fleet twin). Transfers learned corrections.

    Self-reflection logic: The digital twin witnesses the entire forge's electro-thermal-mechanical state. It runs higher-fidelity models than real-time allows, detects anomalies the local controllers miss, and proposes optimizations. The twin is the mirror at system scale.

    The Mirror Protocol (Recursive)

    TierFrequencyScopeAction -------------------------------- Tier 0 (Gate)100 kHzSingle switch → ZVS/desatFPGA hardware trip Tier 1 (Thermal)1 kHzZone → $T_{inner}$ predictionRTU power limit / SIF pre-trip Tier 2 (Cascade)100 HzStage → mass-energy balancePLC alarm / feedforward adjust Tier 3 (Twin)10 HzForge → ML anomaly / optimizationSCADA setpoint suggestion Tier 4 (Fleet)ContinuousFleet → model transferPROD-37 updates all Forges

    The mirror is not passive — it closes the loop. Every tier feeds the next: gate health → thermal model accuracy → cascade balance → twin prediction → fleet optimization. The fabricator (the forge) watches its own electrical fabrication at every scale.

    Participation (Witness)

    How does the inside operator witness the electrical phenomenon into existence? At what points must human judgment authorize electrical consequence?

    Critical Participation Gates

    Gate 1: Batch Recipe Authorization — Electrical Load Profile (PROD-29 Section 4.1)

    • Action: Feedstock UUID scanned → Category A–D → Operator confirms recipe. Recipe defines 8-zone power profile (0–500 kW each), frequency ladder, thermal ramp rates.
    • Witness requirement: Operator verifies recipe power profile matches feedstock composition. Category A (PCBs) = high Z6/Z7 power. Category C (batteries) = high Z3/Z4 power. Wrong profile = thermal runaway or incomplete separation.
    • Why human: Feedstock composition has irreducible variability (Category A: 15–25% Cu, 5–15% Fe, 0.1–0.5% PM). No sensor measures "Category A-ness" — only composition. Operator judgment maps composition to recipe.
    • Cognitive checkpoint: "Does this power profile match what I see in the feed?" — pattern recognition of feedstock vs. recipe.

    Gate 2: Stage Transition Gate — Electrical State Verification (PROD-29 Section 4.3)

    • Action: Stage complete → Shift Lead reviews: energy delivered vs. planned, gas composition vs. setpoint, SIF events, anomaly flags, thermal model residuals.
    • Witness requirement: For Stage 4: visual In-grade confirmation (pyrometer + XRF at Port 4A). For Stage 6: H₂ <4% verification (ZrO₂ pO₂ probe) before Port 6B open. For Stage 8: SiO₂ condenser flow verification (mass spec).
    • Why human: SIF events are recorded but not interpreted. A "cooling water loss" SIF that self-cleared in 50 s might indicate pump cavitation — operator judges if pump needs replacement. Anomaly flags are data — operator judges significance.
    • Cognitive checkpoint: "Is the electrical state clean for the next stage?" — synthesis of energy, gas, SIF, anomaly data.

    Gate 3: SIF Bypass Authorization — Organizational Risk Acceptance (PROD-29 Section 5.2)

    • Action: Dual-key (Shift Lead + Safety Engineer), time-limited (4 hr max), blockchain-audited (Hyperledger Fabric, PROD-37).
    • Witness requirement: Both signatories review: which SIF, why bypass, compensating measures, risk assessment, expiration time. Blockchain record immutable.
    • Why human: Risk acceptance is organizational, not algorithmic. No mathematical function accepts "we'll run with SIF-00-07 bypassed because NGR monitor is drifting." Human judgment weighs production loss vs. safety margin.
    • Cognitive checkpoint: "Do I accept this risk for this duration with these compensations?" — explicit risk acceptance.

    Gate 4: Carrington Ride-Through Exit — Post-Storm Recovery (PROD-29 Section 5.4)

    • Action: Grid stable 30 min → Operator verifies: drum thermal state (no shock >100°C/s), SIF health (all 24 SIL-3 OK), FBG/PTP/TSN sync, LiFePO₄ charge >80%. Authorizes staged grid reconnect with utility coordination.
    • Witness requirement: Thermal shock check is critical — drum at 2200°C, grid reconnect causes inrush. If drum cooled >100°C/s during island, thermal stress could crack ZrB₂-SiC. Operator verifies model-predicted $dT/dt$ < 100°C/s.
    • Why human: Grid coordination requires utility communication (voice, not data diode). Thermal shock judgment combines model prediction + operator experience. No algorithm coordinates with utility dispatcher.
    • Cognitive checkpoint: "Did the forge survive the storm intact?" — holistic electrical-thermal survival judgment.

    Gate 5: FAT/SAT Sign-Off — Electrical Qualification Acceptance (PROD-39)

    • Action: Lead Electrical Engineer witnesses: CT-01 rotordynamics, CT-02 hydrotest, CT-03 megger/hipot, CT-04 SIF proof, CT-05 resonance, CT-06 FBG cal, CT-07 GIC ride-through, CT-08 thermal cycle, CT-09 seismic, CT-10 integrated run.
    • Witness requirement: Reviews all 10 test reports, signs each. Any deviation from spec → NCR (PROD-28) → root cause → re-test.
    • Why human: Test data is necessary but not sufficient. Engineer judges: "Is the 2.3 ms TSN latency spike in CT-05 acceptable?" (Yes, <100 μs guard band). "Is the 0.5 pC PD on XFMR acceptable?" (Yes, <5 pC limit). Data + judgment = sign-off.
    • Cognitive checkpoint: "Does this electrical system meet spec in the real world?" — professional engineering judgment.

    The Participation Principle

    The operator witnesses the electrical system into existence at every irreversible authorization point where: 1. Composition-to-recipe mapping has irreducible variability (feedstock category → power profile) 2. Risk acceptance is organizational, not algorithmic (SIF bypass, ride-through exit) 3. Multi-party coordination is required (utility reconnect, FAT sign-off) 4. Model prediction needs experiential validation (thermal shock, anomaly significance)

    Automation executes the physics; humans authorize the consequences. The forge controls the electrons; the operator witnesses the electrons becoming safe operation.

    The Recursive Guarantee

    The protocol is recursive because the output of each level becomes the input validation for the next level:

    • Component HIL (Level 0) → Module ATP (Level 1)
    • Module ATP (Level 1) → Integration ITF (Level 2)
    • Integration ITF (Level 2) → FAT ATP (Level 3)
    • FAT ATP (Level 3) → SAT ATP (Level 4)
    • Operational trends (Level 4) → Component HIL updates (Level 0)

    This is the fractal pattern: Stimulate at scale N → Observe at scale N → Compare at scale N → Act at scale N → Feedback to scale N-1 and N+1. The same Stimulate→Observe→Compare→Act logic applies whether N = gate, switch, zone, stage, forge, or fleet.

    The protocol guarantees fidelity because it never assumes — it always stimulates and observes against the mathematical key (thermal-admittance model) and validates against the empirical lock (test data). If the model predicts the test, and the test corrects the model, the recursion converges. If it diverges, the protocol catches it at the next level.

    No scale is exempt. The gate is stimulated like the forge. The forge is validated like the gate. The operator participates at every authorization boundary. The machine mirrors itself at every electrical metrology tier. This is the recursive sequence that guarantees the Aegis-Forge I electrical system does not just meet code — it survives the storm.

    All-Dielectric Field Layer, Floating Power Architecture, HEMP/GIC/EMP Protection, Arc Flash Mitigation

    Document Number: CSMFAB000000000126 (PROD-26) Series: Aegis-Forge Thermal Cascade Inductive Material Separator (TCIMS) Date: November 2026 Classification: CSMFAB Internal — Engineering Specification Revision: 1.0

    1. Electrical Safety Architecture

    1.1 Design Philosophy

    The Aegis-Forge I electrical safety architecture is governed by a single irreducible principle: no conductive path shall exist between the process zone (2200°C, 500 kW induction, Carrington-class GIC environment) and earth ground. This constraint forces the entire field layer — 480+ sensors, 96+ actuators, 8 GaN inverter modules — to communicate and be powered through all-dielectric media: PMMA plastic optical fiber (POF) for signals, PEX-a tubing for coolant, BFRP housings for enclosures, ceramic bushings for penetrations.

    Three non-negotiable constraints define the architecture:

    ConstraintImplementationVerification ------------------------------------------ Zero conductive penetrationPMMA POF only fieldbus (980 μm core), PEX-a coolant, BFRP enclosures, ZrO₂/Al₂O₃ bushingsMegger >10 GΩ at 500 VDC between process and earth Floating power distributionIsolation transformer (Δ-Y, floating secondary), NGR 5A, no neutral-earth bondGround fault current <5 A under any single fault Carrington GIC immunity5000 nT/s → <1 V induced on POF; ride-through mode (5 ms cap → 10 ms island → LiFePO₄)Helmholtz coil test 100 A/m, no spurious trips

    Consequences of violation: A single copper wire crossing the pressure boundary becomes a GIC antenna. 5000 nT/s induces >100 V/km. At 50 m cable length: >5 V common-mode on a GaN gate driver (6 V threshold) = destruction. At 100 V common-mode on FBG interrogator = permanent damage. The all-dielectric architecture is not a preference — it is the only topology that survives.

    9. Grounding & Bonding — IEEE Std 142 / IEEE Std 1100

    9.1 Grounding Philosophy

    Single-Point Ground at Substation Only. No ground reference anywhere in the process zone. All "grounding" inside the forge is equipotential bonding via 1 MΩ bleed resistors for static dissipation only.

       ▼
Neutral Grounding Resistor (5 A, 400 V) → Earth
       │
       ├──► Transformer Tank (BFRP, no metal)
       ├──► Cable Trays (BFRP, 1 MΩ bleed)
       ├──► Enclosures (BFRP, 1 MΩ bleed)
       ├──► Cooling Water (PEX-a, DI water 18 MΩ·cm)
       └──► Structure (BFRP frame, no steel)
