    5. Curriculum Modules — Foundation (Safety, Materials, Physics)

    5.1 Module F-01: Industrial Safety & Carrington Immunity (16 hrs)

    Topics:

    • Forge hazard identification: Thermal (2200°C), EMF (500 kW induction), Chemical (H₂, NaHCO₃, HCl), Pressure (10 bar), Radiation (XRF/LIBS)
    • GIC/EMP threat: Carrington storm physics, 5000 nT/s → >100 A/km induction, Faraday cage integrity, LiFePO₄ UPS backup
    • Zero-metal safety: No conductive tools in hot zone, PMMA POF handling, BFRP tooling, PEEK CF40 fasteners
    • Emergency response: E-stop locations, evacuation routes, refuge stations, comms protocols

    Assessment: Written (20 questions, 80% pass) + Practical (E-stop drill, evacuation <30 sec)

    5.2 Module F-02: Zero-Metal Materials Science (16 hrs)

    Topics:

    • ZrB₂-SiC drum: Flash sintering, 3 liner zones, 8 ports, FBG embedding (PROD-04)
    • BFRP vessel: Filament winding, Elium® resin, 50 mm aerogel, YInMn glaze (PROD-06)
    • MAX Phase Ti₃AlC₂: Port actuators, EMI shields, thermal conductivity (PROD-09, FOLLOW-04)
    • Basalt fiber/Elium®: Roving specs, sizing, solvolysis recovery (PROD-12, 33)
    • Critical minerals: In, REE, Co, Zr, Nb — properties, handling, ITAR (PROD-12, 33)

    Assessment: Written (25 questions) + Material identification lab (10 samples blind)

    5.3 Module F-03: Thermal-Acoustic-Inductive Physics (24 hrs)

    Topics:

    • Stage 0: Acoustic liberation (KNbO₃-BaTiO₃ transducers, 20-200 Hz + 40 kHz, PROD-05)
    • Stage 1: IR drying (90°C, moisture <1%, PROD-14)
    • Stage 2: Polymer melt centrifuge (250°C, density stratification, PROD-15)
    • Stage 3: Pyrolysis/char (450°C, thermoset decomposition, PROD-16)
    • Stage 4: Indium-First (160°C, 400 RPM, centrifugal separation, PROD-17)
    • Stage 5: Aluminum window (660-720°C, Mg removal flux, PROD-18)
    • Stage 6: Copper/PM (1085-1200°C, anode casting, PROD-19)
    • Stage 7: Ferrous/REE (1200-1600°C, dual-port REE, PROD-20)
    • Stage 8: Zircon dissociation (1676°C, 3Y-TZP flash sinter, PROD-21)

    Assessment: Written (30 questions) + Simulator: identify stage from thermal/profile data

    6. Curriculum Modules — Systems (Induction, Cascade, Control, QA)

    6.1 Module S-01: Induction Power Electronics (24 hrs)

    Topics:

    • GaN Class E inverters (GS66516T), ZVS at 100 kHz → 1 kHz (PROD-10)
    • FBG sensors: WDM+TDM, 384 ch @ 125 Hz, PMMA POF (PROD-10, FOLLOW-11)
    • PID ±5°C + resonance tracking, varactor bias, cap bank (PROD-10, 23)
    • Microchannel cold plates, liquid cooling, junction-to-case thermal (PROD-10, FOLLOW-10)
    • SIL-3 gate drive: desat detect 10 ns, 2oo3 voting (PROD-23, 28)

    Assessment: Simulator — tune Zone 3 PID to ±2°C at 50 kHz, maintain ZVS >99.9%

    6.2 Module S-02: Distributed Control Architecture (24 hrs)

    Topics:

    • L0 FPGA: Gate drive, desat, ZVS, current sense at 100 kHz (PROD-23)
    • L1 RTU: ARM Cortex-A53, 1 kHz thermal-admittance model, FBG acquisition (PROD-23)
    • L2 PLC: IEC 61131-3, 100 Hz cascade, interlocks, recipe (ISA-88), carousel (PROD-23)
    • L3 SCADA: Linux dual, 10 Hz historian, alarms, batch, twin sync (PROD-23, 29, 37)
    • TSN/PTP: 1 Gbps dual-ring, 4 VLANs, <1 μs sync, FRER (PROD-23, FOLLOW-11)

    Assessment: Practical — configure TSN schedule, verify PTP <1 μs, inject L0 desat

    6.3 Module S-03: SIL-3 Safety Instrumented Functions (16 hrs)

    Topics:

    • 24 SIFs: 3 per zone × 8 zones (overtemp, overpressure, vibration, GIC, comms loss)
    • 2oo3 voting on independent sensors, <50 ms trip, PFD_avg <1×10⁻³ (PROD-28)
    • CT-04 proof test: full injection sequence, SOE verification (PROD-28)
    • SIF bypass: dual-key (SL + Safety Eng), 4 hr max, blockchain audit (PROD-28)
    • SIS proof test interval: quarterly partial-stroke, annual full (PROD-30)

    Assessment: Oral board — walk through CT-04 sequence, justify bypass decision

    6.4 Module S-04: Quality Assurance & NDT (16 hrs)

    Topics:

    • Zero-metal NDT: UT PA (5 MHz, 64-element), CT (200 μm), AE (R15α), IR, VT (PROD-28)
    • FBG-as-primary-metrology: 384 ch @ 125 Hz, drift <0.5%/1000 hrs (PROD-28)
    • Recursive Bayesian health update: Λ > 10 → auto-NCR (PROD-28 Keymaker Key)
    • QR + Hyperledger traceability: UUID chain, immutable record (PROD-28, 38)
    • Four human witness gates: SG-2, SG-3, CT-04, SAT-05 (PROD-28)

    Assessment: Practical — UT PA on ZrB₂-SiC coupon, interpret AE Felicity ratio

    7. Curriculum Modules — Operations (Startup, Steady State, Shutdown, Emergency)

    7.1 Module O-01: Cold Startup Sequence (16 hrs)

    Procedure (PROD-29): 1. Facility systems: HVAC, N₂/Ar/He, cooling water, LiFePO₄ UPS, TSN/PTP 2. SIS proof test (CT-04 partial): verify 24 SIFs trip <50 ms 3. FBG calibration check (CT-06): 5 reference temps, all 384 ch R² >0.999 4. Induction zones cold: verify ZVS at 100 kHz, FBG baseline, varactor sweep 5. Drum drive: piezo motor 0→500 RPM, FBG strain baseline 6. Gas systems: MFC zero/span, leak check, purge sequences 7. SCADA: recipe load (ISA-88 XML), batch UUID generation, twin sync

    Assessment: Simulator — execute cold startup to "Ready for Feed" in <90 min

    7.2 Module O-02: Hot Commissioning & Steady State (24 hrs)

    Procedure (PROD-29): 1. Feed introduction: Category A-D per PROD-13, LIBS verify, MFC setpoints 2. Stage 0-1: Acoustic liberation → IR drying, monitor FBG drum thermal 3. Stage 2-3: Polymer melt → pyrolysis, centrifuge RPM, port valve sequence 4. Stage 4-5: Indium-First → Al window, centrifugal density stratification 5. Stage 6-7: Copper/PM → Ferrous/REE, dual-port REE separation 6. Stage 8: Zircon dissociation, 3Y-TZP flash sinter, drum material loop 7. Continuous: Blend ratio MFC (±2%), off-gas MS, slug mass spec, energy balance

    Assessment: Simulator — run 8-hour steady state, zero SIF trips, >99% mass balance

    7.3 Module O-03: Normal & Emergency Shutdown (16 hrs)

    Normal Shutdown: 1. Feed stop → cascade drain (30 min), induction ramp down (zone 8→1) 2. Gas purge: N₂ all lines, H₂ isolation, cooling maintain 3. Drum stop: 500→0 RPM, quench nozzles if >200°C 4. SIF status: verify all armed, log final state

    Emergency Shutdown (E-Stop): 1. Optical E-stop loop broken → <1 ms all GaN gates off, MFCs close 2. LiFePO₄ UPS: SIS + SCADA + TSN + PTP on backup indefinite 3. H₂ isolation: pneumatic valves fail-safe closed (<50 ms) 4. Post-E-stop: SIF health check, FBG thermal shock check, twin state capture

    Assessment: Simulator — E-stop at Stage 6 peak, verify all safety functions <50 ms

    7.4 Module O-04: Emergency Response & Carrington Ride-Through (16 hrs)

    Scenarios:

    • Carrington GIC Storm: 5 ms grid disconnect, 10 ms island mode, 30 min grid stable → staged reconnect (PROD-23, 26)
    • Induction Zone Fault: GaN desat → L0 FPGA trip, L1 RTU isolates zone, L2 PLC cascade hold
    • Drum Crack (AE detection): Felicity ratio <1.0 → L1 RTU alerts, L2 PLC initiates controlled cool-down
    • H₂ Leak: MS detection → SIF trip, N₂ purge, evacuation if >4% LEL
    • TSN Partition: FRER failover, PTP holdover (24 hr OCXO), L3 SCADA alarm

    Assessment: Tabletop + Simulator — Carrington scenario, verbal walkthrough of SL decisions

    8. Curriculum Modules — Maintenance (PM, CBM, Spares, Tooling)

    8.1 Module M-01: Preventive Maintenance Execution (24 hrs)

    PM Schedule (PROD-30):

    • Daily (Shift): FBG health (Λ check), AE cluster review, MFC zero/span, crate cycle count
    • Weekly: Drum bearing vibration trend, coil cold plate flow, quench nozzle pattern
    • Monthly (168 hrs): Port valve actuation test, flux injector calibration, carousel index
    • Quarterly (500 hrs): FBG full calibration (CT-06), SIF partial-stroke, CT porosity scan
    • Annual (2000 hrs): Drum UT PA + CT, vessel hydrotest (8 bar), TSN cable audit

    Zero-Metal Tooling: BFRP torque wrenches, PEEK CF40 sockets, ceramic feeler gauges, PMMA POF strippers

    Assessment: Practical — execute monthly PM on Zone 3 RTU + Port 4 valve in <4 hrs

    8.2 Module M-02: Condition-Based Maintenance (CBM) (16 hrs)

    CBM Data Sources (PROD-30, 37):

    • FBG: 384 ch @ 125 Hz → drift, strain, thermal gradient
    • AE: 16 ch @ 100 kHz → Felicity ratio, hit location, cluster analysis
    • Vibration: Drum bearings, gearbox → spectral trends, bearing defect frequencies
    • Process: XRF/LIBS composition trends, energy balance deviation, mass balance closure

    Decision Logic:

    • Λ > 10 (Bayesian) → auto-NCR → MT dispatch
    • Trend >3σ from fleet baseline (PROD-37 twin) → predictive work order
    • CT-06 FBG cal drift >0.5%/1000 hrs → schedule replacement at next outage

    Assessment: Simulator — interpret CBM dashboard, generate work order, justify priority

    8.3 Module M-03: Spares Management & Critical Parts (8 hrs)

    Spares Classification (PROD-30, 33):

    • Critical (A): 100% on-site + 1 regional + 1 factory (drum, vessel, modules, FBG, TSN, PTP)
    • Essential (B): 1 regional + 1 factory (graphite die, mandrel, ZrO₂ bolts, molds, isolators)
    • Normal (C): Factory warehouse (PEX-a, NaHCO₃, carbon, gases, PEEK seals)
    • Phoenix (P): Depot network + Forge buffer (Elium® monomer, basalt, hydroxides)

    Process: Kanban pull → QR scan → condition check (FBG/AE active) → install → return core

    Assessment: Written — spares classification, Kanban execution, core return procedure

    9. Curriculum Modules — Phoenix Depot Operations (Cross-Training)

    9.1 Module P-01: Depot Disassembly & Classification (16 hrs)

    Process (PROD-22, 33): 1. Tertiary Hub: QR scan return → Category D1-D7 → BFRP crate load (500 kg, 80% fill min) 2. Secondary Hub: Pre-sort, battery/capacitor discharge (SOC log), crate consolidate 3. Primary Hub: Auto disassembly cell (6-axis + vision, 15 min/product):

    • Step 1: Electronic/optical extraction (2 min) → PCBs, sensors, LoRa → Stage 0 or refurb
    • Step 2: Hardware removal (3 min) → PEEK CF40, ZrO₂, Ti₃AlC₂ → ultrasonic clean → re-use
    • Step 3: BFRP solvolysis (120 min batch) → 350°C, 2h, N₂ → Elium® monomer + basalt fiber
    • Step 4: Ceramic core processing (15 min) → crush → mill → hydromet feed
    • Step 5: Critical mineral glaze recovery (30 min) → ionic liquid extraction

    LIBS/XRF Classification: Every Primary hub runs 100% LIBS/XRF on disassembly output → feeds CMF-RQT M_return vector real-time.

    Assessment: Practical — operate disassembly cell sim, classify 10 returns via LIBS, log crate UUID

    9.2 Module P-02: Solvolysis & Material Recovery (16 hrs)

    Solvolysis Reactor Operation:

    • Elium® depolymerization: 350°C, 2h, 15 bar N₂, 500L reactor
    • Monomer recovery: MMA >99%, glycol >98% → distillation → Elium® reformulation
    • Basalt fiber: 95% yield, 15-20 μm diameter retained → BFRP pultrusion (FOLLOW-05)
    • Crate wash: Closed-loop water, 99% recycle → BFRP crate redeploy (500 cycles)

    Hydrometallurgy Interface:

    • Zr/Y hydroxide gel → calcination → 3Y-TZP powder (Stage 8 loop)
    • In 99.9% (YInMn), Y 98% (YSZ), Co 98% (electroplated) → Forge re-entry

    Assessment: Simulator — run solvolysis batch, verify monomer purity, calculate fiber yield

    9.3 Module P-03: Blend Ratio MFC & Depot Logistics (8 hrs)

    Blend Ratio Control (PROD-22, 31, 33):

    • CMF-RQT computes P_blend ∈ [0.4, 0.6] from M_virgin, M_return, Q_gen, Γ_stage
    • MFC adjusts ±2% tolerance via Stage 0-8 gate thresholds
    • Gate fee economics: higher fee → higher EOL blend → more In/REE/Co recovery (PROD-31)

    Depot Logistics (PROD-33):

    • VRP optimization: Clarke-Wright + 2-opt, minimize Σ(distance × carbon)
    • Electric Class 8 (500 km) Secondary→Primary; Diesel hybrid Tertiary→Secondary
    • Crate turnaround: 14 days (return → clean → redeploy)
    • Carbon intensity: 0.08 kg CO₂e/ton-km (electric) vs 0.22 (diesel)

    Assessment: Simulator — adjust P_blend for In spike in D4 stream, verify Stage 4 recovery

    Heuristic Intro (Combined): PROD-34

    Combined Heuristic Introduction

    PROD-34 Training & Certification

    Carrington Storm Motors Forge — Aegis-Forge I Thermal Cascade Inductive Material Separator

    Williams Heuristic — Architectural Clarity

    Constraint (The Lock)

    The Forge cannot be operated by conventional industrial training. A 2200°C induction furnace with 384 dielectric FBG sensors, GaN inverters at 100 kHz, SIL-3 SIFs on TSN, and a Phoenix Protocol circular supply chain has no precedent in any training curriculum. Conventional training assumes: (a) metal sensors (thermocouples, strain gauges) with backup redundancy, (b) electrical safety (lockout/tagout on copper conductors), (c) linear process flow (feedstock → product), (d) specialist roles (operator ≠ maintenance ≠ QA). The Forge violates all four: sensors are photonics in glass fiber, safety is optical E-stop loops, flow is recursive (EOL → feedstock), and every role must cross-train on the full CMF-RQT loop. The constraint is physics — an operator who cannot witness the FBG wavelength shift at 125 Hz and connect it to the thermal-admittance model running at 1 kHz on the Zone RTU will trip the SIF or miss the anomaly.

    Necessity (The Key)

    The empirical gap is the absence of any training program that develops sensory-motor coupling to a zero-metal, all-dielectric, recursively circular industrial process. No existing curriculum teaches: (a) FBG wavelength as primary metrology (not backup), (b) ISA-88 recipe execution on a TSN-scheduled PLC with PTP <1 μs, (c) SIL-3 SIF bypass as a dual-key human judgment gate, (d) Phoenix depot disassembly/solvolysis as part of Forge operator competency, (e) Carrington storm ride-through as a routine scenario requiring 5 ms island transition. The solution is inevitable because the Forge's physics demands it: the same operator who authorizes the Stage 4 indium-first discharge at 160°C must also classify the EOL return that feeds that indium at the depot. The CMF-RQT tensor (PROD-33) makes this recursive — training must close the loop.

    Commitment (The Turn)

    This document commits to three non-negotiables: 1. 400-hour Apprentice certification with mandatory 40-hour Phoenix Depot cross-training — no Forge operator certifies without operating the disassembly cell, solvolysis reactor, and LIBS classifier that feed their cascade. 2. Simulator fidelity at 95% physics validated against CSMFAB0108 test data — training scenarios are not scripted; they are generated by the PROD-37 digital twin from fleet anomaly data (FOLLOW-29 ML autoencoder). 3. Four cognitive authorization gates (SG-2, SG-3, CT-04, SAT-05) as practical assessment — no written exam substitutes for witnessing the flange torque ceremony, FBG calibration verification, SIS proof test, or first hot slug pour.

    These commitments are irreversible. They define the Forge's human capital architecture. Any deviation requires SCSC unanimous approval and re-validation of the SIL-3 SIF proof test (CT-04) which is the gate to hot commissioning.

    Keymaker Heuristic — Implementation Precision

    The Empirical Lock

    Fabrication fidelity gap: Conventional industrial training programs — OSHA 30-hr, NCCER craft, ISA CAP, vendor-specific — assume: (a) metallic sensor infrastructure with electrical redundancy, (b) linear process flow with defined start/end, (c) role specialization (operator vs. maintainer vs. inspector), (d) classroom + OJT model with competency checklists. They cannot model: (a) FBG wavelength drift as the only in-process temperature verification (no thermocouple backup), (b) recursive CMF-RQT loop where EOL return composition variability (±15% In) changes the Stage 4 thermal profile in real-time, (c) SIL-3 SIF bypass as a human judgment gate that no algorithm can automate, (d) Carrington storm as a routine operational scenario requiring 5 ms island transition. The lock is that no existing training LMS computes the Forge's human-in-the-loop physics.

    The Mathematical Key

    The single computational primitive is the Recursive Competency Tensor (RCT): 
    RCT[K, S, B, J, D, Φ_role, Ψ_scenario, Ω_fleet]


    K ∈ ℝ⁵⁺ : Knowledge vector (physics, systems, procedures, regulations, CMF-RQT)
S ∈ ℝ⁵⁺ : Skill vector (RTU, PLC, SCADA, NDT, depot equipment)
B ∈ ℝ³⁺ : Behavior vector (adherence, communication, safety culture)
J ∈ ℝ⁴⁺ : Judgment vector (stage gate, SIF bypass, Carrington exit, blend ratio)
D ∈ ℝ³⁺ : Digital vector (twin interaction, cyber hygiene, simulator)
Φ_role ∈ {FO, DT, MT, QI, SL} : Role projection operator
Ψ_scenario ∈ ℝ⁵⁰⁺ : Scenario tensor (normal, degraded, emergency, Carrington, Phoenix)
Ω_fleet ∈ ℝᴺ : Fleet anomaly tensor (PROD-37 digital twin ML autoencoder output)

    This tensor generates the entire training program: curriculum hours, scenario library, assessment methods, certification pathways, recertification triggers, cross-training requirements. Every hour in this document is a projection of RCT evaluated at role × scenario × fleet state.

    The atomic computation is likelihood ratio test for judgment competency:

    Λ_J = P(operator_decision expert_decision) / P(operator_decision novice_decision)

    Threshold Λ_J > 10 at Gates SG-2, SG-3, CT-04, SAT-05 certifies Journeyman judgment. This runs in the oral board simulator where the digital twin presents the scenario and the operator's decision is compared to the expert policy (derived from fleet history).

    The Turn (Both Directions)

    Theory → History Validation:

    • RCT predicts 400 hr Apprentice → matches PROD-27 FA data (3 drums, 3 vessels, 8 modules require 350-420 hrs supervised)
    • RCT predicts 50+ simulator scenarios → matches PROD-24 V&V (500 kW step, ZVS lock, SIF trip, char oscillation, GIC ride-through)
    • RCT predicts mandatory Phoenix cross-training → matches PROD-22 depot network (65 hubs, 3500 ton/yr Year 3)
    • RCT predicts 95% simulator fidelity → matches PROD-24 thermal model validation (42 s predicted vs 45 s measured)
    • RCT predicts Λ_J > 10 at SG-2 → matches PROD-28 flange torque ceremony (AE silence + tactile confirmation)

    History → Theory Validation:

    • CSMFAB0108 test data: 2 operators required 380 hrs to independent operation → validates RCT K+S hours
    • PROD-27 FA: 3 drum generations showed FBG drift pattern learned only by doing → validates RCT S-04 practical requirement
    • PROD-28 CT-04: 24 SIFs trip <50 ms only when SL witnesses SOE alignment → validates RCT J-02 oral board
    • PROD-23 Carrington sim: 5 ms island transition only with trained SL → validates RCT O-04 scenario
    • PROD-33 depot ops: 14-day crate turnaround requires DT who knows Forge Stage 0-8 → validates RCT cross-training

    The primitive is validated. The training program is not a curriculum — it is the physical manifestation of RCT evaluated across 5 roles, 50+ scenarios, 4 certification levels, and infinite fleet anomaly generations.

    El Segundo Heuristic — Operational Excellence

    Mirror (Self-Reflection)

    How does the fabricator observe their own fabrication? The Forge's training program is instrumented at every node with the same rigor as the thermal cascade:
    • Knowledge Assessment: Written exams proctored on air-gapped SCADA workstations, questions drawn from PROD-02, 03, 10, 23, 28 question banks (500+ items, version-controlled in Git via PROD-38). Item response theory (IRT) calibrates difficulty; >3σ deviation from fleet mean triggers curriculum review.
    • Skill Assessment: Practical sign-offs recorded via QR on DQR (Hyperledger). Instructor scans operator badge + task badge → timestamp + GPS + sensor data (FBG strain on tool, IR on workpiece). No paper sign-offs — the act of signing is the sensor record.
    • Simulator Telemetry: Every scenario run streams 200+ parameters (PID gains, SIF states, FBG wavelengths, MFC flows, twin health Λ) to PROD-37 at 10 Hz. ML autoencoder (FOLLOW-29) flags >3σ deviation from expert policy → auto-generates remediation scenario.
    • Judgment Assessment: Oral board recorded (audio + HMI screen capture) → transcribed → NLP analyzed for decision logic patterns. Expert vs. novice classification feeds RCT Ω_fleet tensor.
    • Behavioral Observation: 90-day log via shift handover QR scans. Each handover: outgoing scans incoming badge → 5-question safety culture pulse (Likert) → sentiment analysis trends.

    The fabricator sees the training program as a distributed sensor network. Every assessment is a measurement. Every measurement updates RCT. Every RCT update adjusts curriculum hours, scenario weights, recertification triggers.

    Participation (Witness)

    How does the inside operator witness the phenomenon into existence? The training operator does not "instruct" — they witness competency becoming Forge:

    1. Apprentice at Cold Startup (O-01 Simulator) witnesses the 90-minute sequence: HVAC → SIS proof → FBG cal → ZVS verify → drum drive → gas purge → recipe load. They feel the 100 kHz FPGA gate drive latency in the L0 replica, see the TSN schedule slots on the L1 RTU, know this sequence protects the 2200°C drum from thermal shock. 2. Journeyman at SIF Bypass (Oral Board) witnesses the dual-key moment: Shift Lead + Safety Engineer, 4-hr time limit, blockchain audit trail. They witness the organizational risk acceptance — no algorithm, no procedure, only human judgment at the boundary of consequence. 3. Depot Tech at Solvolysis (P-02 Simulator) watches Elium® depolymerize at 350°C, smells monomer vapor, weighs clean basalt bundles. They witness the EOL product becoming the Forge's next batch of feedstock — the CMF-RQT M_return vector becoming M_virgin. 4. Master at Teach-Back witnesses the Apprentice's first Stage 4 indium-first discharge authorization. They witness the recursive loop closed: the Master who was once Apprentice now authorizes the next generation at Gate FO-J-01.

    No slide decks. No checklists. Direct sensory-motor coupling to the RCT tensor. The instructor's hands are on the simulator emergency stop, the oral board recording, the DQR blockchain entry. They are inside the RCT.

    Protocol (Recursive)

    What recursive sequence guarantees fidelity at each scale?

    Per Operation (Seconds — Micro): 

    FBG channel assessment: λ_measured → λ_reference(PQR) → Λ > 10? → auto-NCR → DQR update
Simulator step: operator_action → expert_policy → Λ_J > 10? → PASS/FAIL → scenario weight update
Cyber range: phishing_click → detection_time → <30 sec? → DQR digital score update

    Per Shift (Hours — Meso): 

    Shift handover: outgoing → incoming (QR scan) → 5-question pulse → sentiment trend → B-competency update
CBM review: MT interprets Λ dashboard → work order priority → RCT S-vector calibration
SIF status: SL verifies 24 SIFs armed → blockchain log → RCT J-vector evidence

    Per Certification Cycle (Years — Macro): 

    Annual Refresher (40 hrs):
  Week 1: F-01 Safety/Carrington → written + E-stop drill
  Week 2: S-03 SIL-3 SIFs → CT-04 partial-stroke witness
  Week 3: O-04 Emergency/Carrington → simulator scenario
  Week 4: M-01 PM Execution → practical on assigned zone
    


    Biennial Recertification (80 hrs):
  Phase 1: Written exam (all K competencies) — 80% pass
  Phase 2: Practical circuit (S-01 through S-06, M-01, P-01) — zero critical errors
  Phase 3: Simulator marathon (4 scenarios: normal, degraded, emergency, Carrington) — all PASS
  Phase 4: Oral board (3 examiners, 4 judgment gates) — Λ_J > 10 all gates
    


    Post-Incident Remediation (8-16 hrs):
  Root cause → targeted scenario → 3 practice runs → re-assess specific competency
    


    Post-ECO Delta Training (4-8 hrs):
  Git tag release → changelog review → affected modules → assessment delta

    Quarterly (Fleet — Meta): 

    PROD-37 Twin Review: Fleet anomaly autoencoder → top 10 new scenarios → simulator library update
Curriculum Review Board: RCT Ω_fleet tensor → curriculum hour reallocation → version bump
Instructor Calibration: All instructors run same 3 scenarios → inter-rater reliability >0.9

    Annual (Strategic — Foundational): 

    1. RCT Theory → History: Compare all predictions to actuals (Apprentice hrs, sim fidelity, judgment pass rates)
2. History → Theory: Update RCT coefficients from measured competency decay curves
3. Standards Audit: ISO 9001/AS9100/NQA-1/IEC 61508 training clause compliance
4. Curriculum Version: Git tag train-v.. → all DQRs migrate
5. Cross-Domain Sync: Forge ↔ Depot competency mapping → CMF-RQT workforce term

    The protocol is the RCT evaluated recursively across time scales. Per-operation → Per-shift → Per-cycle → Quarterly → Annual. Each evaluation corrects the previous. The training program does not drift — it converges.

    Synthesis: The Three Prongs as One

    The Williams Constraint (zero-metal, recursive, Carrington-immune) defines the feasible region of human competency. The Keymaker Key (RCT tensor) navigates the feasible region to the optimal training investment — 400 hrs Apprentice, 50+ scenarios, 4 judgment gates. The El Segundo Protocol (recursive evaluation at 5 time scales) guarantees the operating point is held against competency decay, fleet anomaly drift, and ECO-driven obsolescence.

    Together they form the Forge's human capital immune system: It rejects conventional training (Williams), computes the optimal competency tensor (Keymaker), and self-corrects at every temporal scale (El Segundo). This is not a training program — it is a competency circulation engine that runs on physics, not checklists.

    The Forge cannot be operated by conventional human factors engineering. Conventional HFE assumes: (a) metallic sensors (thermocouples, strain gauges) with electrical redundancy, (b) electrical lockout/tagout on copper conductors, (c) linear process flow with defined boundaries, (d) specialist roles in fixed locations, (e) control rooms with standard lighting/acoustics.     Necessity (The Key)

    The empirical gap is the absence of any HFE framework that designs for sensory-motor coupling to a zero-metal, all-dielectric, recursively circular industrial process under GIC/EMP threat. No existing standard addresses: (a) FBG wavelength as primary metrology requiring wavelength-to-color HMI mapping, (b) ISA-88 recipe execution on TSN-scheduled PLC with PTP <1 μs requiring deterministic HMI refresh, (c) SIL-3 SIF bypass as a dual-key human judgment gate requiring exactly-needed information (ISA-101), (d) Phoenix depot disassembly/solvolysis/LIBS as part of Forge operator body schema, (e) Carrington storm ride-through as a routine scenario requiring 5 ms island transition with 30-sec egress. The solution is inevitable because the Forge's physics demands it: the same operator who authorizes the Stage 4 indium-first discharge at 160°C must also classify the EOL return that feeds that indium at the depot. The CMF-RQT tensor (PROD-33) and RCT tensor (PROD-34) make this recursive — HFE must close the loop between Forge and Depot body schemas.

    Commitment (The Turn)

    This document commits to three non-negotiables: 1. Control room designed for 4 operators (2 Forge + 2 Depot) with ISA-101 Level 1-4 HMI hierarchy — 6 monitors per station, 50 lux ambient, <45 dBA, LiFePO₄ UPS 24h holdover, zero alarm flood (<50/hr steady). 2. Hot zone PPE don/doff <3 min / <5 min with Al-coated proximity suit + PAPR — no metal in PPE, buddy check mandatory, QR-logged don/doff cycles on DQR blockchain. 3. Maintenance access 750 mm minimum clearance with zero-metal tooling (BFRP/PEEK/Zirconia) — max manual lift 25 kg, all heavier → BFRP hoist, tool balancers, anti-fatigue mats.

    These commitments are irreversible. They define the Forge's human-system integration architecture. Any deviation requires SCSC unanimous approval and re-validation of the SIL-3 SIF proof test (CT-04) which is the gate to hot commissioning.

    Keymaker Heuristic — Implementation Precision

    The Empirical Lock

    Fabrication fidelity gap: Conventional HFE standards — ISO 11064 control rooms, NUREG-0700 nuclear HFE, ISA-101 HMI, NIOSH lifting — assume: (a) metallic sensor infrastructure with electrical redundancy, (b) linear process flow with defined boundaries, (c) role specialization in fixed locations, (d) electrical lockout/tagout, (e) standard emergency egress. They cannot model: (a) FBG wavelength drift as the only in-process temperature verification requiring wavelength-to-color perceptual mapping, (b) recursive CMF-RQT/RCT loops where EOL return composition variability (±15% In) changes the Stage 4 thermal profile in real-time requiring HMI predictive highlight, (c) SIL-3 SIF bypass as a human judgment gate requiring exactly-needed information with zero alarm flood, (c) Carrington storm as routine scenario requiring 5 ms island transition with 30-sec egress from any zone, (d) Forge↔Depot cross-domain body schema requiring unified PPE, tooling, QR workflow, egress. The lock is that no existing HFE standard computes the Forge's human-in-the-loop physics in dielectric space.

    The Mathematical Key

    The single computational primitive is the Human-System Coupling Tensor (HSCT): 
    HSCT[P, C, E, Z, Φ_role, Ψ_scenario, Ω_fleet]


    P ∈ ℝ⁸⁺ : Perceptual vector (wavelength→color, trend→predictive, alarm→priority, LIBS→class, XRF→grade, AE→Felicity, IR→hotspot, FBG→Λ)
C ∈ ℝ⁵⁺ : Cognitive vector (mental, physical, temporal, effort, frustration — NASA-TLX)
E ∈ ℝ⁴⁺ : Embodiment vector (reach, lift, posture, don/doff — NIOSH/ISO 11064)
Z ∈ ℝ⁸⁺ : Zone vector (Z0-Z8 access, PPE, barrier, interlock, egress, refuge, comms, rescue)
Φ_role ∈ {FO, DT, MT, QI, SL} : Role projection operator
Ψ_scenario ∈ ℝ⁵⁰⁺ : Scenario tensor (normal, degraded, emergency, Carrington, Phoenix)
Ω_fleet ∈ ℝᴺ : Fleet anomaly tensor (PROD-37 digital twin ML autoencoder output)

    This tensor generates the entire HFE program: control room layout, HMI hierarchy, alarm philosophy, PPE matrix, access clearances, egress routes, shift schedules, HRA HEPs. Every parameter in this document is a projection of HSCT evaluated at role × scenario × fleet state.

    The atomic computation is NASA-TLX weighted workload prediction:

    TLX_predicted = w_M·M + w_P·P + w_T·T + w_Pe·Pe + w_E·E + w_F·F

    Where weights w are calibrated per role per scenario from PROD-34 simulator data. Threshold: TLX_predicted > 80 → mandatory second operator + SL awareness.

    The Turn (Both Directions)

    Theory → History Validation:

    • HSCT predicts 4-operator control room → matches PROD-23 L3 SCADA (4 stations, TSN dual-ring)
    • HSCT predicts <50 alarms/hr steady → matches PROD-28 ISA-18.2 alarm management
    • HSCT predicts 3-min don / 5-min doff → matches PROD-29 hot zone access procedures
    • HSCT predicts 750 mm maintenance clearance → matches PROD-27 FA tooling access
    • HSCT predicts <30 sec egress → matches PROD-29 emergency response drills

    History → Theory Validation:

    • CSMFAB0108 test: 2 operators managed 8-zone cascade with 6 monitors → validates HSCT P-vector dimensionality
    • PROD-27 FA: 3 drum generations required 750 mm for FBG tooling → validates HSCT E-vector clearance
    • PROD-28 CT-04: 24 SIFs trip <50 ms only when SL witnesses SOE → validates HSCT C-vector at judgment gates
    • PROD-23 Carrington sim: 5 ms island transition required trained SL → validates HSCT Ψ_scenario Carrington
    • PROD-33 depot ops: 14-day crate turnaround requires DT who knows Forge → validates HSCT Φ_role cross-domain

    The primitive is validated. The HFE program is not a compliance checklist — it is the physical manifestation of HSCT evaluated across 5 roles, 8 zones, 50+ scenarios, and infinite fleet anomaly generations.

    El Segundo Heuristic — Operational Excellence

    Mirror (Self-Reflection)

    How does the fabricator observe their own fabrication? The Forge's HFE program is instrumented at every node with the same rigor as the thermal cascade:
    • Perceptual Calibration: HMI color mapping (wavelength→color) validated via operator color-naming tasks on air-gapped SCADA. >3σ deviation from fleet mean → color LUT recalibration. Item response theory tracks perceptual drift.
    • Cognitive Load Telemetry: NASA-TLX assessed per shift via 6-question pulse (QR on DQR). Real-time TLX estimate from HMI interaction: click rate, scroll depth, alarm acknowledgment latency, gaze tracking (optional IR camera). ML autoencoder (FOLLOW-29) flags >3σ from role baseline.
    • Physical Ergonomics Monitoring: Tool use tracked via QR (badge + tool badge). Force/torque on BFRP wrench via embedded FBG strain. Posture via ceiling-mounted IR depth (opt-in). NIOSH lift index calculated per task → cumulative daily dose.
    • PPE Integrity: Proximity suit RF tag + PAPR flow sensor → don/doff timestamp, cycle count, filter life. QR scan at zone entry/exit → DQR log. Buddy check photo → blockchain.
    • Egress Drill Performance: Monthly unannounced egress from Z4/Z6. Time-to-safe-zone logged. Route choice vs. dynamic LED analyzed. Refuge station supply check.

    The fabricator sees the HFE program as a distributed sensor network. Every human-system interaction is a measurement. Every measurement updates HSCT. Every HSCT update adjusts HMI colors, alarm thresholds, PPE specs, clearance requirements, shift schedules.

    Participation (Witness)

    How does the inside operator witness the phenomenon into existence? The HFE engineer does not "design" — they witness the human becoming the Forge's nervous system:

    1. Apprentice at Cold Startup (O-01 Simulator) witnesses the 90-minute sequence through 6 monitors: they feel the trackball resistance as they navigate Level 1→2→3, see the predictive highlight on Port 4A setpoint, know this HMI is their sensory extension into the 2200°C drum. 2. Journeyman at SG-2 Flange Torque witnesses the dual-wrench ceremony: they feel the 160 N·m breakaway torque through the BFRP wrench, hear the AE silence, know their tactile judgment certifies what no sensor can measure. 3. Shift Lead at Carrington Exit witnesses the 30-min grid-stable decision: they see the drum thermal shock trend on Level 1, hear the utility coordination on voice comms, know their authorization reconnects the Forge to the world. 4. Depot Tech at LIBS Classification witnesses the plasma flash: they see the spectral lines on Monitor 5, hear the auto-classification beep, know their override decision changes the CMF-RQT M_return vector that feeds tomorrow's Stage 4 indium.

    No wireframes. No usability labs. Direct sensory-motor coupling to the HSCT tensor. The HFE engineer's hands are on the trackball, the BFRP wrench, the dual-key token, the LIBS trigger. They are inside the HSCT.

    What recursive sequence guarantees fidelity at each scale?

    The protocol is the HSCT evaluated recursively across time scales. Per-operation → Per-shift → Per-cycle → Quarterly → Annual. Each evaluation corrects the previous. The HFE program does not drift — it converges.

    Synthesis: The Three Prongs as One

    The Williams Constraint (zero-metal, recursive, Carrington-immune) defines the feasible region of human-system coupling. The Keymaker Key (HSCT tensor) navigates the feasible region to the optimal HFE investment — 4-operator control room, 6 monitors, 3-min don, 750 mm clearance, <30 sec egress. The El Segundo Protocol (recursive evaluation at 5 time scales) guarantees the operating point is held against cognitive drift, physical degradation, PPE wear, and fleet anomaly evolution.

    Together they form the Forge's human-system immune system: It rejects conventional HFE (Williams), computes the optimal coupling tensor (Keymaker), and self-corrects at every temporal scale (El Segundo). This is not an HFE program — it is a human-system coupling engine that runs on physics, not checklists.

    2. HFE Program Overview & Regulatory Basis

    2.1 Design Philosophy: "Embodied Cognition in Dielectric Space"

    The Forge HFE philosophy derives from the El Segundo heuristic (PROD-23, PROD-28): the operator does not monitor — they witness the phenomenon into existence through direct sensory-motor coupling. This requires HFE that designs for embodiment, not observation.

    Three HFE Pillars:

    1. Dielectric Embodiment: All sensing is photonic (FBG wavelength, POF level, LIBS plasma, XRF fluorescence). The operator's interface to the process is light through glass fiber. HFE designs for the perceptual-motor loop: wavelength shift → HMI color → operator recognition → authorization gate.

    2. Recursive Judgment Support: At four cognitive gates (SG-2 flange torque, SG-3 FBG cal, CT-04 SIS proof, SAT-05 first pour), the operator makes irrevocable decisions. HFE provides exactly the information needed — no more, no less — via ISA-101 HMI hierarchy and PROD-23 TSN-deterministic data.

    3. Cross-Domain Body Schema: Forge operators work in Depot disassembly cells; Depot techs work in Forge control room. HFE designs a unified body schema for both: same PPE, same tooling (BFRP/PEEK), same QR/DQR workflow, same emergency egress.

PAPR filter log: Scan QR, log cycles (20 sec) Total: ~5 min

    9. Cognitive Load & Decision Support

    9.1 Information Density Management

    ISA-101 Level 1 Display Rules:

    • Max 7±2 elements per display region
    • No scrolling on Level 1-2 (all critical data visible)
    • Trend compression: 1 hr / 8 hr / 24 hr toggle (not simultaneous)
    • Alarm summary: Count by priority + top 3 active (not full list)

    Cognitive Offload Features:

    • Auto-Summary: "Stage 4: In 6.4g, Sn 12g, Pb 45g — all spec" (vs. raw XRF table)
    • Predictive Highlight: Twin predicts Stage 6 Cu grade → pre-highlight Port 6B setpoint
    • Anomaly Card: Λ > 10 → pop-up card with: symptom, likely cause, recommended action, expert policy
    • Gesture Filter: Leap Motion 3D twin — pinch to zoom, swipe stage, point to annotate

    Appendix F: Detailed Maintenance Access Procedures (Expanded)

    F.1 Drum FBG Channel Replacement Procedure (PROD-04, 30)

    Prerequisites:

    • SL authorization (Gate SG-3 FBG cal verify)
    • Zone 4 cold (T_drum <200°C verified by FBG + pyrometer)
    • PPE: Proximity suit, PAPR, Kevlar gloves, ceramic boots (don <3 min)
    • Tools: BFRP scope, PEEK CF40 extractor, Zirconia feeler, FBG interrogator port
    • Spares: FBG array (Zone-specific), PQR-FS-001 calibration data

    Procedure: 1. Entry: SL dual-key → Z4 gate interlock opens → buddy check → QR scan entry log 2. Access: Remove drum port cover (PEEK CF40 bolts, BFRP torque wrench 160 N·m ±5) 3. Inspection: BFRP borescope → FBG channel location → document via QR photo 4. Extraction: PEEK CF40 extractor → pull failed FBG → verify no matrix damage (AE silent) 5. Installation: New FBG array → align to PQR position ±0.5 mm → zirconia feeler verify gap 6. Calibration: Connect interrogator → 5-point reference (25/500/1000/1500/2000°C) → R² >0.999 7. Restoration: Port cover → torque ceremony (SG-2) → AE silence verify → QR log 8. Exit: Doff PPE (5 min) → QR scan exit log → SL debrief

    Time Target: <45 min total (don 3 + access 10 + extract 10 + install 10 + cal 10 + restore 2 + doff 5)

    F.2 Port Valve Actuator Swap Procedure (PROD-09, 30)

    Prerequisites:

    • SL authorization (Gate FO-J-01 stage transition)
    • Port valve closed (SIS interlock verified)
    • PPE: Proximity suit, PAPR, Kevlar gloves, ceramic boots
    • Tools: PEEK CF40 sockets (actuator bolts), BFRP hoist (actuator 12 kg), ceramic feeler
    • Spares: Ti₃AlC₂ actuator assembly, ZrO₂ piston, PQR-ACT-001 test data

    Procedure: 1. Depressurize: N₂ purge port line → verify 0 bar → SIS log 2. Remove Actuator: PEEK CF40 socket → 4 bolts → BFRP hoist lift → clear zone 3. Inspect Piston: Zirconia feeler → gap 0.15±0.02 mm → AE silent verify 4. Install Actuator: Align splines → seat → 4 bolts torque 85 N·m ±2 (BFRP wrench) 5. Functional Test: L2 PLC command → open/close 3× → position feedback ±0.5 mm → response <50 ms 6. SIS Verify: SIF-15 port valve test → trip <50 ms → SOE timestamp align 7. Document: QR photo install → DQR log → SL sign-off

    Time Target: <30 min total

    Appendix I: Additional HFE Validation Methods (Expanded)

    I.1 Control Room Validation (ISO 11064 / NUREG-0700)

    Validation Phase 1 — Design Review (Pre-FAT):

    • Sightline verification: 3D CAD + operator manikins (5th-95th %) → all monitors visible
    • Lighting simulation: Dialux/EAG → 50 lux ambient, 300 lux task, UGR<16 verified
    • Acoustic model: Odeon → NC-35 verified with HVAC + pumps + operator speech
    • Thermal CFD: 22±1°C, 40-50% RH, <0.15 m/s velocity at all stations

    Validation Phase 2 — FAT (Factory Acceptance Test):

    • Hardware-in-loop: L3 SCADA + L2 PLCs + L1 RTUs + L0 FPGAs on TSN
    • Scenario: 8-hr steady state + 3 upsets + 1 Carrington
    • Metrics: Alarm rate, TLX (NASA-TLX per operator), SIF response, authorization gate timing
    • Pass Criteria: Alarm rate <50/hr steady, TLX <60 steady, SIF <50ms, Gates 100% correct

    Validation Phase 3 — SAT (Site Acceptance Test):

    • 10 production batches (PROD-28 SAT-05)
    • Metrics: Batch mass balance >99%, zero spurious SIF trips, operator TLX logs
    • Pass Criteria: All 10 batches meet spec, zero human error requiring recovery

    I.2 HMI Validation (ISA-101 / ISA-18.2)

    Alarm Rationalization (Pre-FAT):

    • Master Alarm Database: 247 alarms (24 SIF + 120 Process + 50 Equipment + 53 Cyber)
    • Each alarm: Priority, Setpoint, Deadband, Shelving limit, Suppression logic, Operator action
    • ISA-18.2 compliance: Rationalization workshop (SL, QI, Safety Eng, Controls Eng)
    • Flood test: Inject 500 alarms/10 min → verify chattering filter, priority audio only

    HMI Usability Test (FAT):

    • 6 operators (2 FO, 2 DT, 1 MT, 1 QI) execute 10 scenarios
    • Metrics: Task completion time, error count, NASA-TLX, SUS (System Usability Scale)
    • Pass Criteria: SUS >80, zero critical errors, TLX <80 all scenarios

    I.3 Maintenance Access Validation (PROD-27 FA)

    First Article Physical Verification:

    • Drum FBG access: 3 FA drums → MT performs procedure → time, clearance, tool fit, PPE
    • Port valve swap: 3 FA ports → MT performs procedure → time, torque, AE silence
    • Coil cold plate: 8 FA zones → MT performs IR scan → access, reach, tool positioning
    • Vessel aerogel: 1 FA vessel → MT performs borescope → access, visibility, documentation

    Pass Criteria: All procedures ≤ target time, 750 mm clearance verified, zero tool interference, PPE don/doff <3/5 min

    I.4 PPE Validation (NFPA 1971 / 1951 / ISO 11612)

    Proximity Suit + PAPR System Test:

    • Radiant heat: 3000°F, 30 sec exposure → interior T rise <10°C
    • Convective heat: 500°C, 5 min → interior T rise <5°C
    • PAPR flow: >170 L/min continuous, 8-hr battery, filter life 500 cycles
    • Don/doff: 10 operators × 5 cycles → avg <3 min don, <5 min doff
    • Buddy check: 100% defect detection (seam, zipper, hose, filter, flow)

    I.5 Egress Validation (PROD-29)

    Monthly Unannounced Drill Protocol:

    • Trigger: SL activates "Egress Drill" via HMI (logged, timestamped)
    • Measurement: Time from drill start to all personnel at Z0 safe zone
    • Routes: Primary + secondary from each zone tested quarterly
    • Pass Criteria: All personnel <30 sec (Z4), <45 sec (Z6), headcount 100% at Z0

    Annual Full-Scale Exercise:

    • Scenario: Carrington storm + H₂ leak + drum crack (multi-hazard)
    • Participants: All shifts, rescue team, safety, management
    • Metrics: Egress time, comms effectiveness, rescue response, PPE integrity
    • After-action: Root cause, corrective actions, procedure updates

The security program optimizes for four simultaneous objectives: (1) prevent unauthorized modification of safety-critical control logic, (2) detect physical tampering with dielectric sensors/actuators, (3) ensure supply chain integrity for firmware/hardware, (4) maintain operational continuity during Carrington-class GIC events.

    2.3 Security Architecture Principles

    1. Defense in Depth at Physical Layer: PMMA POF immune to EMI, no copper antennas, no wireless, no powerline comms 2. Air-Gap as Primary Control: No IP connectivity OT↔IT; data diode enforces unidirectional OT→IT flow 3. SIL-3 SIS Independence: Safety logic on dedicated FPGA, isolated TSN VLAN, 2oo3 voting, no shared infrastructure 4. Deterministic Network Security: TSN schedule frozen, per-stream filtering, FRER for critical paths 5. Supply Chain as Attack Surface: AVL vendors required to provide SBOM, signed firmware, 3rd-party pen test 6. Digital Twin as Sensor: ML anomaly detection (FOLLOW-29) on 384-dim FBG state vector at 10 Hz

    3.2 TSN Security Configuration (IEEE 802.1Qci / 802.1Qbv)

    VLANPriorityTraffic TypeGate Control ListMax Frame SizeFRER ----------------------------------------------------------------------- 10 (SIS)7 (Highest)SIF trip, SOE, 2oo3 votesFixed: 0-100 μs512 BYes (dual path) 20 (RTU)6PID, FBG, MFC, ResonanceFixed: 100-500 μs1518 BYes (FBG) 30 (PLC)5Interlocks, Recipes, CarouselFixed: 500-800 μs1518 BNo 40 (SCADA)4Historian, Alarms, TwinBest effort: 800-900 μs1518 BNo 50 (Mgmt)3PTP, Firmware, ConfigBest effort: 900-1000 μs1518 BNo Guard Band——900-1000 μs——

    TSN Security Controls:

    • Per-Stream Filtering (802.1Qci): Each VLAN isolated; no frame can cross VLAN boundaries without explicit gate control entry
    • Frame Preemption (802.1Qbu): SIF frames preempt all other traffic; 100 μs guard band ensures SIS latency <50 ms
    • Time-Aware Shaper (802.1Qbv): Gate control list frozen at FAT (PROD-39); changes require ECO + CT-04 re-test
    • FRER (802.1CB): SIS and FBG streams duplicated on both rings; zero packet loss on single link failure

    3.3 PTP Security (IEEE 802.1AS)

    ComponentSecurity Feature ----------------------------- GrandmasterGNSS + OCXO (Microchip 5071A), 24h holdover ±1 μs, anti-jamming antenna Boundary ClocksAll L1 RTUs, L2 PLCs, L3 SCADA; verify GM identity via certificate Transparent ClocksTSN switches (BFRP-housed); no PTP modification, only residence time AuthenticationIEEE 802.1AS-2020 TLV-based authentication; reject unauthenticated Announce MonitoringL3 SCADA monitors offset <1 μs; >1 μs → alarm, >10 μs → SIF-24 (comms loss)

    4. FBG/PMF Tamper Detection

    4.1 FBG as Security Sensor

    The 384 FBG channels (125 Hz each) serve dual purpose: process temperature/strain measurement and physical tamper detection.

    Tamper VectorDetection MechanismThreshold ----------------------------------------------- Fiber TapOptical power drop >0.5 dB at interrogatorImmediate alarm Wavelength ShiftUnexpected Δλ >0.1 nm (non-thermal) on any channelAuto-NCR, Λ > 10 Channel CountMissing channels (expected 384, detected <380)Immediate alarm Interrogator ReplacementSerial number mismatch, firmware hash mismatchBoot-time verification WDM/TDM TimingSlot timing deviation >1%Continuous monitor

    4.2 PMF (Process Monitoring Fiber) Security

    Sensor TypeSecurity FunctionAnomaly Response -------------------------------------------------- FBG TemperatureProcess + tamperΛ > 10 → auto-NCR + SL alert FBG StrainDrum flange integrity + tamperFelicity ratio <1.0 → SIF-03 POF LevelSlag/metal interface + tamperUnexpected level → Port valve SIF PyrometerPort window temperature + tamperWindow coating tamper → alarm AE VibrationCrack detection + tamperNon-process impacts → classification

    4.3 Tamper Detection Algorithm (PROD-37 Twin)

    Runs at 10 Hz on PROD-37 Digital Twin (512-core HPC)
    
def detect_fbg_tamper(fbg_state_vector: np.ndarray) -> TamperAlert:
    """
    fbg_state_vector: 384 wavelengths @ 125 Hz → 10 Hz aggregated
    """
    # 1. Thermal model residual (from PROD-24)
    residual = fbg_state_vector - thermal_admittance_model.predict(fbg_state_vector)
    
    # 2. Autoencoder reconstruction error (FOLLOW-29)
    recon_error = autoencoder.reconstruct(fbg_state_vector) - fbg_state_vector
    
    # 3. Spatial correlation check (adjacent channels should correlate)
    spatial_corr = compute_spatial_correlation(fbg_state_vector)
    
    # 4. Tamper score fusion
    tamper_score = 0.4  norm(residual) + 0.4  norm(recon_error) + 0.2 * (1 - spatial_corr)
    
    if tamper_score > THRESHOLD_3SIGMA:
        return TamperAlert(
            channels=identify_anomalous_channels(fbg_state_vector),
            score=tamper_score,
            recommended_action="SL review, potential SIF bypass, physical inspection"
        )
    return None

    7.3 Correlation Engine (PROD-37 Twin)

    The digital twin (PROD-37) runs a correlation engine at 10 Hz that fuses:

    • Network flow anomalies (TSN)
    • Process variable deviations (FBG, MFC, pyro, XRF)
    • Safety system events (SIF trips, 2oo3 votes)
    • Physical tamper signals (FBG optical power, wavelength)
    • Supply chain signals (SBOM, firmware hashes)

    Correlation Logic: 

    ALERT = (Network_Anomaly ∧ Process_Deviation) ∨
        (Process_Deviation ∧ Physical_Tamper) ∨
        (Safety_Event ∧ ¬Process_Cause) ∨
        (Supply_Chain_Drift ∧ Deployed_Version)

    8.1 Incident Classification

    8.2 Incident Response Playbooks

    Playbook IR-01: Unauthorized SIF Bypass Attempt

    1. DETECT: IDS-004 triggers (SIF trip without process cause OR dual-key not presented)
2. CONTAIN: SIS FPGA locks all 24 SIFs in "armed" state; no further bypass possible
3. ERADICATE: SL + Safety Eng investigate; revoke compromised tokens; rotate keys
4. RECOVER: CT-04 partial-stroke test all 24 SIFs; verify SOE integrity
5. LESSONS: Root cause (token theft? insider? supply chain?); update playbook

    Playbook IR-02: FBG Tamper Detected (Physical)

    1. DETECT: IDS-003 or tamper algorithm >3σ
2. CONTAIN: SL authorizes zone hold; affected zone PID → safe setpoint; SIF-24 armed
3. ERADICATE: MT + QI physical inspection (PPE, <3 min don); fiber continuity test
4. RECOVER: FBG recalibration (CT-06) on affected channels; CT-04 SIF proof
5. LESSONS: Physical security review; camera footage; access log correlation

    Playbook IR-03: Supply Chain Firmware Compromise

    1. DETECT: IDS-005 (firmware hash mismatch) OR CVE match in deployed version
2. CONTAIN: Block affected version in TUF repo; isolate affected nodes (TSN VLAN 50)
3. ERADICATE: Vendor CAPA; rebuild from source; sign new version; SBOM regenerate
4. RECOVER: Staged rollout (1 zone → 1 stage → full); CT-04 if SIS affected
5. LESSONS: SLSA level review; vendor security reassessment; pen test scope expand

    Playbook IR-04: Carrington Storm + Cyber Event (Combined)

    1. DETECT: PROD-26 GIC sensors + IDS correlation (GIC + network anomaly)
2. CONTAIN: 5 ms island transition (PROD-23); SIS on LiFePO₄ UPS; data diode holds
3. ERADICATE: Post-storm (30 min grid stable): full SIS CT-04; FBG CT-06; TSN verify
4. RECOVER: Staged grid reconnect (PROD-23); twin state reconciliation (PROD-37)
5. LESSONS: GIC-cyber correlation analysis; update threat model; tabletop exercise

    Appendix F: Detailed FBG Tamper Detection Algorithms (Expanded)

    F.1 Multi-Hypothesis Tamper Classification

    Runs at 10 Hz on PROD-37 Digital Twin
    
class FBGTamperClassifier:
    def __init__(self):
        self.thermal_model = ThermalAdmittanceModel()  # PROD-24
        self.autoencoder = Autoencoder(latent_dim=32)  # FOLLOW-29
        self.spatial_graph = SpatialCorrelationGraph()  # 384-channel topology
        
    def classify(self, fbg_wavelengths: np.ndarray) -> TamperClassification:
        """
        fbg_wavelengths: shape (384,) - current wavelength readings (nm)
        Returns: TamperClassification enum + confidence + affected channels
        """
        
        # Hypothesis H0: Nominal thermal operation
        thermal_pred = self.thermal_model.predict(fbg_wavelengths)
        residual = fbg_wavelengths - thermal_pred
        H0_score = np.linalg.norm(residual)
        
        # Hypothesis H1: Localized physical tamper (fiber tap, cut, strain)
        recon = self.autoencoder.reconstruct(fbg_wavelengths)
        recon_error = fbg_wavelengths - recon
        spatial_corr = self.spatial_graph.correlation(fbg_wavelengths)
        H1_score = 0.5  np.linalg.norm(recon_error) + 0.5  (1 - spatial_corr)
        
        # Hypothesis H2: Interrogator compromise (all channels shifted)
        common_mode = np.mean(fbg_wavelengths - thermal_pred)
        H2_score = np.abs(common_mode)
        
        # Hypothesis H3: Selective channel spoofing (adversarial injection)
        channel_stats = self.compute_channel_statistics(fbg_wavelengths)
        H3_score = self.detect_adversarial_pattern(channel_stats)
        
        # Bayesian model selection
        scores = np.array([H0_score, H1_score, H2_score, H3_score])
        priors = np.array([0.95, 0.03, 0.015, 0.005])  # From fleet history
        posteriors = scores  priors / np.sum(scores  priors)
        
        max_idx = np.argmax(posteriors)
        confidence = posteriors[max_idx]
        
        if max_idx == 0:
            return TamperClassification.NOMINAL, confidence, []
        elif max_idx == 1:
            affected = self.localize_tamper(recon_error, spatial_corr)
            return TamperClassification.LOCALIZED_TAMPER, confidence, affected
        elif max_idx == 2:
            return TamperClassification.INTERROGATOR_COMPROMISE, confidence, list(range(384))
        else:
            affected = self.identify_spoofed_channels(channel_stats)
            return TamperClassification.SELECTIVE_SPOOFING, confidence, affected

    Heuristic Intro (Combined): PROD-36

    Combined Heuristic Introduction

    PROD-36 Cyber-Physical Security

    Carrington Storm Motors Forge — Aegis-Forge I Thermal Cascade Inductive Material Separator

    Williams Heuristic — Architectural Clarity

    Constraint (The Lock)

    The Forge cannot be secured by conventional IT/OT cybersecurity. A 500 kW induction furnace at 2200°C with 384 dielectric FBG sensors, GaN inverters at 100 kHz, SIL-3 SIFs on TSN, and a physically air-gapped network has no precedent in any security framework. Conventional security assumes: (a) IP-connected networks with firewalls/IDS/IPS, (b) copper Ethernet with electromagnetic shielding, (c) software-based authentication, (d) patch management via network, (e) cloud-connected monitoring. The Forge violates all five: the network is physically air-gapped (no IP routes), the fieldbus is PMMA POF (immune to EMI/GIC), authentication is hardware-token-based (YubiKey), firmware updates are staged via TSN VLAN 50 (read-only from OT), and the only OT→IT path is a hardware data diode. The constraint is physics — a single IP route from IT to OT becomes a GIC antenna during a Carrington storm (5000 nT/s induces >100 V/km); a single wireless device becomes an EMP antenna; a single unauthenticated firmware load destroys the SIL-3 SIFs. The air-gap is not a policy — it is a dielectric requirement.

    Necessity (The Key)

    The empirical gap is the absence of any security framework that protects an all-dielectric, air-gapped, SIL-3 safety-critical system under Carrington-class GIC threat. No existing standard addresses: (a) FBG wavelength shifts as tamper detection vectors (384 channels at 125 Hz), (b) TSN per-stream filtering (IEEE 802.1Qci) as mandatory security control, (c) PTP grandmaster compromise as safety-critical (resonance tracking depends on <1 μs sync), (d) supply chain firmware signing for GaN drivers/TSN switches/PTP grandmasters as SIL-3 requirement, (e) data diode as the only OT→IT path with protocol break at application layer. The solution is inevitable because the Forge's physics demands it: the same TSN network that carries SIF trips at <50 ms must also carry FBG data at 125 Hz/channel; the same PTP that synchronizes resonance tracking must also timestamp SOE for SIF proof tests. Security cannot be bolted on — it must be architected into the dielectric control fabric.

    Commitment (The Turn)

    This document commits to three non-negotiables: 1. Physical air-gap absolute — no IP routes OT↔IT, no wireless, no powerline comms; hardware data diode enforces unidirectional OT→IT only; violation requires SCSC unanimous + full SIL-3 re-certification (CT-04). 2. FBG as security sensor — 384 channels monitored for tamper (optical power, wavelength shift, channel count) at 10 Hz via PROD-37 digital twin; Λ > 10 on >5 channels = auto-NCR + SIF-24 evaluation. 3. Supply chain firmware integrity — all Tier 1 vendors (12 critical) must provide SBOM (CycloneDX), signed firmware (RSA-4096/HSM), 3rd-party pen test, secure boot; SLSA Level 3 build pipeline; TUF repository with in-toto attestations.

    These commitments are irreversible. They define the Forge's cyber-physical immune system. Any deviation requires SCSC unanimous approval and re-validation of the SIL-3 SIF proof test (CT-04) which is the gate to hot commissioning.

    Keymaker Heuristic — Implementation Precision

    The Empirical Lock

    Fabrication fidelity gap: Conventional OT security frameworks — IEC 62443, NERC CIP, NIST SP 800-82 — assume: (a) IP-routable networks with firewalls/DMZs, (b) copper Ethernet with MACsec/IPsec, (c) software-based patch management, (d) centralized SIEM with log aggregation, (e) remote vendor access via VPN. They cannot model: (a) physically air-gapped network with zero IP routes where the only OT→IT path is a hardware data diode, (b) PMMA POF fieldbus immune to EMI/GIC where tamper detection is optical (FBG wavelength shifts), (c) TSN time-aware scheduling (802.1Qbv) as a security control with frozen gate control lists, (d) PTP grandmaster as safety-critical component (resonance tracking fails at >1 μs offset), (e) firmware updates staged via read-only TSN VLAN 50 with staged rollout and CT-04 re-test. The lock is that no existing security framework computes the Forge's cyber-physical physics where the network schedule IS the access control, the fiber IS the tamper sensor, and the air-gap IS the firewall.

    The Mathematical Key

    The single computational primitive is the Cyber-Physical Anomaly Tensor (CPAT): 
    CPAT[N, P, S, F, V, Φ_role, Ψ_threat, Ω_fleet]


    N ∈ ℝᵛ : Network tensor (TSN frame rates, VLAN isolation, gate control list, FRER status)
P ∈ ℝ³⁸⁴ : Process tensor (FBG wavelengths @ 10 Hz, 384 channels from PROD-37 twin)
S ∈ ℝ²⁴ : Safety tensor (SIF states, 2oo3 votes, SOE timestamps, trip logic)
F ∈ ℝⁿ : Firmware tensor (hashes, versions, SBOM components, signatures for L0/L1/L2/L3)
V ∈ ℝᵐ : Vendor tensor (AVL tier, pen test results, CVE exposure, firmware freshness)
Φ_role ∈ {FO, DT, MT, QI, SL, Safety, Controls, Cyber} : Role projection
Ψ_threat ∈ ℝᵏ : Threat tensor (GIC, APT, insider, supply chain, ransomware, hacktivist)
Ω_fleet ∈ ℝᴺ : Fleet anomaly tensor (PROD-37 digital twin ML autoencoder output)

    This tensor generates the entire security program: network architecture, TSN configuration, FBG tamper thresholds, IAM policies, IDS rules, IR playbooks, resilience targets, vendor requirements, testing schedule. Every parameter in this document is a projection of CPAT evaluated at role × threat × fleet state.

    The atomic computation is multi-source likelihood fusion for intrusion detection:

    Λ_CP = P(observation intrusion) / P(observation nominal)


    observation = {TSN_frame_anomaly, FBG_Λ>10, SIF_unexpected_trip, PTP_offset>1μs, 
               firmware_hash_mismatch, SBOM_drift, JIT_unauthorized, AE_non_process}
    


    P(obs intrusion) = ∏ P(source_i intrusion)  [conditional independence given intrusion]
P(obs nominal) = ∏ P(source_i nominal)       [baseline from fleet history]

    Threshold Λ_CP > 100 triggers SEV-1; Λ_CP > 10 triggers SEV-2; Λ_CP > 3 triggers SEV-3. This runs in PROD-37 digital twin at 10 Hz on fused sensor stream.

    The Turn (Both Directions)

    Theory → History Validation:

    • CPAT predicts physical air-gap → matches PROD-23 L3 SCADA (data diode only OT→IT)
    • CPAT predicts FBG tamper detection → matches PROD-28 Λ > 10 auto-NCR on 384 channels
    • CPAT predicts TSN per-stream filtering → matches PROD-23 VLAN 10-50 isolation
    • CPAT predicts firmware signing requirement → matches PROD-38 SLSA Level 3, TUF repo
    • CPAT predicts RTO 4 hr / RPO 1 hr → matches PROD-30 cold standby, historian backup

    History → Theory Validation:

    • PROD-23 GIC ride-through test: 100 A/m Helmholtz, 30 min — zero data loss, zero spurious trips → validates CPAT N-tensor GIC immunity
    • PROD-28 CT-04: 24 SIFs trip <50 ms, 2oo3 voting, SOE aligned — validates CPAT S-tensor SIS independence
    • PROD-10 EMC test: CISPR 11 Class A passed 20 dB margin, no metal shielding — validates CPAT P-tensor dielectric transparency
    • PROD-33 AVL audit: 12 Tier 1 vendors, all SBOM + signed firmware + pen test — validates CPAT V-tensor supply chain
    • PROD-37 twin: ML autoencoder detects FBG drift 48 hrs before operator — validates CPAT Ω_fleet fleet anomaly

    The primitive is validated. The security program is not a compliance checklist — it is the physical manifestation of CPAT evaluated across 5 VLANs, 384 FBG channels, 24 SIFs, 4 firmware layers, 12 critical vendors, and infinite threat generations.

    El Segundo Heuristic — Operational Excellence

    Mirror (Self-Reflection)

    How does the fabricator observe their own fabrication? The Forge's security program is instrumented at every node with the same rigor as the thermal cascade:
    • Network Telemetry: TSN switch mirrors capture every frame on VLANs 10-50; Zeek/Suricata parse with custom TSN dissectors; per-stream counters (rate, size, timing, VLAN) stream to PROD-37 at 10 Hz. Anomaly: VLAN 10 frame from unauthorized MAC → immediate port shutdown.
    • Process Telemetry: 384 FBG channels @ 125 Hz → 10 Hz aggregated → PROD-37 ML autoencoder (FOLLOW-29) computes reconstruction error >3σ → auto-NCR. Spatial correlation check across adjacent channels detects localized tamper.
    • Safety Telemetry: 24 SIFs SOE timestamps aligned across zones; 2oo3 vote logic verified per cycle; unexpected trip (no process cause) → immediate SIF lockdown + SL alert.
    • Firmware Telemetry: Boot-time hash verification (SHA-256) on all L0/L1/L2/L3; mismatch → boot halt + SL + Controls Eng. Weekly automated SBOM diff vs. TUF repo; drift → block deploy.
    • Access Telemetry: Every JIT request logged (requestor, approver, duration, actions); badge-in/out at zone gates; USB port monitors on all OT workstations; UEBA on access patterns.

    The fabricator sees the security program as a distributed sensor network. Every frame, wavelength, vote, hash, and badge swipe is a measurement. Every measurement updates CPAT. Every CPAT update adjusts TSN gates, FBG thresholds, SIF logic, firmware pins, JIT policies.

    Participation (Witness)

    How does the inside operator witness the phenomenon into existence? The security engineer does not "monitor" — they witness the security posture becoming the Forge's immune response:

    1. Shift Lead at SIF Bypass Gate (IR-01) witnesses the dual-key moment: YubiKey + Safety Eng YubiKey, 4-hr blockchain timer starts, SOE logs every SIF state change. They witness the organizational risk acceptance — no algorithm, only human judgment at the boundary of consequence. 2. Cyber Engineer at TSN Schedule Freeze witnesses the FAT gate control list: 1 ms cycle, 4 slices, 100 μs guard band, VLAN 10 highest priority.     2.3 FBG Channel Health & Tamper Integration

    Per PROD-36, FBG channels serve dual purpose — process metrology AND security sensing:

    def fbg_health_check(channel_data, twin_autoencoder):
    # Process health
    snr = channel_data.optical_power / channel_data.noise_floor
    wavelength_drift = abs(channel_data.λ - channel_data.λ_nominal)
    
    # Tamper detection (PROD-36 CPAT)
    Λ_tamper = twin_autoencoder.anomaly_score(channel_data.window_10Hz)
    
    if snr < 10 or wavelength_drift > 0.5:  # nm
        return ChannelStatus.DEGRADED
    elif Λ_tamper > 10:
        return ChannelStatus.TAMPER_SUSPECT  # Auto-NCR triggered
    else:
        return ChannelStatus.NOMINAL

    Degraded channels are excluded from thermal reconstruction but logged for tamper forensics. Tamper-suspect channels trigger immediate SIF-24 evaluation and CPAT update.

  }
}

    The ROM executes on the HPC at 10 Hz with the same input trajectory as the full twin but 118× faster — enabling Monte Carlo UQ (1000 samples/cycle) and ML training data generation.

    3.3 Twin-Process Synchronization

    The digital twin maintains lock with the physical process through the Twin Synchronization Protocol:

    Every 100 ms (10 Hz):
  1. Receive SCADA state frame via data diode (merkle-verified)
  2. Compare twin state vs. process state: Δx = x_twin - x_process
  3. If Δx₂ > 3σ_threshold:
       a. Log synchronization anomaly
       b. Trigger ML autoencoder retraining (FOLLOW-29)
       c. Operator alert: "Twin drift detected — review recommended"
  4. Update twin initial condition: x_twin ← x_process (soft reset, ω = 0.1)
  5. Advance twin by 100 ms
  6. Publish twin predictions (T+1s, T+10s, T+60s) to SCADA HMI

    The soft reset (ω = 0.1) prevents discontinuity in ML autoencoder latent space while correcting drift.

    4. Real-Time Twin Sync

    4.1 OPC-UA over Data Diode

    The OT→IT data path uses OPC-UA PubSub over TSN on the OT side, converted to Kafka on the IT side:

    OT Side (SCADA → Data Diode):

    • OPC-UA PubSub dataset: ForgeStateDataSet (10 Hz)
    • Fields: timestamp, zone_states[8], drum_profile[384], SIF_states[24], gas[4], merkle_root
    • Transport: TSN VLAN 50 (read-only from OT), 1 Gbps, priority 7 (highest)
    • Security: No encryption (air-gap provides), but signed with L3 SCADA HSM key

    Data Diode:

    • Hardware: Fox DataDiode 1G, unidirectional fiber, protocol break
    • Application layer: OPC-UA binary → Kafka Avro schema translation
    • Integrity: SHA-256 merkle tree per frame, root in frame header

    IT Side (Data Diode → Kafka → Data Lake):

    • Kafka topic: forge.twin.state.v1 (Avro schema registered in Schema Registry)
    • Consumers: Digital twin HPC, Fleet analytics, Training simulator, Compliance archive
    • Retention: Hot (SSD) 30 days, Warm (HDD) 1 yr, Cold (tape/S3) 7 yrs

    4.2 Bandwidth & Latency Budget

    StageData VolumeLatencyBudget ------------------------------------- SCADA frame assembly12 KB2 ms<5 ms Data diode transit12 KB50 μs<100 μs OPC-UA → Kafka translation12 KB1 ms<2 ms Kafka commit (acks=all)12 KB5 ms<10 ms HPC ingest + twin step12 KB50 ms<100 ms Total OT→Twin12 KB~58 ms<120 ms

    The 10 Hz cycle provides 100 ms budget; 58 ms leaves 42 ms margin for GC pauses, network jitter, and twin compute.

    4.3 Integrity Verification

    Every frame carries a merkle tree root over the 384 FBG channels + 8 zone states + 24 SIF states:

    Frame Merkle Tree:
Leaf 0-383:  FBG_001 FBG_002... FBG_384 (each: λ[nm] + power[dBm] + status)
Leaf 384-391: Zone_01 ... Zone_08 (each: P[kW] + V[V] + I[A] + f[Hz] + status)
Leaf 392-415: SIF_01 ... SIF_24 (each: state + timestamp + vote)
Root: SHA-256(Leaf_0 Leaf_1... Leaf_415)


    Verification (IT side):
  1. Reconstruct leaves from Kafka message
  2. Compute root = merkle(leaves)
  3. Compare root == frame.header.merkle_root
  4. If mismatch: log integrity violation, increment CPAT V-tensor (PROD-36), alert

    This detects both data diode bit errors AND malicious frame injection at the IT ingress point.

    5. ML Anomaly Detection

    5.1 Autoencoder Architecture

    The ML anomaly detector (FOLLOW-29) is a deep autoencoder trained on the 384-dim FBG state at 10 Hz:

    Encoder:     384 → 128 → 64 → 32 (latent)
Latent:      z ∈ ℝ³²  (compressed FBG thermal state)
Decoder:     32 → 64 → 128 → 384 (reconstruction)
Loss:        MSE(x, x̂) + λ·KL(q(zx) p(z))  // VAE with β=0.1
Activation:  Swish (encoder), Linear (decoder output)
Training:    Adam, lr=1e-3, batch=256, 500 epochs on 6-month nominal data

    Anomaly score per 10 Hz frame: 

    Λ_ML = x - x̂²₂ / σ²_nominal
    where σ²_nominal is the running variance of reconstruction error on validated nominal frames.

    Threshold: Λ_ML > 3σ → SEV-3 anomaly card on HMI (PROD-35) Threshold: Λ_ML > 10σ → SEV-2 auto-NCR + CPAT update (PROD-36) Threshold: Λ_ML > 100σ → SEV-1 SIF-24 evaluation + twin resync

    5.2 Multi-Source Anomaly Fusion (CPAT Integration)

    Per PROD-36, the Cyber-Physical Anomaly Tensor (CPAT) fuses ML with other sources:

    CPAT_fused = logit( P(obs intrusion) / P(obs nominal) )


    obs = {
  FBG:        Λ_ML from autoencoder,
  TSN:        frame_rate_anomaly, VLAN_crossing, timing_violation,
  SIF:        unexpected_trip, vote_mismatch, SOE_timestamp_drift,
  PTP:        offset > 1 μs, grandmaster_failover,
  Firmware:   hash_mismatch, SBOM_drift, boot_verification_fail,
  Access:     JIT_unauthorized, badge_anomaly, USB_event,
  AE:         non_process_hits, crack_growth_signature
}
    


    P(obs intrusion) = ∏ P(source_i intrusion)  [conditional independence]
P(obs nominal)   = ∏ P(source_i nominal)    [fleet baseline]

    This runs at 10 Hz in the digital twin HPC, feeding SEV levels to PROD-36 IDS and PROD-35 HMI.

    5.3 Scenario Auto-Generation for Training

    Per PROD-34 (Training), the digital twin auto-generates simulator scenarios:

    Monthly Scenario Generation Pipeline:
  1. Sample from fleet anomaly database (Λ_ML > 3σ events)
  2. Cluster by root cause (k-means on latent z, k=20)
  3. For each cluster centroid:
       a. Extract 300s pre-event trajectory
       b. Inject into PROD-37 twin with perturbed initial conditions
       c. Generate 50 Monte Carlo variants (±10% params)
       d. Label with root cause, severity, optimal operator actions
  4. Export as PROD-34 simulator scenario packs (JSON + initial conditions)
  5. Curate: Operator validation → remove unrealistic, add expert annotations
  6. Deploy to training fleet with RCT tensor update (PROD-34)

    This closes the loop: Process anomalies → Twin scenarios → Operator training → Better anomaly response.

    6. Fleet Optimization

    6.1 Bayesian Parameter Updates

    Updates use Hamiltonian Monte Carlo on the HPC (512 cores, 4 chains, 1000 warmup + 1000 samples). Posterior means update ROM coefficients; posteriors propagate to PROD-33 CMF-RQT tensor for feedstock planning.

    6.2 Fleet-Level CMF-RQT/RCT/HSCT Tensor Feeds

    The digital twin consumes and produces the three cross-document tensors:

    CMF-RQT (PROD-33 Supply Chain): Feedstock composition → predicted recovery, energy, slag 

    CMF_RQT[feedstock_UUID] = E[recovery | composition, twin_params]
    Updated per batch from actual vs. predicted.

    RCT (PROD-34 Training): Operator competency → scenario performance 

    RCT[operator_ID, scenario] = P(pass | competency, twin_difficulty)
    Updated per training session; feeds personalized remediation.

    HSCT (PROD-35 HFE): Human-system coupling → error rates, response times 

    HSCT[operator_ID, task] = (error_rate, response_time, cognitive_load)
    Updated per shift; feeds HMI adaptation and staffing model.

    6.3 Continuous Optimization Loop

    Daily Fleet Optimization (02:00 UTC):
  1. Aggregate prior day batches across all Forges (N sites)
  2. Update twin parameter posteriors (HMC)
  3. Re-optimize PID gains per zone (Bayesian optimization, 50 evals)
  4. Re-optimize RPM profiles per stage (genetic algorithm, 200 pop)
  5. Re-optimize flux rates per category (gradient-based, adjoint)
  6. Validate: simulate 100 virtual batches → check SI > 0.99, energy < budget
  7. If improvement > 2%: stage ECO for PID/RPM/flux updates (PROD-38)
  8. Publish updated parameters to all Forges via data diode (OT→IT→OT at next site)

    This is the fleet learning loop — each Forge's data improves all Forges' parameters.

    Heuristic Intro (Combined): PROD-37

    Combined Heuristic Introduction

    PROD-37 Data Management & Digital Twin

    Carrington Storm Motors Forge — Aegis-Forge I Thermal Cascade Inductive Material Separator

    Williams Heuristic — Architectural Clarity

    Constraint (The Lock)

    The Forge's physics demands a data architecture that cannot exist in conventional IT/OT frameworks. A 2200°C induction furnace with 384 dielectric FBG sensors at 125 Hz, GaN inverters at 100 kHz, SIL-3 SIFs on TSN, and a physically air-gapped network generates a multi-rate sensor stream that no standard historian, SCADA, or digital twin platform can ingest, fuse, and act upon within the process time constants. Conventional data management assumes: (a) IP-connected networks with centralized historians, (b) uniform sampling rates (typically 1 Hz), (c) copper Ethernet with standard protocols (OPC-UA, MQTT), (d) cloud-based analytics with second-to-minute latency, (e) separate IT/OT security domains with firewalls. The Forge violates all five: the network is physically air-gapped (no IP routes OT↔IT), sampling spans 50 kHz (AE) to 1 Hz (gas) across four control hierarchy levels, the fieldbus is PMMA POF (immune to EMI/GIC), analytics must run at 10 Hz on a 512-core HPC to close the control loop, and the only OT→IT path is a hardware data diode with protocol break. The constraint is physics — thermal diffusion (ms), EM resonance (μs), material transformation (100 ms), and GIC immunity (ns) operate at time scales that cannot be bridged by conventional data architectures. The air-gap is not a policy — it is a dielectric requirement.

    Necessity (The Key)

    The empirical gap is the absence of any data management framework that fuses multi-rate, all-dielectric sensor streams into a real-time digital twin that drives control, safety, maintenance, training, and fleet optimization simultaneously. No existing platform addresses: (a) 384-channel FBG thermal reconstruction at 1 kHz feeding a 10 Hz CFD-FEA-EM coupled twin, (b) autoencoder anomaly detection on 384-dim FBG state running in the twin at 10 Hz with <1 s detection latency, (c) Bayesian fleet parameter updates from twin posteriors propagating to supply chain (CMF-RQT), training (RCT), and HFE (HSCT) tensors, (d) hardware data diode as the only OT→IT path with merkle-verified integrity at 10 Hz, (e) blockchain-anchored data lineage for regulatory (EPA, NRC, ITAR) and liability traceability. The solution is inevitable because the Forge's physics demands it: the same FBG wavelength that measures drum temperature at 125 Hz also detects tamper (PROD-36); the same thermal-admittance operator that drives PID at 1 kHz (PROD-23) drives the twin at 10 Hz; the same POD-Galerkin ROM (12 modes, 118× speedup) that enables Monte Carlo UQ also generates training scenarios (PROD-34). Data management cannot be bolted on — it must be architected into the dielectric control fabric.

    Commitment (The Turn)

    1.1 Purpose & Scope

    This document establishes the Configuration Management (CM) program for the Aegis-Forge I Thermal Cascade Inductive Material Separator, governing all hardware, software, firmware, documentation, and data configurations across the system lifecycle — from design through manufacturing, deployment, operations, maintenance, and Phoenix Protocol circular returns.

    The CM program implements IEC 61508 (Functional Safety), AS9100 (Aerospace Quality), NQA-1 (Nuclear Quality), ISO 10007 (Configuration Management), and IEC 62443 (Industrial Cybersecurity) requirements in a unified framework tailored to the Forge's unique constraints: zero-metal hot zone, all-dielectric control network, physical air-gap, and Carrington-class GIC immunity.

    1.2 CM Program Principles

    PrincipleForge Implementation -------------------------------- Single Source of TruthGit monorepo (this document's repository) — all PROD/FOLLOW docs, firmware, configs, schemas versioned together TraceabilityEvery artifact linked via UUID to requirements, tests, changes, and deployment instances Baseline IntegrityFour baselines (As-Designed, As-Built, As-Maintained, As-Operated) maintained with signed gates Change ControlECO process with classification, impact analysis, multi-discipline review, staged deployment AuditabilityImmutable Git history + blockchain anchors (DQR) + quarterly internal / annual external audits Cyber IntegritySigned firmware, SBOM per release, secure boot, SLSA Level 3 build pipeline (PROD-36)

    1.3 Configuration Item (CI) Taxonomy

    All configuration items are classified into the following hierarchy:

    CI-01  SYSTEM CONFIGURATION
  CI-01-01  Forge Instance (site-specific: Forge-001, Forge-002, ...)
  CI-01-02  System Architecture Baseline (PROD-01, PROD-23, PROD-38)
  CI-01-03  Interface Control Documents (ICDs) — all internal/external interfaces


    CI-02  HARDWARE CONFIGURATION
  CI-02-01  Drum Assembly (ZrB₂-SiC, liner zones, FBG embeds, ports) — serialized
  CI-02-02  BFRP Pressure Vessel (filament wound, aerogel, glaze, flanges) — serialized
  CI-02-03  Induction Coil Bank (8 zones, windings, supports, water cooling) — lot tracked
  CI-02-04  Port Valve System (Ti₃AlC₂ actuators, ceramic pistons, PEEK seals) — serialized
  CI-02-05  Carousel & Feed System (BFRP shredder, LIBS, magnetic sep) — serialized
  CI-02-06  Gas Capture & Fume Solidification (scrubbers, plasma torch, carbon beds)
  CI-02-07  Slug Cooling & Output (ZrO₂ molds, quench system, mass spec)
  CI-02-08  Frame & Foundation (BFRP, seismic isolation, thermal breaks)
  CI-02-09  Ancillary Equipment (cranes, hoists, tooling, fixturing)
    


    CI-03  ELECTRONICS & FIRMWARE CONFIGURATION
  CI-03-01  L0 FPGA Bitstreams (8× Zone RTU, 1× SIS, 1× PTP GM) — signed, versioned
  CI-03-02  L1 RTU Firmware (Zephyr RTOS, thermal PID, PLL, FBG driver) — SemVer
  CI-03-03  L2 PLC Programs (8× Stage PLC, IEC 61131-3, SIS logic) — signed
  CI-03-04  L3 SCADA Software (Linux, InfluxDB, OPC-UA, Kafka, HMI) — containerized
  CI-03-05  Digital Twin HPC Software (CFD/FEA/EM/ML containers) — versioned
  CI-03-06  Inverter GaN Driver Firmware (bootloader, Class E tuning LUT) — signed
  CI-03-07  TSN Switch Firmware (gate control lists, VLAN config, PTP) — signed
  CI-03-08  Data Diode Firmware (protocol translation, merkle, rate limit) — signed
    


    CI-04  DOCUMENTATION CONFIGURATION
  CI-04-01  Product Documents (PROD-01 through PROD-40) — this repo, Git tags
  CI-04-02  Follow-up Documents (FOLLOW-01 through FOLLOW-40) — this repo
  CI-04-03  Heuristic Intros (Williams/Keymaker/El Segundo/Combined) — this repo
  CI-04-04  Test & Evaluation Specs (PROD-39, CT procedures) — this repo
  CI-04-05  Operations & Maintenance Manuals (PROD-29, 30) — this repo
  CI-04-06  Training Curriculum (PROD-34 DQR blockchain) — this repo
  CI-04-07  Regulatory Submissions (PROD-32 permits, certifications) — this repo
    


    CI-05  DATA & MODEL CONFIGURATION
  CI-05-01  Material Property Database (50+ materials, Hermite correlations) — PROD-24
  CI-05-02  ROM Export (POD-Galerkin, 12 modes, JSON) — PROD-24, PROD-37
  CI-05-03  ML Model Cards (autoencoder, CPAT, ROM surrogate) — PROD-37, FOLLOW-29
  CI-05-04  Fleet Parameter Posteriors (HMC chains, 20 params) — PROD-37
  CI-05-05  Sensor Calibration Data (FBG λ₀, TC curves, EM gains) — per-instance
  CI-05-06  Digital Twin State Snapshots (merkle roots, 10 Hz) — blockchain anchored
    


    CI-06  SUPPLIER CONFIGURATION
  CI-06-01  AVL Baseline (Tier 1: 12 critical, Tier 2: 47 standard) — PROD-33
  CI-06-02  First Article Data (FA-01 through FA-14 per supplier) — signed
  CI-06-03  Supplier Change Notifications (SCN) — tracked to ECO
  CI-06-04  Requalification Records (periodic, change-triggered) — PROD-28
