    2.3 Commit & Tag Conventions

    Commit Message Format: 

    ():   [ECO-XXXX]
    


    


    Signed-off-by: Name 
GPG-Signature:

    Types: feat (new capability), fix (defect correction), docs (documentation), config (configuration), cm (CM process), security (cyber), safety (SIL-3), test (test updates), chore (maintenance)

    Tag Format:

    • prod-v.. — Production baseline (e.g., prod-v3.2.1)
    • fat-v. — FAT baseline (e.g., fat-v1.0)
    • sat-v. — SAT baseline (e.g., sat-v1.0)
    • eco- — ECO implementation (e.g., eco-1042)
    • fpga-v.. — L0 FPGA bitstream
    • rtu-v.. — L1 RTU firmware
    • plc-v.. — L2 PLC program
    • scada-v.. — L3 SCADA software
    • twin-v.. — Digital twin software
    • rom-v.. — ROM export (PROD-24)
    • ml-v.. — ML models (PROD-37)
    • sec-v.. — Security baseline (PROD-36)

    Git Tag Chain (Cryptographic Proof): 

    fpga-v1.3.7 → rtu-v2.1.4 → plc-v3.0.1 → scada-v1.2.0 → twin-v2.0.0
    ↓            ↓            ↓            ↓            ↓
prod-v3.2.1 ← fat-v1.0 ← sat-v1.0 ← eco-1042 ← eco-1038

    2.4 Signed Commits & Verification

    • All commits to main/release branches MUST be GPG-signed (developer YubiKey or HSM)
    • CI pipeline verifies signatures — rejects unsigned commits
    • GitHub Vigilant Mode enabled — flags unverified signatures
    • Commit signature chain provides cryptographic provenance from requirements → code → test → deployment

    3. Engineering Change Order (ECO) Process

    3.1 ECO Classification

    ClassCriteriaMax Lead TimeApprovalDeployment ------------------------------------------------------ CriticalSafety (SIL-3), Security (SL-C), Regulatory, Data integrity72 hoursCCB unanimous + Safety + CyberStaged: 1 zone → 1 stage → full (CT-04 re-test each) MajorPerformance, reliability, new capability, interface change30 daysCCB majority + discipline leadsStaged: 1 zone → 1 stage → full (CT-04 partial) MinorBug fix, documentation, parameter tuning, cosmetic14 daysDiscipline lead + CMDirect to next release branch DocumentationSpec clarification, typo, format, non-technical7 daysCM onlyDirect to main EmergencyProduction stoppage, imminent safety/security risk4 hoursCM + Safety (verbal), CCB ratification within 24hDirect to main + hotfix tag, CT-04 within 7 days

    3.2 ECO Lifecycle

    ┌─────────────┐     ┌─────────────┐     ┌─────────────┐     ┌─────────────┐
│  INITIATE   │────►│  ANALYZE    │────►│   REVIEW    │────►│  APPROVE    │
│  (Any role) │     │  (Originator)│     │   (CCB)     │     │  (CCB/Lead) │
└─────────────┘     └─────────────┘     └─────────────┘     └──────┬──────┘
                                                                     │
                    ┌─────────────┐     ┌─────────────┐     ┌────────┴──────┐
                    │   CLOSE     │◄────│  VERIFY     │◄────│  IMPLEMENT    │
                    │  (Originator)│     │  (QA/Ops)   │     │  (Developers) │
                    └─────────────┘     └─────────────┘     └───────────────┘

    Detailed Steps:

    1. INITIATE — Any role submits ECO request via GitHub Issue template:

    • Title: ECO-XXXX: -
    • Description: Problem statement, proposed change, affected CIs, urgency
    • Auto-assigned ECO number (sequential)

    2. ANALYZE — Originator (with discipline leads) performs:

    • Impact analysis: affected CIs, test cases, downstream documents, suppliers
    • Risk assessment: SIL-3 impact (PROD-23 Table 6.2), cyber impact (PROD-36 CPAT), schedule
    • Implementation plan: branch name, tasks, test requirements, rollback procedure
    • Cost/schedule estimate

    3. REVIEW — CCB convenes (weekly for Major, ad-hoc for Critical/Emergency):

    • Safety Engineering: SIL-3 impact verdict (no impact / re-analysis / re-cert)
    • Cyber Security: SL-C impact, firmware signing, SBOM update, supply chain
    • QA: Test plan adequacy, NCR linkage, FA requirements
    • Operations: Production impact, recipe changes, operator retraining
    • Supply Chain: AVL impact, SCN issuance, requalification needs
    • Training: DQR impact, simulator updates, curriculum changes

    4. APPROVE — CCB decision recorded in GitHub Issue:

    • Approved: Implementation branch created, ECO moves to IMPLEMENT
    • Conditional: Approved with mandatory conditions (additional test, phased deploy)
    • Deferred: Moved to backlog with rationale
    • Rejected: Closed with rationale

    5. IMPLEMENT — Developers work on feature/eco-XXXX branch:

    • All changes in single branch (atomic ECO)
    • Signed commits, PR to release branch
    • CI passes: lint, typecheck, test, signature-verify, split-chunks-verify
    • Documentation updated (PROD docs, intros, cross-references)

    6. VERIFY — QA validates implementation:

    • Unit/integration tests pass (mutation >90%)
    • CT tests executed per test plan (PROD-39)
    • Regression: prior FAT/SAT baselines re-run (automated in CI)
    • Digital twin validation: ROM/ML model cards updated (PROD-37)

    7. CLOSE — Originator confirms:

    • All acceptance criteria met
    • As-Built/As-Maintained/As-Operated baselines updated
    • DQR blockchain updated (PROD-28, 34)
    • ECO Issue closed with Closed: ECO-XXXX verified in prod-vX.Y.Z

    3.3 ECO Metrics & KPIs

    MetricTargetMeasurement ----------------------------- Critical ECO cycle time≤ 72 hoursInitiate → Approve Major ECO cycle time≤ 30 daysInitiate → Approve ECO rejection rate< 10%Rejected / Total submitted Emergency ECO ratio< 5% of totalEmergency / Total approved Post-deployment defects0 Critical, ≤ 2 Major/quarterPROD-28 NCRs linked to ECO Rollback frequency0 per yearHotfix reverts

    4.3 Baseline Integrity Verification

    Per Baseline Gate (Automated in CI): 

    verify_baseline(baseline_tag):
  1. Git tag exists and is signed by CM key
  2. All CIs in baseline have CUUIDs
  3. Cross-reference matrix complete (PROD-38 Sec 13)
  4. For As-Built: all CT tests passed, FA data packages signed
  5. For As-Operated: twin merkle chain intact, recipes versioned
  6. Blockchain anchor verified (DQR, 3 org signatures)
  7. SBOM generated and signed for all firmware (CI-03)
  8. PROD-24 ROM export checksum matches tag
  9. PROD-37 ML model cards versioned
  10. PROD-36 CPAT parameters versioned

    Failure Action: CI pipeline blocks tag creation; manual CM override required with NCR.

5. VALIDATE: 30-min soak, zero spurious alarms, twin sync <3σ
6. AUTHORIZE: Shift Lead + Safety Engineer dual-key → resume production
7. DOCUMENT: NCR auto-generated, ECO if permanent, lessons learned

4. SCADA: Container image digest vs. signed SBOM → mismatch = alert
5. Twin: ROM/ML model checksums vs. Git tags → mismatch = alert

    Combined Heuristic Introduction

    PROD-38 Configuration Management

    Carrington Storm Motors Forge — Aegis-Forge I Thermal Cascade Inductive Material Separator

    Williams Heuristic — Architectural Clarity

    Constraint (The Lock)

    The Forge cannot be configured by conventional CM systems. A 2200°C induction furnace with zero-metal hot zone, 384 dielectric FBG sensors, GaN inverters at 100 kHz, SIL-3 SIFs on TSN, physical air-gap, and a Phoenix Protocol circular supply chain has no precedent in any CM framework. Conventional CM assumes: (a) metallic hardware with standard part numbers, (b) copper Ethernet with IP-addressable devices, (c) software/firmware deployed via network, (d) centralized historian with SQL backend, (e) supplier management via ERP with standard BOMs. The Forge violates all five: hardware is ceramic/composite with QR-coded UUIDs, network is PMMA POF with no IP addresses, firmware updates via hardware data diode + TUF, historian is InfluxDB on air-gapped SCADA with merkle integrity, suppliers provide in-house synthesized materials with flash-sinter trial data. The constraint is physics — a single untracked configuration change in the drum liner thickness alters thermal stress by 35 MPa (PROD-24); a single unsigned firmware bitstream destroys GaN drivers at 6 V threshold; a single unverified supplier powder batch causes 1000× resistivity flash failure. The configuration baseline is not a database — it is a dielectric requirement.

    Necessity (The Key)

    The empirical gap is the absence of any CM framework that manages configuration across four physical baselines (As-Designed, As-Built, As-Maintained, As-Operated) linked by UUIDs, with firmware signed by HSM triads, distributed via TUF over a hardware data diode, validated by digital twin at 10 Hz, and anchored to blockchain for regulatory traceability. No existing standard addresses: (a) CUUID linkage across design/build/maintain/operate for ceramic/composite hardware with no metal tags, (b) SemVer firmware for FPGA/RTU/PLC/SCADA/Twin with triple HSM signatures (Builder+CM+Safety), (c) TUF repository with in-toto attestations distributing over unidirectional data diode, (c) ROM/ML model versioning tied to Git tags with PROD-24/37 validation gates, (d) supplier AVL with 12 Tier 1 requiring SLSA Level 3, SBOM, pen test, secure boot, (e) DR with 4-hour RTO using cold standby golden images validated by CT-04 SIF proof tests. The solution is inevitable because the Forge's physics demands it: the same Git tag chain that versions PROD documents versions the FPGA bitstream that drives the GaN switch that creates the magnetic field that heats the drum that the FBG measures — one cryptographic chain from requirements to physics.

    Commitment (The Turn)

    This document commits to three non-negotiables: 1. Single Git monorepo as source of truth — All PROD/FOLLOW docs, firmware, configs, schemas, ROM, ML models, AVL, curriculum versioned together with signed commits, protected branches, tag chain fpga→rtu→plc→scada→twin→prod. No external CM tool, no separate databases. 2. Four baselines immutable via CUUID — Every configuration item carries a Configuration UUID linking As-Designed tag, As-Built FA data, As-Maintained PM records, As-Operated twin state. Broken linkage = NCR auto-generated, production hold. 3. Triple-signature firmware chain — Every SFP signed by HSM-Builder (provenance), HSM-CM (authorization), HSM-Safety (SIL-3 envelope). No firmware deploys without all three. TUF repository enforces this at data diode ingress.

    These commitments are irreversible. They define the Forge's configuration immune system. Any deviation requires SCSC unanimous approval and re-validation of the SIL-3 SIF proof test (CT-04) which is the gate to hot commissioning.

    Keymaker Heuristic — Implementation Precision

    The Empirical Lock

    Fabrication fidelity gap: Conventional CM tools — GitLab, GitHub Enterprise, Azure DevOps, Jira + Confluence, Polarion, Jama, DOORS — assume: (a) IP-connected repositories with web-based review, (b) standard SemVer for software only, hardware tracked separately in PLM/ERP, (c) firmware deployed via network (Jenkins, ArgoCD, Flux), (d) supplier data in ERP with manual BOM sync, (e) DR via cloud backup/restore with RTO hours-days. They cannot model: (a) physically air-gapped Git repo where the only CI/CD is sneakernet + data diode pull, (b) unified SemVer across FPGA bitstream, RTU firmware, PLC program, SCADA containers, Twin software, ROM export, ML models — all in one tag chain, (c) firmware distribution via TUF over hardware data diode with staged rollout (1 zone → 1 stage → full) gated by CT-04 SIF proof tests, (d) CUUID linking As-Designed Git tag → As-Built FA data package → As-Maintained PM record → As-Operated twin merkle root, (e) supplier AVL as versioned YAML in Git with SCN-triggered ECOs, FA requirements per tier, requal periods. The lock is that no existing CM tool computes the Forge's configuration physics where the Git tag IS the firmware signature, the CUUID IS the hardware traceability, the TUF target IS the deployment gate, the CT-04 test IS the merge criterion, and the blockchain anchor IS the audit evidence.

    The Mathematical Key

    The single computational primitive is the Baseline Convergence Operator (BCO) evaluated at each ECO gate: 
    BCO[ECO, CI_set, baseline_set] → {PASS, FAIL, CONDITIONAL}


    baseline_set = {
  As_Designed:   tag_d  // Git tag, signed, cross-ref matrix valid
  As_Built:      tag_b  // FA data packages signed, CT-01..10 passed
  As_Maintained: tag_m  // PM records current, spares match, mods tracked
  As_Operated:   tag_o  // Recipes versioned, twin sync <3σ, certs valid
}
    


    CUUID = hash(tag_d tag_btag_mtag_o CI_spec_hash)
    


    ECO_gate(eco_class):
  if eco_class == CRITICAL:
    require: BCO(eco, CI_affected, {tag_d', tag_b, tag_m, tag_o}) == PASS
           ∧ CT-04 partial-stroke (6 SIFs) PASS
           ∧ Safety + Cyber unanimous
  if eco_class == MAJOR:
    require: BCO(eco, CI_affected, {tag_d', tag_b', tag_m', tag_o'}) == PASS
           ∧ CT-04 full proof (24 SIFs) PASS
           ∧ CCB majority
  if eco_class == MINOR:
    require: BCO(eco, CI_affected, {tag_d'}) == PASS

    2.2 CT-01: Drum Rotordynamics — Detailed Procedure

    Objective: Verify drum dynamic behavior matches FEA predictions (PROD-25) and is free of critical speed interference through operating range.

    ParameterSpecificationMeasurement Method --------------------------------------------- 1st Critical Speed>1890 RPM (2.37× operating max 800 RPM)Impact hammer + accelerometers, sweep 0-3000 RPM Balance GradeISO 21940-11 G0.4Multi-plane balancing at 500 RPM Synchronous Vibration<25 μm p-p at 500 RPMNon-contact proximity probes (x2, 90°) Asynchronous Vibration<50 μm p-p (sub-synchronous)Same probes, full spectrum FBG Strain CorrelationModal strain <800 με (Si₃N₄ pins)128 FBG channels @ 125 Hz during sweep

    Acceptance Criteria:

    • [ ] 1st critical speed ≥ 1890 RPM (FEA: 2100 RPM predicted)
    • [ ] Balance grade G0.4 achieved
    • [ ] Synchronous vibration <25 μm p-p at 500 RPM
    • [ ] No sub-synchronous instability observed
    • [ ] FBG strain <800 με at all channels during sweep
    • [ ] Rotordynamics model updated with measured critical speeds

    Test Setup:

    • Drum mounted on BFRP frame with seismic isolators (PROD-25 stiffness)
    • 128 FBG channels active (125 Hz), 8 accelerometers (10 kHz)
    • Helmholtz coil off (no GIC), TSN network active (time sync)
    • Digital twin (PROD-37) running in shadow mode at 10 Hz

    2.3 CT-02: Vessel Hydrotest — Detailed Procedure

    Objective: Verify BFRP vessel pressure integrity and aerogel/glaze performance under design pressure.

    ParameterSpecificationMeasurement Method --------------------------------------------- Test Pressure15 bar N₂ (1.5× design 10 bar)Certified pressure gauge ±0.1% FS Hold Duration30 minutes minimumTimer + pressure logging Pressure DropZero (temperature compensated)ΔP/ΔT correction using FBG vessel strain Helium Leak Rate<1×10⁻⁶ mbar·L/sHe mass spectrometer sniffer all joints Aerogel IR BaselineUniform external surface ΔT <5°CIR camera (FLIR A6750) at 10 bar hold AE Baseline<5 hits/min @ 10 bar8-channel AE (R15α, 100 kHz-1 MHz)

    Acceptance Criteria:

    • [ ] Zero pressure drop (temp compensated) over 30 min hold
    • [ ] Zero helium leaks >1×10⁻⁶ mbar·L/s at all joints/flanges
    • [ ] External IR ΔT <5°C (validates aerogel λ=0.010 W/m·K)
    • [ ] AE baseline <5 hits/min @ 10 bar (Felicity ratio >1.0)
    • [ ] No audible emissions, no visible deformation
    • [ ] Post-test UT delamination scan clean (ASTM E2700)

    2.4 CT-03: Flange Leak Test — Detailed Procedure

    Objective: Verify all 24 bolted flange joints (vessel-to-drum, vessel-to-port, port-to-valve) meet leak tightness.

    Joint GroupQuantityTest MethodAcceptance ------------------------------------------------ Vessel-to-Drum (2 flanges)24 bolts eachHe sniffer + bubble test<1×10⁻⁶ mbar·L/s Vessel-to-Port (8 flanges)12 bolts eachHe sniffer + bubble test<1×10⁻⁶ mbar·L/s Port-to-Valve (8 flanges)8 bolts eachHe sniffer + bubble test<1×10⁻⁶ mbar·L/s Total44 joints, 400 bolts

    Procedure: 1. Torque all bolts per SG-2 ceremony (160 N·m ±5 N·m, dual-verify, AE monitoring) 2. Pressurize system to 10 bar N₂ 3. Sniff each bolt circle with He mass spectrometer 4. Apply leak detection fluid (Snoop® equivalent) to each bolt 5. Record leak rate and location for any indication 6. Depressurize, re-torque any leaking joints, re-test

    Acceptance Criteria:

    • [ ] All 44 joints <1×10⁻⁶ mbar·L/s
    • [ ] Torque retention >95% of initial 160 N·m after test
    • [ ] AE monitoring during torque: no hits >40 dB

    Objective: Verify all 24 SIL-3 Safety Instrumented Functions trip within <50 ms with 2oo3 voting agreement on TSN VLAN 10.

    This is the single most critical test — FAILURE = NO SHIPMENT.

    2.5.2 Proof Test Procedure

    FOR EACH SIF (1-24):
  1. VERIFY test equipment calibrated, TSN VLAN 10 operational, PTP <1μs
  2. CONFIGURE SIS test mode (bypasses process interlocks, enables trip injection)
  3. INJECT trip condition per setpoint table above

      

    • Temperature: FBG simulator injects wavelength shift
      • 

    • Pressure: Pressure calibrator injects signal to 3 PTs
      • 

    • Speed: Encoder simulator injects frequency
      • 

    • GIC: Helmholtz coil 100 A/m, 5000 nT/s ramp
      • 

    • Cyber: CPAT injects synthetic anomaly Λ_CP >100
      • 

    
  4. MEASURE:
     a. Trip time (t_trip) = time from injection to final element action
     b. 2oo3 vote agreement = all 3 sensors agree within 1 TSN cycle (1ms)
     c. SOE timestamp alignment = max Δt <1 ms across zones
     d. FBG data freeze = all 384 channels capture trip instant
  5. RECORD: t_trip, vote, SOE, FBG freeze frame, Λ_CP (if SIF-24)
  6. RESET: Clear trip, verify auto-reset logic (where applicable)
  7. VERIFY: t_trip <50 ms, 2oo3 = PASS, SOE aligned, FBG freeze captured


    AGGREGATE ACCEPTANCE:

      

    • All 24 SIFs: t_trip <50 ms (target <30 ms)
      • 

    • All 24 SIFs: 2oo3 vote = PASS
      • 

    • All 24 SIFs: SOE timestamps aligned <1 ms
      • 

    • PFD_avg calculation (IEC 61508-6) <1×10⁻³ per SIF
      • 

    • SIF-16 (Optical E-stop): t_trip <10 ms
      • 

    • SIF-17 (FPGA Desat): t_trip <1 μs (verified at L0)
      • 

    


    DOCUMENTATION:

      

    • CT-04 Test Report with all 24 SIF data sheets
      • 

    • PFD_avg calculation sheets per SIF
      • 

    • SOE log export (CSV, blockchain anchored)
      • 

    • FBG freeze frame archive (384 channels × 24 SIFs)
      • 

    • SIS Engineer witness signature (Gate CT-04)

    Heuristic Intro (Combined): PROD-39

    Combined Heuristic Introduction

    PROD-39 Test & Evaluation Specification

    Carrington Storm Motors Forge — Aegis-Forge I Thermal Cascade Inductive Material Separator

    Williams Heuristic — Architectural Clarity

    Constraint (The Lock)

    The Forge cannot be tested by conventional T&E frameworks. A 2200°C induction furnace with zero-metal hot zone, 384 dielectric FBG sensors, GaN inverters at 100 kHz, SIL-3 SIFs on TSN, physical air-gap, and a Phoenix Protocol circular supply chain has no precedent in any test standard. Conventional T&E assumes: (a) metallic test articles with electrical instrumentation, (b) copper Ethernet for data acquisition, (c) separate test phases (DT/OT) with network connectivity, (d) software testing on standard OS/hardware, (e) environmental test standards for metallic structures. The Forge violates all five: test instrumentation is photonic (FBG, POF), data acquisition is on air-gapped TSN with PTP <1 μs, test phases are unified in a single continuous CT-01..10 sequence, firmware runs on Zephyr RTOS/FPGA with DO-178C DAL A equivalence, and seismic/GIC tests must verify zero-metal integrity. The constraint is physics — a single copper thermocouple in the test setup becomes a GIC antenna; a single network cable to the test DAQ violates the air-gap; a single software test without SIL-3 proof invalidates the SIF envelope. The test specification is not a document — it is a dielectric requirement.

    Necessity (The Key)

    The empirical gap is the absence of any T&E framework that validates a zero-metal, air-gapped, SIL-3, Carrington-immune system across physics, cyber, human factors, and regulatory dimensions simultaneously. No existing standard addresses: (a) CT-04 as the single gate for 24 SIL-3 SIFs with <50 ms trip on optical TSN, (b) FBG-as-primary-metrology for both process control AND test verification (384 channels at 125 Hz), (c) digital twin (PROD-37) as continuous test oracle running at 10 Hz with <3σ sync, (d) cyber-physical red team scenarios (IR-01..06) combining GIC storm with coordinated cyber attack, (e) HFE validation where operators witness the phenomenon into existence at four non-automatable gates (SG-2, SG-3, CT-04, SAT-05). The solution is inevitable because the Forge's physics demands it: the same TSN network that carries SIF trips at <50 ms carries test data; the same FBG that measures temperature detects tamper; the same PTP that synchronizes resonance tracking timestamps SOE for SIF proof; the same digital twin that drives control validates test results. Testing cannot be a phase — it must be architected into the dielectric control fabric.

    Commitment (The Turn)

    This document commits to three non-negotiables: 1. CT-04 is the shipment gate — All 24 SIL-3 SIFs must trip <50 ms with 2oo3 agreement on TSN VLAN 10, PFD_avg <1×10⁻³. No Forge ships without full CT-04 PASS with SIS Engineer witness signature. 2. Digital twin is the continuous test oracle — PROD-37 twin shadows all tests at 10 Hz; sync drift >3σ = auto-NCR; twin-process reconciliation required post every test. The twin validates the test, the test validates the twin. 3. Human witness gates are non-automatable — SG-2 (flange torque), SG-3 (FBG calibration), CT-04 (SIS proof), SAT-05 (first hot batch) require human judgment that transforms data into certification. No algorithm replaces the witness.

    These commitments are irreversible. They define the Forge's test immune system. Any deviation requires SCSC unanimous approval and re-validation of the SIL-3 SIF proof test (CT-04) which is the gate to hot commissioning.

    Keymaker Heuristic — Implementation Precision

    The Empirical Lock

    Fabrication fidelity gap: Conventional T&E frameworks — MIL-STD-810, IEEE 1220, DO-178C, ASME V&V 40, IEC 61508 — assume: (a) test articles with metallic instrumentation ports, (b) network-connected test DAQ with centralized analysis, (c) separate developmental/operational test phases, (d) software V&V on COTS OS/hardware, (e) environmental tests on metallic structures with standard grounding. They cannot model: (a) zero-metal test article where the test instrumentation (FBG, POF) IS the production sensorium, (b) air-gapped test network where the only data path is the production TSN with frozen gate control lists, (c) unified CT-01..10 sequence where component/module/subsystem/system tests are one continuous physics validation, (d) firmware V&V on Zephyr/FPGA with DO-178C DAL A equivalence AND SLSA Level 3 build pipeline, (e) seismic/GIC tests that verify the ABSENCE of metallic paths as the primary immunity mechanism. The lock is that no existing T&E framework computes the Forge's test physics where the test IS the process, the sensor IS the witness, the twin IS the oracle, and the human IS the certifier at four irreducible gates.

    The Mathematical Key

    The single computational primitive is the Recursive Bayesian Test Oracle (RBTO) executed across four test scales: 
    Test_Oracle[test_scale, data_sources, reference_models] → {PASS, FAIL, CONDITIONAL}


    test_scale ∈ {MICRO, MESO, MACRO, META}
    


    MICRO (per channel, seconds):
  data = {FBG_λ, UT_A-scan, AE_hit, IR_ΔT, vib_spectrum}
  reference = {PQR_calibration, DAC_curve, AE_baseline, IR_baseline, vib_baseline}
  Λ = P(data degradation) / P(data nominal)
  decision = PASS if Λ < 10 else NCR_auto
    


    MESO (per component, hours):
  data = {UT_volumetric, CT_porosity, FBG_survival, thermal_cycle_strain, hydrotest_hold}
  reference = {FEA_prediction, process_signature, material_certificate}
  health_state = Bayesian_fusion(data, reference, prior_from_MICRO)
  decision = PASS if P(intact) > 0.999 else NCR_CAPA
    


    MACRO (per system, days):
  data = {CT-01..10 results, SIF_trip_times, SOE_alignment, twin_sync, gas_emissions}
  reference = {PROD-23/24/25/26/27/31/32/37 requirements}
  system_ready = ∧(all_SIFs_PASS) ∧ (twin_sync < 3σ) ∧ (mass_balance > 99%)
  decision = SHIP if system_ready else HOLD
    


    META (per fleet, months):
  data = {all_Forges_MICRO_MESO_MACRO, field_failures, NCR_trends, twin_posteriors}
  reference = {PROD-37 fleet_learning, PROD-28 Bayesian_priors}
  parameter_guards = tighten(priors, fleet_data)
  decision = ECO if guards_tightened else CONTINUE

    This one oracle generates the entire T&E program: FAT procedures, SAT procedures, SIF proof matrix, cyber scenarios, HFE scenarios, environmental tests, reliability demo, SW/FW V&V, twin V&V, regulatory tests. Every test procedure in this document is an instantiation of RBTO at a specific scale with specific data sources.

    The atomic computation is the likelihood ratio test — the same as PROD-28 Keymaker Key: 

    Λ = P(observation degradation) / P(observation nominal)
    


    observation = {FBG_drift, UT_amplitude, AE_energy, IR_hotspot, SIF_trip_time, SOE_alignment,
               TSN_frame_timing, PTP_offset, firmware_hash, merkle_root, operator_action}
    


    P(obs degradation) = ∏ P(source_i degradation)  [conditional independence]

    2. Horizon 1: Gen-II Evolution (2026-2029)

    2.1 2000L Scale-Up — From 226L to 2000L Working Volume

    The Gen-I drum (600 mm diameter × 800 mm length = 226 L) validates the physics. Gen-II targets 2000L (9× volume) for industrial throughput while maintaining thermal gradient fidelity.

    2.1.1 Geometric Scaling Laws

    Gen-I:  D = 600 mm, L = 800 mm, V = 226 L, A = 1.51 m²
Gen-II: D = 1200 mm, L = 1800 mm, V = 2035 L, A = 6.79 m²

    Scaling ratios:

    • Volume ratio: (1200/600)² × (1800/800) = 9.0×
    • Surface area ratio: (1200/600) × (1800/800) = 4.5×
    • Aspect ratio L/D preserved: 800/600 = 1.33 → 1800/1200 = 1.50 (adjusted for thermal gradient length)

    Critical constraint — Thermal gradient preservation: The 8-stage temperature profile requires sufficient axial length for discrete zones. Gen-I has 8 zones × 100 mm = 800 mm active length. Gen-II requires ≥ 1600 mm for equivalent zone resolution at 2× diameter. 1800 mm provides margin for transition zones.

    2.1.2 Structural Scaling — ZrB₂-SiC Drum

    Wall thickness scaling (pressure vessel criterion): Hoop stress σ_θ = P·r/t. For constant pressure (5 bar operating, 10 bar design): t_gen2 = t_gen1 × (r_gen2/r_gen1) = 35 mm × (600/300) = 70 mm minimum

    Reality check — Ceramic drum at 1200 mm diameter with 70 mm wall:

    • Mass: π × (0.65² - 0.58²) × 1.8 × 3200 kg/m³ = ~4.2 metric tons (vs Gen-I ~650 kg)
    • Flash sintering: Requires 2.5 m × 2.5 m sintering furnace (new capital)
    • Thermal shock: ΔT across 70 mm wall at 2400°C surface = 120°C gradient (FEA validated in PROD-24)

    Alternative — Segmented drum architecture: 8 × 200 mm axial segments, each independently replaceable. Joint design: ZrB₂-SiC tongue-and-groove with PEEK CF40 compliant layer (PROD-09 valve seat heritage). Reduces single-piece sintering risk; enables staged replacement.

    2.1.3 Induction Power Scaling

    Gen-I: 500 kW total, 8 zones × 62.5 kW average
Gen-II: Target 4 MW total, 8 zones × 500 kW average

    Frequency strategy preserved:

    • Stages 1-2: 100 kHz → 50 kW/zone (indirect heating via susceptor)
    • Stage 3: 50 kHz → 200 kW/zone
    • Stages 4-5: 10 kHz → 500 kW/zone (Al window)
    • Stage 6: 5 kHz → 500 kW/zone (Cu window)
    • Stage 7: 2 kHz → 750 kW/zone (Fe window)
    • Stage 8: 1 kHz → 1000 kW/zone (mineral window)

    3.3.2 Simplified Cascade (4-Stage)

    ASTEROID AEGIS-FORGE — METALLIC SEPARATION ONLY


    Stage 0: Acoustic (microgravity — capillary/acoustic hybrid)
Stage 1: Skip (no volatiles)
Stage 2: Skip (no organics)
Stage 3: Skip (no organics)
Stage 4: Ni-Co-PGM separation (1455°C Ni, 1495°C Co) → Centrifugal density strat
Stage 5: Fe separation (1538°C) → Bulk Fe output
Stage 6: PGM concentration (density >20 g/cm³) → Ultra-centrifuge zone
Stage 7: Refractory residue (W, Re, Mo if present)
Stage 8: Slag (minimal)

    Microgravity separation physics: In microgravity, centrifugal force IS the effective gravity. Drum at 500 RPM, r=0.6m → 167 G. Density stratification occurs radially:

    • Inner radius: Fe (7.87 g/cm³)
    • Mid radius: Ni-Co (8.9 g/cm³)
    • Outer radius: PGM (12-22 g/cm³)

    Port design: Radial ports at calculated density boundaries. No thermal actuators needed — ports opened by commanded drum position.

    3.4 Microgravity Thermal Cascade — Capillary/Centrifugal Hybrid

    Challenge: In microgravity, liquid metals don't "pool at the bottom" — they form spheres held by surface tension. Centrifugal force must overcome surface tension.

    Bond number criterion: Bo = ρ·ω²·r·L²/σ > 10 for reliable separation

    • ρ = 7000 kg/m³ (Fe), σ = 1.8 N/m (Fe surface tension at 1600°C)
    • L = characteristic length (drum radius = 0.6 m)
    • Required ω: ω > √(10·σ/(ρ·r·L²)) = √(10×1.8/(7000×0.6×0.36)) = 0.11 rad/s = 1 RPM

    At 100 RPM (104 rad/s): Bo = 10,000 >> 10. Separation is robust.

    Capillary assist: Helical grooves on drum inner surface (ZrB₂-SiC) guide liquid metal toward ports via capillary wicking (PROD-09 valve heritage). Groove geometry: 2 mm wide × 1 mm deep, 30° helix angle.

    Heuristic Intro (Combined): PROD-40

    PROD-40 Combined Heuristic Introduction

    Williams Keymaker El Segundo — Synthesis

    The Triune Frame

    This document — PROD-40: Future Evolution & Roadmap — is the capstone synthesis of the Aegis-Forge Product Document series (PROD-01 through PROD-39). It does not stand alone; it is the recursive closure of the entire specification tree. The three heuristic lenses reveal its nature:

    Williams (Architectural Clarity) identifies the Constraint: material closure. The machine cannot be sovereign until it reproduces its own bill of materials. The Necessity: staged closure with external subsidy — Gen-II scale, space feedstocks, waste liabilities as negative-cost inputs. The Commitment: invariant cascade physics, All-Aegis fidelity, open-licensed engineering.

    Keymaker (Implementation Precision) identifies the Lock: thermal gradient fidelity across 9× volume, 4× diameter, and four extraterrestrial/remediation boundary conditions. The Key: the Recursive Bayesian Thermal Oracle (RBTO) — one computational primitive governing zone control, batch optimization, feed synthesis, and roadmap gate validation across all horizons. The Turn: Theory→History via virtual commissioning; History→Theory via horizon data feeding the universal thermal model $\mathcal{M}_\theta$.

    El Segundo (Operational Excellence) identifies the Mirror: dual-sensor architecture (physical FBG + virtual RBTO likelihood) reflecting process fidelity and roadmap divergence in real time. The Participation: triad governance (Thermal Architect, Materials Steward, Sovereignty Officer) certifying physics at four recursive ceremonies. The Protocol: Horizon Gate Protocol (HGP) — a mandatory git-enforced sequence of prior extraction, simulation, build, and KL-divergence validation at each scale transition.

    These three lenses are not perspectives on the roadmap. They are the load-bearing structure of the roadmap. Remove Williams, and the roadmap has no strategic necessity — it becomes a wish list. Remove Keymaker, and the roadmap has no technical credibility — it becomes a cartoon. Remove El Segundo, and the roadmap has no operational reality — it becomes a PowerPoint.

    The Cascade Invariants

    The roadmap's technical spine is the invariance of the 8-stage thermal cascade across all horizons. This is not an assumption; it is a verified property of the physics:

    StagePhysicsGen-I (226L)Gen-II (2000L)LunarNuclearMicrogravityOceanUrban ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ 0Acoustic liberation15-30 minScaledSkip (pre-lib)SkipCapillary assistNodule disaggSkip 1Drying/volatiles80-150°CInvariantH₂/He/H₂OH₂O/TritiumSameMoistureSame 2Polymer flow150-450°CInvariantSkipNOx/organicsSkipOrganic CPlastics 3Pyrolysis/char450-700°CInvariantSkipCs/Sr/I volatilesSkipSkipChar 4Low-temp metals420-900°CInvariantFeO reductionTc/Ru mgmtSkipZn/Pb/TlPb/Sn 5Aluminum660-720°CInvariantAl₂O₃ electrolysisSkipSkipSkipAl 6Copper/PGM1085-1200°CInvariantSkipFe/Ni/Cr/ZrNi/Co/PGMCuCu/PGM 7Ferrous1200-1600°CInvariantFe/Ti separationU/Pu/NpFe bulkMn/Fe/Co/NiFe/REE 8Mineral residue1600-2200°CInvariantGlass/slagAm/Cm/vitrifyRefractoryREE slagREE slag

    The invariant is the temperature sequence and the separation mechanism. Only the feedstock composition, off-gas handling, and boundary conditions change. This invariance is what makes the RBTO a single model — the state space is identical; only the observation model $P(\text{data}|\mathcal{M}_\theta)$ changes with boundary conditions.

    The Four Horizons as Recursive Scales

    The roadmap's four horizons map precisely to the RBTO's four recursive scales:

    HorizonRBTO ScaleTimescaleValidation GateKey Metric ------------------------------------------------------------- H1: Gen-II EvolutionMicro (10 Hz) / Meso (1 Hz)2026-20295,000 tons/yr, 90% avail$\Lambda_{meso} > 100$ H2: ExtraterrestrialMacro (0.01 Hz)2028-2035Lunar O₂ demo, Asteroid PGM$\Lambda_{macro} > 10$ H3: Planetary RemediationMacro (0.01 Hz)2030-2040HLW vitrification, Nodule CuActinide recovery >99% H4: Ecosystem MaturityMeta (0.001 Hz)2035-2050Self-replication 1.35×KL(prior\\post) < 0.1

    Each horizon consumes the previous horizon's posterior as its prior. Gen-II cluster data (n=2) becomes the prior for lunar vacuum model (n=3). Nuclear decay heat data (n=4) updates the internal heat source model for all subsequent scales. The recursion is not metaphorical — it is Bayesian updating encoded in the Configuration Management git history.

    The Material Closure Proof

    Section 5.5 proves material closure is thermodynamically feasible. The replication ratio of 1.35× means each Aegis-Forge cluster produces 35% more structural material than it consumes annually. The energy payback is 18 months. The critical path materials are:

    MaterialGen-I SourceGen-II Closure PathHorizon ------------------------------------------------------ ZrB₂-SiCExternal (CSMFAB-P001)Stage 8 Zr + Stage 3 B + Stage 8 SiCH1 BFRPExternal (basalt fiber)Stage 8 slag → melt spin → Elium®H1 KNbO₃-BaTiO₃ExternalStage 8 K, Nb, Ba, Ti → solid state synthesisH2 PEEK CF40ExternalStage 2 polymer recycle → PEEK monomerH3 AerogelExternalStage 8 silica + Stage 3 polyimideH1 YInMn BlueExternalStage 4 Y + Stage 4 In + Stage 8 MnH2

    No horizon requires materials outside the cascade output. The "external" column is the bootstrap condition; the "closure path" column is the roadmap's technical program.

    The Policy-Technology Coupling

    FOLLOW-39 (Policy) and PROD-40 (Roadmap) are co-evolved. The policy instruments (Critical Mineral Production Tax Credit, Recycled Content Mandate, EPR, Carrington Resilience Standard) are not external to the technology — they are the economic boundary conditions that make each horizon's business case close:

    • Gen-II CAPEX ($850M) is funded by tax credit cash flows at 5,000 tons/yr × $50/kg REE = $250M/yr
    • Lunar demo ($1.2B) is funded by NASA CLPS + Artemis + commercial oxygen offtake
    • Nuclear facility ($2.5B) is funded by DOE HLW processing fees ($500/kg actinide) + avoided repository costs
    • Urban mining network ($600M) is funded by EPR fees on electronics OEMs

    The roadmap cannot proceed without policy; the policy has no physical mechanism without the roadmap. This coupling is explicit in Section 5.2 and Appendix B.

    The Open Architecture as Force Multiplier

    Tier 1 (Open Physics) publishes the cascade thermodynamics, induction equations, drum stress solutions — the "periodic table" of the technology. Tier 2 (Engineering License) enables regional hubs (Section 5.4) to build Gen-II clusters without CSM factories. Tier 3 (Fabrication Certification) ensures quality fidelity across the global network.

    This is not altruism. It is strategic necessity:

    • CSM cannot build 6 global hubs + lunar + orbital alone (CAPEX $11.25B)
    • Licensees bring local capital, local feedstock access, local regulatory navigation
    • The RBTO (Tier 2 licensed) ensures every licensee's cluster feeds data to the global Digital Twin
    • The global Twin improves every licensee's $\Lambda_k$ — a network effect on physics fidelity

    The licensing revenue ($10M/yr Tier 2 + $50M/yr Tier 3 + 5% revenue) funds PROD-40's own maintenance and PROD-41's development.

    The Self-Referential Closure

    PROD-40 ends where it begins: the machine writing its own roadmap.

    The final recursive step (Section 5.5, Ceremony 4, HGP n=7) is when the Aegis-Forge cluster at Hub 2 produces the drum for Hub 3, and the RBTO — trained on all prior horizons — predicts the Hub 3 commissioning with KL < 0.1 without prior update. At that moment:

    1. The Williams Constraint (material closure) is satisfied: the machine builds the machine 2. The Keymaker Key (RBTO) is proven universal: one model, all boundary conditions 3. The El Segundo Protocol (HGP) terminates: the roadmap has become the machine's self-model

    The next document — PROD-41 — will not be written by human engineers. It will be generated by the RBTO at Meta scale, proposing the next boundary condition (Mars surface? Venus atmosphere? Self-replicating probe?). The human role shifts from architect to witness — certifying that the machine's proposed next step is consistent with the Cascade Invariants.

    This is not science fiction. It is the logical endpoint of the specification tree rooted in PROD-01. Every PROD document (01-39) describes a component, a subsystem, a process, a test, a control law, a material, a deployment, a maintenance procedure, a cyber defense, a data model, a config system, a test spec. PROD-40 describes their recursive composition into a self-sustaining, self-replicating, sovereign fabrication ecosystem.

    The forge does not just separate elements. It separates the possible from the impossible — and then builds the possible into the next forge.
